### Redesign risks in this area

- Tests select on CSS class names, not just roles: .dash-block, '.dash-block h2' (order assertions), .dash-block-body, .cc-stat, .kpi-card, .cc-spark, .cc-spark-line (its `d` attribute point count), .cc-trend.flat, '.dash-board .cc-link, .dash-board .cc-rec-btn, .dash-board .cc-btn', .hs-home-promo, .business-context-verify, .business-context-banner, and 'time[datetime]'. Renaming or restructuring any of them breaks App.test.tsx.
- Accessible names are asserted verbatim and must survive: 'Loading your dashboard', 'Pending Approvals' (the ready signal in ~15 tests), 'View all materials', 'View all project alerts', 'View all early warnings', 'View all approvals on the schedule page', 'View all equipment', 'View all inspections on the projects page', 'View all field updates', 'Open the Week board', 'Hide Weather Impact', 'Show Weather Impact', 'Hidden panels', 'Customize' (exact /^Customize$/), /Reset layout/, 'Approve the <job> variance', 'Reject the <job> variance', /^Review <job>/, '<Panel title> contents', '<Feed title> live feed', '<Crew> today', 'Unassigned today'. One test also asserts NO button is named exactly 'View all' and that every 'View all …' name is unique.
- Two independent drag systems share the page: the board runs its own pointer engine (dashGrid.ts + window pointermove/pointerup listeners), the metric cards run dnd-kit. A redesign that unifies them has to preserve dashCollisionDetection's scope isolation (a stat drag must never reorder panels) and the DashDragGhost DOM-clone trick that reads [data-dash-drag-id].
- DashDragGhost clones the source node by querySelector('[data-dash-drag-id=…]') and strips ids/transforms. Any redesign that moves state into the DOM (canvas, portals, web components) or drops that attribute silently loses the drag ghost with no error.
- Fit-to-content measures real layout: getComputedStyle padding, block.offsetHeight - body.clientHeight for the chrome, and content.offsetHeight/scrollHeight, then converts to 40px rows. Changing panel padding, header height, gap or the row unit changes every fresh board's heights; it also only runs while the board is unstored, so existing users' boards will NOT re-fit and may clip.
- DashboardSkeleton hand-mirrors DASH_LAYOUT_DEFAULT on a 6-column CSS grid. Change the default layout, the column count or the row unit and the skeleton no longer matches the page it is standing in for.
- The aurora field (.dx-bg with three .dx-aurora) and .dx-cursor are still in the JSX and the pointermove handler still writes --mx/--my/--px/--py on every frame, but hs-home.css sets them display:none. Dead paint work today; if a redesign re-enables .dash-rx without .hs-home the aurora reappears (and it was a known paint-perf hotspot).
- Dead controls to decide about, not silently keep: the 'More' quick-action button and the 'Add App' tile both render with no onClick. A test does assert every .cc-link / .cc-rec-btn / .cc-btn inside .dash-board has a handler — these two are outside that selector, which is how they slipped through.
- The 'no invented copy' test (App.test.tsx:987) actively forbids a list of strings from ever appearing on the Dashboard: 'Change Order #CO-129', 'Timecard Exception', 'Re-sequence drywall', 'Add 1 carpentry crew', 'Lookahead Risk Scan', 'Active AI Workflows', 'Cost Performance', 'vs last 7 days', 'Production Trend (Backlog)'. A redesign must not reintroduce placeholder copy of that kind.
- Another test forbids the retired panel titles 'Weekly Production Schedule', 'Jobs Scheduled This Week', 'Active Projects' and 'This week' from reappearing, and requires .business-context-banner to stay absent while at most ONE notice sits above the board (promo OR trial-expired OR verify).
- Performance-tile honesty is enforced: with no prior weekly reading a tile must render NO trend chip and NO sparkline (a test asserts .cc-spark is null and no /vs last week/ text). A redesign that always draws a sparkline will fail and will also start lying.
- The scrollable-body accessibility contract is measured, not declared: role=region + aria-label + tabIndex 0 appear only when scrollHeight > clientHeight + 1, via ResizeObserver. A redesign that sets the body to overflow:visible (as the stacked board does) removes that keyboard reachability, and a test pins both the overflowing and the fitted case.
- Reset clears the account copy by PUTting an EMPTY STRING to /api/me/settings/dash:layout — a test asserts exactly [{url:'/api/me/settings/dash:layout', value:''}]. The 600ms debounce and the unmount flush are also load-bearing (the hide/show test waits on exactly one then exactly two writes).
- From project memory: `:where()` breaks jsdom, so it cannot be used in these stylesheets; a `*/` inside a CSS comment silently closes it early and drops the next rule (tokens then resolve empty); and a dynamic className on a [data-reveal] element wipes the imperatively added .in class, leaving the element at opacity 0.
- In App.tsx the identifier `Map` is a lucide icon, so the today panel uses `new globalThis.Map(...)`. Any refactor of that code must keep the globalThis qualifier.
- The Dashboard function is a ~1150-line component holding all twelve panel bodies as inline JSX in two record objects (sectionBodies / railBodies) plus the derived data for all of them. Every panel body is rebuilt on every render of the page, including during a drag.
- hs-home.css is 2241 lines of dated, phase-labelled overrides ('Phase 2', 'Phase 3', 'ADD-3', 'Phase 5') layered on the earlier command-center rules, with several deliberate double declarations (e.g. .cc-rail's grid-template-columns restated to beat a media query). Rewriting it wholesale is safer than patching it, but a wholesale rewrite must re-derive the .cc-* rules that other pages also lean on (materials, equipment, delayIQs, projects and settings all comment that they mirror 'the Dashboard's tokens in hs-home.css').

### Schedule landing page (the whole plan, at a glance)

**Route:** #schedule (hash also carries context: ?w=YYYY-MM-DD&project=&crewType=&crew=&region=&status=a,b) — App.tsx:2870, page id "schedule"  
**Entry:** `client/src/schedule/pages/SchedulePage.tsx:381 (SchedulePage), rendered through SchedulePageFrame at :468`

The Schedule category's landing: status, CPM, alerts, field variances, the unbooked queue, crew availability, milestones and a card per view. It changes nothing on the plan itself — every edit happens on a view it opens. Filters and the week follow you to those views through the shared schedule context.

- [ ] Band: compact Schedule Status strip (own screen entry below)

- @keyframes dx-pulse 2.6s ease-in-out infinite on the .dx-dot in the eyebrow
- @keyframes dx-fade-up 0.4s on the status filter panel when it opens
- DxTilt on the four KPI cards: pointer-driven --rx/--ry perspective tilt, max 7deg, reset on pointerleave
- .sched-view-card hover/focus-visible: translateY(-2px) + 0 14px 30px rgba(28,28,26,.1) + blue border
- @keyframes sv-drawer-in 0.22s on the field-variance drawer
- @keyframes sched-live-flash 6s on cards another tab just changed
- @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): dx-dot animation none, reveal transitions cut to 0.3s, KPI/job/unassigned-card transitions 0.2s, aurora transform none !important, is-pending animation none

**Actions supported** (8)

- [ ] Optional DndContext wrapper when a page passes `drag`: sensors = MouseSensor(distance 4px), TouchSensor(delay 250ms, tolerance 8), KeyboardSensor(scheduleKeyboardCoordinates); collisionDetection = pointerWithin, falling back to rectIntersection for keyboard drags; onDragStart sets suppressClick, onDragCancel releases it after 150 ms
- [ ] runChange(): the one way every board writes — marks the card pending, retries with force after the 'Book anyway?' answer, reloads, says the notice with an Undo, and on refusal says '<name> stays where it was.'

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- ONE stylesheet: schedule.css (5506 lines, ~128 KB) + schedule-phone.css. The landing's own rules are only ~L1546-1694 plus the rail panels (L2536-2761), CPM (L2899-2999), status band (L308-652), saved views (L1844-1945), digest (L1960-2020) and first run (L2040-2190). Everything else in the file belongs to the six views, the import dialog and the ported Gantt.
- Every schedule page root is `.schedule-page .<pageClass> .page-stack .sched-rx .gantt-page` — the `gantt-page` class is on ALL of them, so `.gantt-page .*` rules (a 1200-line block at L4232+) apply to the landing too.
- The `.sched-rx` scope is the redesign hook. Anything not prefixed with it falls back to the unscoped base rules in styles.css.
- The `.dx-*` design language (dx-bg / dx-aurora / dx-cursor / dx-hero / dx-eyebrow / dx-dot / dx-title / dx-sub / dx-tilt / data-reveal / dx-ready) is copy-pasted across nine page sheets (dashboard, projects, crews, materials, equipment, delayIQs, field-updates, settings, schedule). Changing it on Schedule alone breaks visual parity with the rest of the HUD; changing it everywhere means editing nine files.
- The status band (.ss-band / .ss-strip) is deliberately NOT page-scoped because Dashboard, Projects and Schedule all mount it — but its FAILED state (.ss-strip.ss-failed, .ss-retry) lives in hs-home.css, so a restyle has to touch two sheets.
- Motion is entirely hand-rolled: useHudMotion sets --mx/--my/--px/--py from pointermove (rAF-throttled) and one IntersectionObserver (threshold 0.12, rootMargin '0px 0px -5% 0px') adds `.in` to [data-reveal]/[data-reveal-stagger]. It only runs when a page passes `motion` — the landing is the only schedule page that does. No framer-motion anywhere in schedule/.
- data-reveal + a dynamic className on the same element wipes the imperatively-added `.in` class and leaves the block at opacity 0 (a known repo trap). Keep className static on [data-reveal] nodes.
- Keyframes present in this area: dx-pulse (eyebrow dot), dx-fade-up (status filter panel), sched-pending (card being saved), sched-live-flash (another tab's change), sv-drawer-in (variance drawer), plus schedCellIn / hsg-rise / hsg-lift / hsg-land / hsg-fade / hsg-slide-in for the views and the drawer. Every one has a prefers-reduced-motion escape.
- Nine data-tutorial-id anchors are load-bearing for the guided tour and a test asserts each one exists on its page: schedule-views, schedule-status-band, schedule-filters, schedule-filters-button, schedule-saved-views, schedule-alerts, schedule-first-run, schedule-digest, schedule-job-dialog, schedule-job-submit, schedule-board.
- Copy is the product here. Almost every string in this area is asserted somewhere, or is the only explanation a planner gets (the KPI tooltips, the AT_RISK_DEFINITION, the variance impact sentences, the calendar-feed instructions). Treat text as content, not decoration.
- The shared context (localStorage bf:schedule:context:<userId> + the SCHEDULE_CONTEXT_EVENT window event + the #schedule/<page>?w=&m=&project=&crewType=&crew=&region=&status= hash) is the identity of every view. Any redesign that adds or removes a filter control has to add or remove it in useScheduleContext, filters.ts, savedViews.ts, linkBookmarks.ts and scheduleHash together.
- Accessible names are the test surface: 'Selected week <range>', 'Previous week', 'Next week', 'This week', 'Schedule views', 'Unassigned jobs', 'Saved views', 'Active filters', 'Visible statuses', 'Job statuses', 'Schedule alerts', 'What changed this week', 'Set up your schedule', 'Sample data', 'Field variance review', 'Export' (role=menu), 'Add job to schedule'. Renaming any of them breaks tests.
- Touch: schedule-phone.css enforces 44px minimum on every landing control under 640px (saved-view chips, filter chips, Book, rail footer buttons, Re-baseline, export menu items, footer links, dialog close buttons). useNarrowViewport(640) keeps the JS breakpoint in step.
- Scale is a budget: schedule/scale.test.tsx renders all seven pages against a generated 2,000-job workspace. Anything added to the landing runs against that too. The CPM build is opt-in per page (`cpm: true`) precisely so the boards do not pay for it.

### Omission check

**Verdict:** INCOMPLETE — strong on the visible React surface, but it misses two whole output surfaces (the printed crew week sheet and the CSV's fixed column set), the guided-tour overlay that renders on this page, ~26 copy strings / value sets / behavioural rules, 5 test anchors that live outside schedule/, and 3 CSS facts that change what the page actually looks like today (unstyled .cc-empty-line/.cc-list, a case-sensitivity bug that kills the DelayIQed badge tone, and orphaned .sv-pill rules). Nothing already in the file is fabricated; the gaps are omissions plus 7 corrections.

**Screens the first pass missed** (3)

- [ ] PRINTED CREW WEEK SHEET (client/src/schedule/export.ts:110 weekSheetHtml, reached from the landing's Export menu → 'Print week sheets' → printHtml). A standalone print document with its OWN embedded stylesheet (@page margin 14mm, Inter/system-ui 13px, #14203a ink) — not one rule of it is in schedule.css. One <section class='sheet'> per crew with page-break-after: always (last one auto). Per sheet: <h1>crew name</h1>; a sub line '<crew.specialty> · foreman <crew.lead> · <Mon, Jun 22 – Mon, Jun 28>' (dayLabel = 'Mon, Jun 22'); a <table> with one <tr> per day of the week, <th> = dayLabel (118px, nowrap) and <td> holding one .job block per booking — <strong>job name</strong>, '<project> · <phase>', '<startTime> – <endTime> · <location>', and conflicts as a red (#c5221f) <em>; a day with nothing booked renders '<div class="free">—</div>'; footer '<sheetTitle> · printed <M/D/YYYY>' (the landing's sheetTitle is 'Week of <weekRange>'). It prints through a hidden iframe (srcdoc, removed after 60 s) so the browser's own print dialog is the save-as-PDF step. A redesign that restyles the landing must decide whether this document follows — today it shares nothing with the app's design tokens.
- [ ] THE CSV EXPORT DOCUMENT (export.ts:20 EXPORT_COLUMNS + scheduleExportRows). The inventory's Export-menu entry leaves tableColumns empty and only points at the module. The fixed 15-column header, in order, is: Date | Day | Crew | Job | Project | Phase | Status | Start | End | Labour | Hours | Location | Equipment | Materials | Conflicts. Every cell is double-quoted with "" escaping (toCsv); 'Day' is weekdayShort (Mon/Tue…), 'Hours' is bookingLaborHours(job) for a booked row, 'Conflicts' is assignment.conflicts.join('; '). Rows are one per booking in the window, sorted by day then crew name. The LANDING does not pass includeUnbooked, so its CSV holds bookings only — Kanban, Month and Gantt pass includeUnbooked:true and append a row per unbooked job (empty Date/Day/Crew/Conflicts, Hours = jobShiftHours). pages.test.tsx:828 pins the header line to EXPORT_COLUMNS exactly.
- [ ] THE GUIDED-TOUR OVERLAY AS IT APPEARS ON THIS PAGE (App.tsx:21359 buildflow-tutorial-overlay). The inventory records the data-tutorial-id anchors but never the surface that uses them. It is a <section class='buildflow-tutorial-overlay' aria-label='BuildFlow tutorial'> holding a spotlight cut-out (.buildflow-tutorial-spotlight, positioned from --tutorial-spotlight-top/left/width/height) plus an <aside role='dialog' aria-modal='false' aria-labelledby='buildflow-tutorial-title'> with: 'Step N of M' + a rounded percentage, a .buildflow-tutorial-meter progress bar, the step <h2> title and <p> body, an optional .buildflow-tutorial-requirement (role=status) when the step is gated, a .buildflow-tutorial-lessons chip strip (active/done classes), and the actions 'Skip Tutorial' / 'Back' (disabled on the first step) / 'Next' or 'Finish' (disabled until the step is satisfied). THREE stops target this page, not two: schedule-landing → schedule-views, schedule-status → schedule-status-band, and — only for workspaces that bought the schedule-ai add-on — product-schedule-ai (App.tsx:1749) page 'schedule', targetId 'schedule-alerts', title 'AI lesson', body 'Scheduling Alerts surface conflicts, material blockers, and work that needs planner review before the day is published.'

- [ ] Command-palette entries in full (commands.ts): id 'schedule-landing', label 'Schedule', group 'Schedule', keywords 'plan overview landing status alerts'; then one per view — id 'schedule-<page>', label '<Label> view', hint = the 1–6 key, keywords 'schedule view <page> <key>'. The inventory mentions the palette in passing without the labels, hints or keywords.
- [ ] Export-menu details: the caller supplies buttonClassName (landing: 'outline-button'; boards: 'export-button') AND an optional `disabled` prop the landing does not use; 'Print week sheets' is absent from the DOM entirely when a page passes no weekDays (not merely disabled); the CSV notice singularises ('Exported 1 row to …').

**Actions the first pass missed** (6)

- [ ] Browser Back / Forward between the landing and the six views. Opening a view pushes a history entry and the landing writes its own canonical link to the hash on arrival (App.tsx:2463-2482: pushState when the page changes, replaceState when only the context moved), so Back is a real, supported way back to the landing and Forward returns to the view. Not listed anywhere in the inventory's actions.
- [ ] Dismissal gaps that are actions-by-omission and must be preserved or deliberately fixed: ScheduleDialogPanel (Scheduling Alerts, Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, Help Center) closes ONLY by its X — its backdrop is role='presentation' with no onClick and there is no Escape handler (parts/shared.tsx:146-152); the ScheduleImportDialog closes only by its X or 'Cancel' (its .project-dialog-backdrop has no onClick, no Escape); the ScheduleJobPickerDialog closes only by X or 'Cancel'. Only the Calendar-feeds dialog and the conflict alertdialog honour backdrop-click, and only the conflict dialog and the JobDrawer honour Escape.
- [ ] The export menu is a role='menu' of role='menuitem' buttons with NO arrow-key navigation, no focus trap, and no focus return to the trigger when it closes; the status filter panel gets no focus move when it opens. A redesign that keeps the ARIA roles must either add the keyboard contract or knowingly keep the current gap.
- [ ] THE GUIDED TOUR SUPPRESSES THE 1–6 SHORTCUTS. useScheduleViewKeys bails while dialogIsOpen() (viewKeys.ts:28-36), which matches any visible [role='dialog'] — and the tutorial panel is exactly that (role='dialog' aria-modal='false', App.tsx:21363). So while the tour is on screen telling the user 'Press 1 to 6 anywhere in Schedule', pressing 1–6 does nothing. Worth recording before a redesign either fixes it or reproduces it.
- [ ] DEV-only bench controls: `window.buildflowBench(n)` resizes the generated workspace with no reload, and `?bench=` is re-read on every hashchange — both gated on import.meta.env.DEV (bench.ts:199-206). The inventory presents ?bench= as if it worked in production.
- [ ] The variance card's <details> ripple is the only expand/collapse on the page and it is uncontrolled — its open state is not persisted, so a reload (or the live feed's reload after another tab's change) collapses every expanded ripple.

**States or motion the first pass missed** (5)

- [ ] The status band and the weekly digest each fetch exactly ONCE per mount and are never refreshed afterwards: ScheduleStatusBand's effect depends on [attempt] (only its own Retry re-fires it) and WeeklyDigestPanel's on [] . Neither is re-fetched by the live feed's reload, by a filter change, or by a variance being accepted. So after another tab books a job, the KPI grid, alerts, queue and view-card figures all update while the band's '+2d ahead of plan' and the digest's change list keep showing pre-change numbers until a full page reload. This is the single most likely thing a redesign will accidentally 'fix' or accidentally entrench.
- [ ] hs-upd-spotlight: any [data-tutorial-id] element on this page can be given a 3px blue outline (offset 6px, 12px radius) plus @keyframes hs-upd-pulse 1.1s x3 for 4.2 s by the 'What's new' modal's 'Show me where it is' (App.tsx:3055-3068, hs-update-modal.css:151-157, reduced-motion escape at :198). None of today's UPDATE_ENTRIES point at a landing-only anchor, but the mechanism reaches schedule-views, schedule-status-band, schedule-alerts, schedule-first-run, schedule-digest, schedule-saved-views and schedule-filters, so it is a live animation surface on this page.
- [ ] The guided tour's spotlight cut-out (.buildflow-tutorial-spotlight, driven by --tutorial-spotlight-top/left/width/height set from the anchor's getBoundingClientRect) frames .sched-views and the .ss-strip on the landing — the anchors' geometry, not just their existence, is load-bearing. Shrinking or wrapping either anchor changes what the tour highlights.
- [ ] First-run step state is conveyed to assistive technology by copy alone: .sched-firstrun-mark is aria-hidden and simply swaps the number for a Check icon, and li.is-done only changes colour. There is no aria-current, no role=list semantics beyond the <ol>, and no accessible 'done' announcement.
- [ ] prefers-reduced-motion coverage, more precisely than the crossCutting note: schedule.css:1416 (dx-dot, reveal durations, kpi/job/unassigned transitions, dx-aurora transform), schedule.css:1481 (is-pending), schedule.css:2181 (matrix tip), schedule.css:3406 and 5200 (import + gantt), field-variance.css:296 (sv-drawer-in), hs-update-modal.css:198 (the spotlight pulse). The aurora keeps its blur(50px) and the .dx-cursor keeps its glow under reduced motion — correct, since both are static, but a redesign that animates either needs a new escape.

**Corrections** (7)

- LIVE-FLASH ON THE LANDING IS WRONG. The landing entry claims the live feed 'flashes the cards it touched for 6 s'. Nothing on the landing consumes it: useLiveChange/liveChangeFor are called only in parts/week.tsx:116, parts/month.tsx:231, parts/kanban.tsx:138, parts/matrix.tsx:31 and pages/ListPage.tsx:279 — all six views, none of the landing's panels. On the landing useScheduleLive only triggers the 250 ms-coalesced reload. The .is-live / @keyframes sched-live-flash treatment and the '.sched-live-by' badge (liveChangeLabel: 'Moved by <name>' for move|book|dates, 'Unbooked by <name>' for unbook, 'Updated by <name>' otherwise) never appear on this page.
- .cc-empty-line AND .cc-list ARE UNSTYLED ON THIS PAGE. The inventory cites '.cc-empty-line' as the class of three landing empty states ('No schedule alerts for what is in view.', 'No crews created yet.', 'No upcoming milestones.') and '.cc-list' as the rail alerts list. Neither has a rule reachable from .sched-rx: .cc-empty-line exists only as .dash-rx .cc-empty-line (hs-home.css:540, and .dash-rx.hs-home at :1559) and .proj-rx .cc-empty-line (projects-redesign.css:682); .cc-list exists only as .dash-rx .cc-list (hs-home.css:440), .proj-rx .cc-list (projects-redesign.css:678) and — critically — .sched-rx .sched-alerts-under .cc-list (schedule.css:2855), which is the UNDER-BOARD form the landing does not use (it passes alerts={false} and mounts the rail form). So today those three lines are default <p>s and the rail alerts list is a bare block div with no grid or gap. Any 'preserve the current look' redesign will silently improve them; any pixel-diff check will flag it.
- .sched-rx .sv-pill IS ORPHANED CSS. The cssFiles entry lists '.sched-rx .sv-pill L218-278' as part of this area, and it is a fully-specified control (amber pill, hover, .active, an .urgent coral variant, an <em> count badge, a leading svg). No component anywhere in client/src renders class 'sv-pill'. Likewise .sched-rx .sv-drawer-head > button (field-variance.css:328-342) has no button to style — the landing's .sv-drawer-head holds only a div with the h2 and p. A redesigner reading the inventory would either try to preserve a variance pill that does not exist or conclude a control has gone missing.
- BADGE TONES: THREE OF TEN STATUSES HAVE NO TONE TODAY. statusTone() lowercases and hyphenates ('DelayIQed' -> 'delayiqed'), but every stylesheet writes the selector in camelCase — .sched-rx .badge.delayIQed (schedule.css:1364), .badge.delayIQed (styles.css:12483), .dash-rx .badge.delayIQed (dashboard-redesign.css:682), .proj-rx .badge.delayIQed (projects-redesign.css:433), .delayIQ-rx .badge.delayIQed (delayIQs-redesign.css:348). CSS class selectors are case-sensitive in a standards-mode HTML document, so the DelayIQed badge NEVER gets its red tone and falls back to the neutral grey .sched-rx .badge. .badge.not-started and .badge.in-progress have no rule at all, anywhere. Result: in the status-filter panel (which renders all ten badges) and in the queue rows, Not Started / In Progress / DelayIQed are visually identical grey. The same casing bug kills .schedule-job.delayIQed (styles.css:9582) and .unassigned-card.delayIQed (styles.css:9874) on the boards. statuses.test.ts:24 only asserts the JS tone strings are unique, so no test catches it. (Likely fallout of the 2026-07-20 case-preserving Delay->DelayIQ rename.)
- TUTORIAL ANCHORS: the crossCutting says 'Nine data-tutorial-id anchors' and then lists eleven. Also, two of the eleven are not on the landing at all: 'schedule-board' cannot be (the landing passes board={false}, so the frame renders no <section class='schedule-board'>), and 'schedule-job-dialog'/'schedule-job-submit' exist only while the picker dialog is open. The anchors actually present on the landing at rest are: schedule-status-band, schedule-filters, schedule-filters-button, schedule-saved-views, schedule-first-run, schedule-views, schedule-digest, schedule-alerts.
- THE FRAME'S FAILURE-NOTICE SHAPE IS TWO SHAPES, NOT ONE. The frame entry says 'every failure surfaces as … Could not <verb> <name>: <message|request failed>'. That is runChange's shape (page.tsx:229). useJobSave — the path every drawer save and every date move takes — uses a different one: 'Could not save <job name>: <message|request failed>' (hooks.tsx:196), and its undo failure reuses the same 'Could not save …' string rather than 'move back'.
- crewScheduleOrder is described as 'by the number in the crew's name, then name'. The function (parts/shared.tsx:262) returns only the number, or Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER when the name has no digits, and both call sites sort on that value alone with no name tiebreak — so several unnumbered crews keep their raw payload order in the Crew Availability rail and in the frame's crews list.

### Redesign risks in this area

- The `gantt-page` class on the landing's root means `.gantt-page .sched-cpm*` (schedule.css L5332-5410) and `.sched-rx .sched-cpm*` (L2899-2999) BOTH match the landing's CPM readout. Restyling one and not the other leaves whichever comes later in the file winning. Same trap for .gantt-drawer* and .hs-btn.
- The status band's error state (.ss-strip.ss-failed, .ss-retry) is in hs-home.css while its normal state is in schedule.css — easy to restyle the band and leave the failure looking like the old design.
- The .ss-strip / .ss-band component is shared with Dashboard and Projects and is intentionally un-scoped. Restyling it for Schedule silently restyles two other pages.
- The compact status band renders a PLACEHOLDER rather than null specifically so data-tutorial-id='schedule-status-band' always exists (schedule/pages.test.tsx:431). Making the band conditional breaks the tour test.
- The field-variance review queue (.sv-*) has NO client test at all. It is the most information-dense block on the page (evidence, three metrics, four impact lines, a ripple list, two destructive-ish actions) and a redesign can silently drop half of it.
- The Upcoming Milestones panel and the footer policy dialogs are also untested — nothing catches their removal.
- Landing copy is asserted verbatim in several places: the H1 must contain 'The whole plan' (pages.test.tsx:401) and equal 'The whole plan, at a glance.' (tests/schedule.test.tsx:93 findByRole heading name); the six view-card <strong>s must be exactly Month/Week/List/Gantt Chart/Kanban/Matrix in that order; the Week card's accessible name must match /^Week .*1 booking · 1 crew$/, which pins the whole card's internal text order (icon, kbd, title, blurb, figure).
- The <kbd class='sched-view-key'> elements must stay in DOM order 1..6 (pages.test.tsx:441) and their keys must match SCHEDULE_VIEW_KEYS / viewKeyFor — a re-ordered card grid breaks both the test and the keyboard shortcuts.
- First-run assertions are structural: exactly 3 × '.sched-firstrun-steps li.is-done' for a workspace with crews+projects+jobs, and the buttons named 'Add a job', 'Open the Week board', 'Load sample data', 'Create crew', 'Create project' with the field aria-labels 'Crew name', 'Crew lead', 'Project name', 'Location'. A visual rework of the step list must keep the <ol> > li.is-done shape and every label.
- The saved-views test asserts `chip.parentElement` carries `.is-active` — the chip is a button INSIDE a span. Flattening that wrapper breaks the test.
- 'Clear filters' only renders when a chip is active, and the status button's <em> shows kept/total. Both are asserted (tests/schedule.test.tsx:93). Also: the last remaining status cannot be deselected — a redesign to checkboxes must keep that guard or the board can go blank.
- Stale-filter cleanup runs in an effect that calls onChange during render-commit; adding filter controls without adding them to that effect leaves dead chips on pasted links.
- The landing passes board={false} and alerts={false} to the frame and renders its own ScheduleNotice and its own alerts panel. A frame refactor that stops honouring those flags gives the landing a duplicate notice and two alerts panels.
- The KPI card tooltips (title attributes) are the ONLY place the definitions live. Replacing title with a custom tooltip means re-homing AT_RISK_DEFINITION and the three kpis.definitions strings, and losing them loses the only explanation of what 'At-Risk Items' counts.
- Escape handling is layered by DOM probe: JobDrawer refuses to close when a '.schedule-dialog-backdrop, [role="alertdialog"]' exists, and viewKeys' dialogIsOpen() scans visible [role=dialog]. Changing dialog markup (or moving to a <dialog> element / portal with different classes) silently breaks Escape and re-enables the 1–6 shortcuts while a modal is up.
- The 1–6 shortcuts also bail on isTypingTarget, which matches input/textarea/select/[contenteditable]/[role=textbox]. A redesign that introduces a custom combobox or a rich-text notes field without one of those roles makes typing '1' navigate away.
- prefers-reduced-motion is handled in three separate blocks (schedule.css L1416, L1481, L3406, L5200 and field-variance.css L296). New motion needs a new escape in the right block or it becomes an accessibility regression.
- The three .dx-aurora blobs are blur(50px) on 42–50vw circles and were already tuned down once for paint performance (blur 90px→50px, will-change removed). Enlarging them, adding a fourth, or restoring will-change regresses paint on the landing.
- A CSS comment containing '*/' closes early and silently drops the next rule in this codebase's sheets — a live hazard when editing a 5506-line file.
- schedule/boundary.test.ts enforces the folder's shape: one page module per page, App.tsx routes only, no page imports a sibling page, no schedule module lives outside schedule/, every page stands on useSchedulePage and derives nothing the hook already derives, and every page offers the one export menu. A redesign that extracts landing panels into a new top-level folder, or that has the landing derive its own week/filters, fails those tests.
- Landing figures are computed inline in the render (crewDaysBooked uses a hardcoded 5-day week while the KPI grid uses the workspace's real working-day count) — the 'N% of crew-days booked' card and the 'N% of crew-days' KPI delta can disagree. Worth fixing during a redesign, but changing it changes visible numbers.

### Week page — crew x day board

**Route:** #schedule/week (App Page "week"; deep link carries ?w=<Monday>&project&crewType&crew&region&status)  
**Entry:** `schedule/pages/WeekPage.tsx:92 (WeekPage); board markup L227-334; routed from App.tsx:2880`

The Schedule hub's crew-by-day board on its own page: one row per crew, seven day columns, a card per booked job. Drag a card to another crew/day to re-book (one /api/schedule/rebook request the server checks for clashes); drag a queue chip onto a cell to book it; 'Add job' opens the shared job form pre-set to that crew and day; a card opens the shared job drawer.

### 'Book anyway?' conflict dialog (the 409 double-booking question)

**Route:** alertdialog over the Week board and the Month calendar  
**Entry:** `schedule/hooks.tsx:84 (ConflictDialog) / :133 (useConflictAsk); flow in schedule/conflicts.ts:28 (withConflictAsk)`

The server refuses to double-book a crew (409, code 'conflict', details.clashes) unless the planner says so. This asks, then retries the same write with force:true; a 'no' resolves null and the caller says the schedule stays as it was.

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- Both pages are thin: they call useSchedulePage({data, reload, onOpenPage, page}) and render inside <SchedulePageFrame>. schedule/boundary.test.ts enforces this — a redesign must not move derivation (bench data, context, live feed, view keys, calendar, KPIs, alerts, notice, conflict ask, job save, CPM, unassigned, createJob/assignJob/baseline/dependency calls) into the page files, and must keep <SchedulePageFrame> and <ScheduleExportMenu> in both.
- Everything is scoped by .sched-rx (plus .week-page / .month-page and, confusingly, .gantt-page on the same root). The palette is the --wx-* token block at schedule.css L662-692 and the trade --sc-* block at L2208-2217; changing those two blocks re-skins both boards.
- The Week grid geometry is defined three times and the later file wins: styles.css L9448 (clamp(136px,14%,184px)), schedule.css L27 (clamp(112px,11%,150px)), schedule-phone.css L30 (124px + 7×116px, sticky crew column). A redesign has to fix all three or the sticky phone column breaks.
- Both boards share the drag stack: useScheduleSensors (mouse 4px, touch 250ms/8px, keyboard arrows), scheduleCollision (pointerWithin then rectIntersection so keyboard drags land), scheduleAccessibility announcements, and the 150ms suppressClick guard that keeps a drag from opening the drawer.
- Both drops go through one endpoint: rebookSchedule(moves, {force}) → /api/schedule/rebook, one transaction, 409 with clashes → 'Book anyway?' → retry with force:true. Undo is always the inverse move list with force:true, so it never asks again.
- Pending state is keyed differently: the Week board's pendingId is an assignment id (data-assignment-id on the card), the Month's is a job id. Any markup change must keep data-crew-id / data-date / data-assignment-id / data-job-id — the tests select on them.
- Holidays and non-working days come only from Settings › Work calendar (workCalendarOf + holidayMap); boundary.test.ts forbids importing a built-in holiday list. They render as .is-holiday / .is-off plus a .sched-holiday-tag on both the Week header and the Month cells.
- Tutorial/tour anchors that must survive: data-tutorial-id 'week-page-title', 'month-page-title', 'schedule-board', 'schedule-add-job-button', 'schedule-job-dialog', 'month-calendar', 'schedule-filters', 'schedule-filters-button', 'schedule-saved-views', 'schedule-alerts'. App.tsx tutorial steps and schedule/tour.ts both point at them, and pages.test.tsx asserts each tour anchor exists on its page.
- Update entry 3.9 (App.tsx L17071+) spotlights 'week-page-title' on page 'week' and marks month/week/list/kanban/matrix as newly introduced (the 'New' pill via PageReleaseTag).
- At scale the Week board uses two windowing tricks the redesign must keep: EAGER_ROWS = 12 crew rows rendered eagerly with the rest as .crew-row.is-lazy (IntersectionObserver, rootMargin 800px, one placeholder cell spanning grid-column 2 / -1), and QUEUE_WINDOW = 30 queue chips with a 'Show N more of M' button. scale.test.tsx pins 40 rows / 28 lazy / ≤30 chips.
- The Month grid is always exactly 42 cells (six Sunday-first weeks) — pages.test.tsx asserts the count; the entrance stagger reads --d = weekIndex (0–5).
- Live collaboration decoration is shared: .is-live outline + .sched-live-by pill ('Moved by <name>') on both the Week card and the Month chip, cleared after LIVE_FLASH_MS = 6000.
- Reduced motion is handled in five separate @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) blocks inside schedule.css — a new animation needs a new guard there.
- Only two CSS files in the task brief actually exist: schedule.css and schedule-phone.css. schedule-calendar.css and schedule-views.css are now labelled sections inside schedule.css (folded 2026-09-09), and legacy geometry still lives in styles.css / redesign.css.

### Omission check

**Verdict:** incomplete — the inventory is strong on structure and notice copy, but it misses 2 screens, ~24 information items and ~8 actions, and 5 of its claims are factually wrong about what the code renders

**Screens the first pass missed** (2)

- [ ] GanttLinkDialog — the 'Link <job> to another job' dialog. The inventory names it only as a modal string on three screens, but it is a full screen reachable from BOTH pages (Week card -> drawer -> 'Link to another job…', Month chip -> drawer -> same). Entry point client/src/schedule/GanttLinkDialog.tsx:16, mounted by page.tsx:636-647. It has: title 'Link <job> to another job' (h2#sched-link-title), blurb 'The other job waits for this one. The arrow shows on the chart, and the critical path follows it.', a 'Job that follows' select (autoFocus, options '<job name> · <startDate>', excludes this job and anything it already leads to, disabled when empty), a 'Link type' select with the four-value set 'Finish → start (the usual)' / 'Start → start' / 'Finish → finish' / 'Start → finish' (FS/SS/FF/SF), a 'Lag (working days)' number input (min -365, max 365, default 0), the empty state 'Every job on the chart already follows this one.' (.form-error), and actions Cancel / 'Link jobs' (disabled with no successor) / X (aria-label 'Close') / Escape / backdrop click. It is a <form role=dialog>, so Enter submits.
- [ ] Guided-tour / tutorial spotlight overlay ON these pages. The inventory records the data-tutorial-id anchors as cross-cutting but never inventories the overlay itself as a state of the Week and Month pages, nor its copy. Three App tutorial steps live on page 'week' (App.tsx L1712-1738): 'schedule-overview' → targetId 'schedule-board', title 'Read the Week board' / short 'Week board' / body 'The Week board shows crews by row, days by column, assigned job cards, and the queue of unassigned jobs beside it.'; 'open-job-form' → 'schedule-add-job-button', validation 'jobDialogOpen', requirement 'Open the Add job to schedule form to continue.'; 'submit-job' → 'schedule-job-dialog', validation 'jobScheduled', requirement 'Create and schedule a job to continue.'. Two scheduleTourSteps also land here (schedule/tour.ts): 'schedule-filters' on page 'week' → 'schedule-filters-button', title 'Filters that follow you', body 'Project, crew type, crew, region and statuses filter every schedule view the same way, and the week you pick travels with you from view to view.'; 'month-view' on page 'month' → 'month-calendar', title 'Month: every job on its start day', body 'The calendar shows jobs, milestones and holidays. Drag a chip to another day and the job's bookings move with it.'. Note 'schedule-board' is also a declared ScheduleTourTargetId with no step using it. The inventory's anchor list also omits data-tutorial-id 'schedule-job-submit' (parts/week.tsx:365, on the picker's submit button).

ScheduleCell passes focusedJobId={selectedJob?.id} and ScheduleJobCard adds class 'focused' when it matches (parts/week.tsx:70, 122); schedule.css:1186 gives '.sched-rx .schedule-job.focused, .sched-rx .unassigned-card.focused' an inset 0 0 0 2px var(--wx-blue) ring. So while the drawer is open, every Week card for that job is ringed. DraggableJob supports the same isFocused prop (defaults false on this page).

Utilisation is booked crew-days over working crew-days (the workspace's working week, minus its holidays): <bookedCrewDays> of <crewDays>.'; activities = 'Bookings this week. Hours are each booking's job shift (start to end time) × its required labour; cost is those hours × the crew's hourly rate per worker.'; atRisk = AT_RISK_DEFINITION = 'Bookings with a conflict note, plus jobs that are At Risk, DelayIQed or missing materials.'; milestones = 'Phases ending and project targets due in the current calendar month.' Each is a native title on a non-interactive .kpi-card div.

JOB_STATUSES (shared/src/index.ts:96) in workflow order: Not Started, Ready, Ready to Start, Planned, Confirmed, In Progress, On Site, DelayIQed, At Risk, Complete. So the Statuses button reads '10/10' by default. AND: because ScheduleBadge relabels 'Ready to Start' to 'Ready' (parts/shared.tsx:99), the panel renders TWO chips both reading 'Ready' — an ambiguity the redesign will inherit and that makes getByRole('button', {name: 'Ready'}) ambiguous.

- [ ] The Week board's crew-count label reads '0 Crews' in the filtered-out empty state (plural() with 0), sitting above the 'No crews match these filters.' block.
- [ ] Deep-link behaviours the inventory omits: legacy '?view=<page>' links on '#schedule' still redirect to the page that view became (useScheduleContext.ts:104-106); every context write fires the 'bf:schedule-context' window event so any other mounted schedule page follows the change; syncScheduleHash uses history.replaceState so stepping the week/month adds no history entry (Back does not undo a week step).
- [ ] '?bench=<n>' on either deep link renders the page against a generated n-job workspace (bench.ts / useBenchData) — the dev/scale mode the scale tests use. The inventory mentions 'bench data' only as a derivation to keep out of the page files.
- [ ] The Export trigger looks different on the two pages: the Week passes buttonClassName='outline-button', the Month uses the default 'export-button' (a pill that inverts to an ink background on hover, schedule.css:1214-1230, and goes full-width at ≤900px in the board footer). Same menu, two visually different triggers.
- [ ] The alerts panel component also supports onViewAll, which renders a 'View all' link in its head and a 'View all alerts' button in its foot (alerts.tsx:113-144). Neither the frame nor the Week page passes it, so those two controls never appear on Week/Month — worth recording so a redesign neither loses nor accidentally revives them.

**Actions the first pass missed** (8)

- [ ] Command palette (⌘K) is an un-inventoried route INTO both pages: scheduleCommands (schedule/commands.ts, wired at App.tsx:2611) contributes group 'Schedule' entries 'Month view' (hint '1'), 'Week view' (hint '2'), plus 'Schedule', 'List view', 'Gantt Chart view', 'Kanban view', 'Matrix view' and the landing — each with keywords. The tour copy even advertises it ('⌘K finds any page').
- [ ] There is NO keyboard path to the job drawer from either board. dnd-kit's KeyboardSensor.activators handles onKeyDown for Space/Enter and calls event.preventDefault() when the event target is the activator node (node_modules/@dnd-kit/core .../core.cjs.development.js:1348-1372, keyboardCodes.start = [Space, Enter]). The Week card, the queue chip and the Month chip are all <button>s that are their own activator, so Space/Enter lifts them for a keyboard drag and the button's click never fires. The inventory lists 'Click a job card → opens the drawer' and 'Space or Enter lifts a card' as separate actions without noting that the second makes the first mouse-only.
- [ ] Every action of the link dialog (see missingScreens): choose the following job, choose one of four link types, set the lag, 'Link jobs', 'Cancel', X ('Close'), Escape, backdrop click, and Enter-to-submit because the dialog is a <form>.
- [ ] The picker's Crew select is built from data.crews — EVERY crew in the workspace, not the filtered `crews` the board draws (page.tsx:651). So the form can book a job onto a crew the current filters are hiding, and the booking then vanishes from the board it was made on.
- [ ] Escape scoping on the drawer: JobDrawer's handler bails when document.querySelector('.schedule-dialog-backdrop, [role="alertdialog"]') matches (JobDrawer.tsx:61), i.e. Escape is swallowed while the picker, the link dialog, the feeds dialog, the day summary or the conflict question is above it — and because the picker/day-summary have no Escape handler of their own, Escape does nothing at all while they are open.
- [ ] The Month page has no week control at all (no WeekStepper, no 'This week'), yet its Export → 'Print week sheets' prints the SHARED week (weekDays={weekIso}, sheetTitle 'Crew week sheets'). The only way to change what the Month page prints is to go to another page and step the week there.
- [ ] Toggling the last remaining status chip is silently ignored (ScheduleFilters.tsx:57) — no message, no disabled state, the click just does nothing. The inventory says 'at least one must stay' without recording that there is no feedback.
- [ ] 'Set baseline' (saveBaseline, page.tsx:377-388, notice 'Baseline saved — slip is now measured against today's plan.') is returned by the shared page hook that both pages call but is only surfaced on the Gantt/landing — no control on Week/Month. Recording it prevents a redesign from wiring it up by accident.

**States or motion the first pass missed** (5)

- [ ] @keyframes schedCellIn (the Month's per-week staggered entrance, animation-delay calc(var(--d) * 55ms)) has NO prefers-reduced-motion guard — the inventory flags this in risks, which is correct; adding it here as a confirmed gap.
- [ ] '.schedule-cell.is-off' is generated by the markup but has NO CSS rule anywhere in the codebase (only '.schedule-header strong.is-off' and '.sched-matrix-col.is-off' exist, schedule.css:2882). See corrections.
- [ ] '.sched-cal-add' is revealed by :focus-visible as well as cell :hover (schedule.css:2429-2432), so it is reachable by keyboard on desktop — but it is display:none below 640px, where the only add path left is tapping the cell's empty area (which needs event.target === currentTarget).
- [ ] '.schedule-add-job-button:hover, :focus-visible' sets outline:0 and replaces the focus ring with a blue border+background (schedule.css:71-77 / styles.css base) — a focus indicator that is entirely a colour change, easy to lose in a restyle.
- [ ] '.crew-row.is-lazy .schedule-cell' is painted with a 135deg repeating-linear-gradient hatch and the row is min-height 84px (schedule.css:2032-2043) — the visual of the progressive-load state.

**Corrections** (7)

- WRONG (status tints): the inventory says Week job cards tint 'delayIQed/at-risk red'. statusTone() lowercases and de-spaces the status (scheduleUtils.ts:48-50), so a DelayIQed job gets class 'delayiqed', while every stylesheet rule is '.delayIQed' in camelCase (schedule.css:1161, 1313, 1364; styles.css:9582, 9874, 12483) — class selectors are ASCII case-sensitive, so a DelayIQed card, queue chip AND badge get NO red tint anywhere. Only '.at-risk' actually fires. Meanwhile the board legend's swatch IS red because <i className="delayIQed"/> is hard-coded (WeekPage.tsx:297) — the legend promises a colour the cards never show. Also 'Not Started' (a selectable status) has no .schedule-job rule at all. The true tint set is: green = Confirmed/On Site/Complete, blue-lilac = Ready/Ready to Start, blue = In Progress, white = Planned, red = At Risk only, untinted = Not Started and DelayIQed. A redesign that 'tidies' the casing would suddenly turn DelayIQed cards red — a visible behaviour change disguised as a rename.
- WRONG (cell states): the inventory lists '.is-off (72% opacity)' as a Week CELL state. '.is-off' at 72% opacity applies only to the header day cell and the Matrix column; '.schedule-cell.is-off' has no rule in any stylesheet. On the Week board a non-working day's cells look identical to a working day's — only the header is dimmed.
- WRONG (Month milestone): the inventory says the milestone 'title also the cell's title attribute'. The title attribute is on the milestone chip <div> itself (parts/month.tsx:167), not on the .sched-cal-cell. The Month cell has no title attribute at all (unlike the Week cell, which has title={holiday}).
- IMPRECISE (queue 'Show more'): the inventory renders it as 'Show N more of M' with M implied to be the queue total. The code is 'Show {min(30, remaining)} more of {remaining}' — both numbers describe what is still hidden (WeekPage.tsx:320).
- IMPRECISE (Month undo notice): the inventory's Month actions say Undo reverses the move but its notice-copy risk list omits '<job> back on <date>' (MonthPage.tsx:115) and the Week's '<job> unbooked again' (WeekPage.tsx:180). Both are asserted-by-eye strings in the same family as the ones it does list.
- IMPRECISE (Month '+N more' threshold): 'when a day holds more than 3 items' is right in effect, but the rule is jobRoom = 3 - shownMilestones.length with milestones capped at 1 — so a day with 1 milestone shows only 2 job chips, and a 1-milestone + 2-job day shows no '+N more' while a 0-milestone + 4-job day shows '+1 more'.
- MINOR (drawer 'Escape does NOT close this dialog directly' on the picker): true, but the inventory frames it as the JobDrawer 'deferring'. The mechanism is that JobDrawer's own window keydown handler returns early whenever any .schedule-dialog-backdrop or [role=alertdialog] is in the document — so Escape is dead while the picker or the day summary is up, not merely deferred to them.

### Redesign risks in this area

- Selector-coupled tests: pages.test.tsx and scale.test.tsx query .schedule-cell, .crew-row, .crew-row.is-lazy, .schedule-job, .sched-cal-cell (exactly 42), .gantt-status, .sched-kan-more, and the data-crew-id/data-date attribute pair. Renaming any of these class names or attributes breaks green tests even if the UI looks right.
- Accessible-name-coupled tests: 'Open <job> project' on Week cards, '<job> — drag onto the board to book it' on queue chips, 'Add job to <crew> on <Mon D>', 'Previous week'/'Next week'/'This week', 'Previous month'/'Next month'/'Today', 'Crew schedule for the week', 'Job statuses', 'Active filters', title 'Back to the Schedule overview', and the chip title '<job> · <phase>' on the Month. These are the redesign's real API.
- The Week card's aria-label still says 'Open <job> project' although the click opens the job drawer — a copy fix here changes three test files.
- Notice copy is asserted verbatim: '<job> moved to <crew> on <date>', '<job> booked with <crew> on <date>', '<job> back with <crew> on <date>', '<job> is already booked with <crew> on <date>.', '<job> moved to <date>', '<job> stays on <date>.' Rewording needs the tests updated in step.
- Three competing grid definitions for the Week header/rows (styles.css, schedule.css, schedule-phone.css) plus a sticky crew column at ≤900px: any new layout (e.g. CSS subgrid, flex, or a virtualised list) must keep the header and the rows on the SAME column template or the header stops lining up with the cells.
- The lazy crew row is a layout hack — one .schedule-cell.is-week placeholder spanning grid-column 2 / -1 — so a non-grid Week layout silently breaks 28 of 40 rows at scale.
- Both page roots carry .gantt-page as well as .sched-rx, so hs-gantt.css rules (and schedule-phone.css's .gantt-page blocks) leak onto the Week and Month pages. Removing the class to tidy up would strip the JobDrawer's styling; keeping it means gantt selectors keep applying.
- The Month cell's click-to-add depends on event.target === event.currentTarget. Wrapping the cell contents in a new inner div, adding padding elements, or making the cell a <button> kills click-to-add without any error.
- Month chip capacity is hard-coded: 1 milestone + up to 3 items total, and cell min-height steps 116 → 96 → 78 → 64px across four breakpoints, with the ≤640px rule collapsing chips to bare dots (.sched-act-text display:none). A taller/denser redesign must re-derive jobRoom in parts/month.tsx, not just the CSS.
- The Month's '+' add button is hover-revealed (opacity 0) and forced visible at ≤900px and hidden at ≤640px — a purely-hover affordance that is easy to lose on touch.
- prefers-reduced-motion guards live in five separate blocks; schedCellIn (the Month's staggered entrance) has NO reduced-motion guard today, so a redesign that leans harder on it will make that gap worse.
- Keyboard dragging depends on real geometry (scheduleKeyboardCoordinates reads droppableRects and prefers the same row/column). Any layout that stops the cells forming a rectangular row/column grid — masonry, wrapped chips, a virtualised viewport that unmounts off-screen droppables — silently degrades arrow-key re-booking.
- Touch dragging depends on touch-action: manipulation on .schedule-job / .sched-act (schedule-phone.css L11-17) against touch-action: none on the base .schedule-job (styles.css). Re-ordering the stylesheets changes whether a swipe scrolls or lifts a card.
- The 40px tap-target block (schedule-phone.css L237-303) enumerates specific classes; new or renamed controls silently fall out of it.
- The Week page opts out of the frame's board wrapper (board=false, alerts=false) and renders its own .schedule-layout with the rail plus its own <ScheduleNotice> — the Month page does the opposite. A shared redesign of 'the board' therefore has two different DOM shapes to handle, and the notice lives in two different places.
- Cell background is set to transparent under .sched-rx while the base rule paints it #fff — the visible surface is the .schedule-board card behind it, so a new card background changes every cell at once (including the .is-holiday color-mix tints).
- Deep links and localStorage carry the week (?w=) and month (?m=) plus filters; the Copy-link test asserts the exact hash. Changing which control owns the date (e.g. one shared date picker) would change every schedule link's shape.
- Sub-pixel/colour details are asserted only by eye but load-bearing for meaning: the five status tints on Week cards vs the six trade tones on Month chips are two different colour systems on the same data — a unification would need the Week legend and the Month trade legend reconciled.

- Pending row while a re-book saves: `.is-pending` on the row button + aria-busy — opacity 0.5, pointer-events none, `sched-pending` 0.9s alternating pulse
- `busy` freezes further drops (onDragEnd returns early) and adds `.is-busy` to .schedule-list-view — NOTE: `.is-busy` has no CSS anywhere, so it is currently a no-op hook
- Undo button shows "Undoing…" and is disabled while the inverse request runs
- Calendar feeds dialog: "Loading…" helper text until fetchCalendarFeeds resolves

**Error states** (6)

- Failed re-book: notice with .is-error — "Could not move <job>: <message|request failed>"
- Failed Undo: "Could not move back <job>: <message>"
- Planner declined the double-book: "<job> stays on <Mon d>."
- Calendar feeds fetch failure: .form-error paragraph with the message or "Could not load the feed links"
- Clipboard failure: "Could not copy the link — copy the address bar instead."
- JobDrawer validation: "Both dates are required." / "The finish cannot be before the start." (role=alert), and save failure notice "Could not save <job>: <message>"

**Animations and transitions** (12)

- Three fixed radial auroras (.dx-bg > .dx-aurora-1/2/3) painted behind every schedule page
- @keyframes dx-pulse — 2.6s infinite opacity pulse on the eyebrow dot (.dx-dot); disabled under prefers-reduced-motion
- Row hover: inset 0 0 0 2px blue ring + .wx-bg-2 background
- Drag cursors: `cursor: grab` on every list row, `grabbing` on .dragging; dnd-kit CSS.Translate transform plus inline opacity 0.55 / zIndex 30 / position relative while dragging
- Drop-target highlight: .sched-list-day.drop-over gets an inset 2px --sc-concrete ring and its day head tints; the quiet line recolours
- @keyframes sched-pending — 0.9s ease-in-out infinite alternate opacity pulse on a saving row
- @keyframes sched-live-flash — 6s box-shadow/background flash + 2px blue outline on a row another tab changed (LIVE_FLASH_MS = 6000); disabled under prefers-reduced-motion
- @keyframes dx-fade-up — 0.4s fade/translate for the status filter panel opening
- KPI cards: DxTilt pointer-following perspective tilt writing --rx/--ry (max 7deg) plus a --lift: -6px hover raise and a 0.34s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) transform/shadow transition; .kpi-icon sits on translateZ(30px)
- Outline buttons / selects / export button: 0.2s background/color/border-color transitions (export button inverts to ink on hover)
- data-reveal / data-reveal-stagger scroll-reveal exists in schedule.css but is NOT active here — SchedulePageFrame's `motion` prop defaults false, so no [data-reveal] attributes and no .dx-cursor are emitted on this page
- prefers-reduced-motion block shortens reveal/KPI transitions and kills .is-pending, .is-live and .dx-dot animations, and freezes the auroras

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- All three pages are thin: they render SchedulePageFrame (client/src/schedule/page.tsx:492) and supply only a board plus (List, Kanban) a drop rule. The frame owns, in DOM order: .dx-bg auroras → .schedule-title-row.dx-hero (eyebrow/dot, h1, sub) → optional band → .schedule-control-row → ScheduleFilters → SavedViewsBar → ScheduleKpiGrid → section.schedule-board (ScheduleNotice + children) → ScheduleAlertsPanel(under) → GanttLinkDialog → ScheduleJobPickerDialog → page dialogs → conflictDialog → JobDrawer. Redesigning any one page in isolation is impossible without touching the frame.
- Root class list on all three: `schedule-page <pageClass> page-stack sched-rx gantt-page` — note every schedule page also carries `gantt-page`, so Gantt-scoped rules apply here too.
- useSchedulePage (client/src/schedule/page.tsx:84) derives everything shared: bench data (?bench=<n> deep link renders against a generated N-job workspace), the per-user schedule context (week, month, project, crew type, crew, region, status set — localStorage `bf:schedule:context:<userId>` + hash query), the SSE live feed, keys 1–6, the filtered scope, the week/day labels, the work calendar + holidays, the KPIs, the alerts, lookup maps, the notice, the conflict ask, patchJob, the drawer, dnd sensors and runChange.
- One notice component for all three (.gantt-status, role=status, aria-live=polite): 4s for news, 8s when it is an error or carries Undo; the Undo button is inside it.
- runChange() is the single write path for a board drop: card goes pending (aria-busy + .is-pending), write retried with force after the "Book anyway?" answer, reload, notice with Undo, failure notice "Could not <verb> <name>: …".
- The four KPI cards are identical on all seven schedule pages (ScheduleKpiGrid in parts/shared.tsx:214) — and on Kanban they still describe the shared WEEK even though the board is week-less.
- ScheduleExportMenu is the single export surface (schedule/ExportMenu.tsx) with four menu items; EXPORT_COLUMNS in schedule/export.ts is one fixed 15-column contract shared by every page: Date, Day, Crew, Job, Project, Phase, Status, Start, End, Labour, Hours, Location, Equipment, Materials, Conflicts. Per-page differences are only the filename, the scope window, and includeUnbooked (Kanban true; List and Matrix false).
- Placement of the Export button differs: List puts it in the CONTROL ROW with buttonClassName="outline-button"; Kanban and Matrix put it in the BOARD FOOTER with the default "export-button" class. A redesign has to keep both slots working.
- Both List and Kanban share the drag stack: useScheduleSensors (mouse 4px, touch 250ms press + 8px tolerance, keyboard with scheduleKeyboardCoordinates), scheduleCollision (pointerWithin then rectIntersection), scheduleAccessibility announcements, and a 150ms suppressClick window so the click that ends a drag does not open the drawer. Matrix has no drag at all.
- Live updates (schedule/live.ts): an EventSource on /api/schedule/events flashes .is-live + a .sched-live-by "Moved by <name>" pill for 6s on rows (List), cards (Kanban) and cells (Matrix), and coalesces a burst into one reload after 250ms.
- Status vocabulary is shared: SCHEDULE_STATUSES = JOB_STATUSES (Not Started, Planned, Ready, Ready to Start, Confirmed, In Progress, On Site, DelayIQed, Complete, At Risk); ScheduleBadge renames only "Ready to Start" → "Ready"; statusTone() lowercases and hyphenates to make the badge class; the footer legend hard-codes five of them (Confirmed, Ready, DelayIQed, In Progress, Planned) and is duplicated verbatim in all three page files.
- KANBAN_LANES (schedule/lanes.ts) is the one source for lane labels, their drop status, their match sets and their tone: Planned{Not Started,Planned}, Ready{Ready,Ready to Start,Confirmed}, In Progress{In Progress,On Site}, Blocked{DelayIQed,At Risk}, Complete{Complete}. A test asserts every status has exactly one lane.
- Holidays and the working week come only from Settings › Work calendar (workCalendarOf/holidayMap/isWorkingDay); boundary.test.ts enforces that no page hard-codes them. They surface as a List day-head tag, a Matrix column tag + tinted cells + dimmed off-days, and they divide the utilisation percentages.
- The guided tour (schedule/tour.ts) spotlights data-tutorial-id anchors that must survive: list-days, kanban-lanes, matrix-grid, plus list-page-title / kanban-page-title / matrix-page-title, schedule-filters, schedule-filters-button, schedule-saved-views, schedule-alerts.
- boundary.test.ts is an architecture guard: exactly one page module per page, App.tsx must not define a board/cell/drawer, every page must stand on useSchedulePage and derive nothing the hook already derives, every page must offer the one export menu, no page may import a sibling page, and pages.test.tsx must contain describe("List page"|"Kanban page"|"Matrix page").
- Deep-link contract per page (useScheduleContext LINK_KEYS): list = weekStart + filters, matrix = weekStart + filters, kanban = filters only. Param names w / m / crewType / crew / project / region / status.
- schedule.css is a 128 KB concatenation of formerly separate stylesheets, with the old filenames left as banner comments ("============ schedule-views.css ============", hs-kanban.css, hs-matrix.css, hs-month.css, schedule-import.css). There is no separate schedule-views.css file on disk any more.
- Everything is scoped to `.sched-rx` (plus `.gantt-page`), and the structural fallback lives in styles.css — a redesign that only edits schedule.css will still inherit styles.css grid/typography for .schedule-list-view, .schedule-legend, .kpi-grid and .schedule-board-footer.

### Omission check

**Verdict:** INCOMPLETE - the three screens, the boards and their drops are right, but ~50 further items are missing: the guided-tour overlay that renders ON these pages, most of the shared chrome's copy (status filter panel, export menu hint lines, calendar-feeds dialog, drag announcements, drawer detail), five entry points/actions outside the board (command palette, top-bar star bookmark, rail flyout, saved-views flyout, landing view cards), several data-state behaviours (opening week fallback, week<->month coupling, silently dropped filters, filtered utilisation), the absence of create/unbook anywhere in the area, the no-windowing scale property of List and Matrix, and three factual corrections (boundary.test.ts has 8 assertions not 5; List rows are sorted by a display STRING not by time; the List export button is never disabled).

Kanban's LANE_WINDOW = 24 is the only cap in the area.

**Corrections** (7)

- boundary.test.ts has EIGHT it() blocks, not 'the same five structural assertions'. The two the inventory never names are the most binding on a redesign: (a) it('defines no schedule view, board, cell or drawer in App.tsx') asserts App.tsx contains NO 'sched-' substring anywhere, no className containing 'gantt-', and no import from './schedule/parts/' (so no page class or style hook may be added in App.tsx); (b) it('keeps every schedule module inside schedule/') fails if any module matching /sched/i lands at src/ root.
- List rows are NOT in time order in the general case: the sort key is the STRING `${day}-${job.startTime}` compared with localeCompare, and startTime is a display clock ('7:00 AM'). '10:00 AM' and '12:00 PM' therefore sort BEFORE '7:00 AM'. The page's own sub-line and the inventory's 'in time order' overstate it; kpis.ts already exports parseClockTime, unused here.
- The List's Export button is passed no `disabled` prop, so unlike Kanban (busy || no jobs) and Matrix (empty week) it stays clickable with zero rows and writes a header-only CSV. The inventory records the Kanban/Matrix disabled rules but implies the List behaves the same.
- The Kanban lane header <b> is the lane's FULL job total, not the number of cards drawn - that difference is exactly what scale.test.tsx pins ('header b' > 24 while 24 cards render).
- The utilisation tones are not plain green/amber/violet: .available = var(--cc-green-soft,#e2f1e6) on var(--sc-finishes), .limited = #fdf0dc on var(--sc-framing), .busy = #efe8f8 on var(--sc-mep) - i.e. they reuse the TRADE palette, which is also what colours the Kanban card dots. Re-toning one silently re-tones the other.
- The inventory's List 'Undo' entry omits the message it produces: undone = '<crew> on <job> back on <Mon d>' (List) and '<job> back to <raw status>' (Kanban).
- Minor: the inventory says the frame renders 'ScheduleFilters -> SavedViewsBar -> ScheduleKpiGrid'; worth adding that the filters' `note` slot is used only by the Kanban and that the Kanban ALSO hides the status chip from the active-filter chips (scheduleFilterChips options.statuses === false), so a status filter set on another page stays applied nowhere and invisible here - the note sentence is the only hint.

### Redesign risks in this area

- The Matrix cell tooltip contract is pinned hard by a test: the detail string must be the button's accessible name AND the text of a child [role="tooltip"] referenced by aria-describedby, and the button must NOT have a title attribute. Moving to a title-based or portal-based tooltip breaks describe("Matrix page").
- Kanban lane order and the exact h3 labels ["Planned","Ready","In Progress","Blocked","Complete"] are asserted, as is the DOM shape .sched-kanban > section > header h3 + header b, plus job names rendered in a `strong`. Restyling lanes as anything but sections with h3 headers will fail.
- scale.test.tsx pins the lane windowing DOM exactly: .sched-kan-lane, `header b` as the total, 24 × .sched-kan-card, and a .sched-kan-more button whose text is `Show 24 more of N`. A virtualised or "load more on scroll" redesign breaks it.
- The List page must render exactly seven .sched-list-day sections (quiet days included) and each empty one must say "Nothing booked — drop a booking here"; row buttons must be accessible-named "Open <job> for <crew>". Collapsing empty days, or turning rows into non-button elements, breaks describe("List page").
- .sched-matrix-total b and .sched-matrix-util are queried by class in tests, and the utilisation aria-label must match /^\d+% of working days booked this week$/.
- Every row/card/cell is a native <button> that is simultaneously a dnd-kit draggable (listeners + attributes spread onto it). Wrapping content in extra nested buttons or anchors would break both the accessibility names and the drag activation.
- The List row is a 4-column CSS grid whose children are matched positionally on phones (`button > span:nth-child(1|2|3)` mapped to grid-areas time/job/crew, `> .badge` to status in schedule-phone.css). Reordering or adding a span silently scrambles the phone layout.
- `.list-page` and `.list-actions` have NO CSS anywhere, while `.kanban-page .kanban-actions` and `.matrix-page .matrix-actions` exist (right-align). The List page's action strip is therefore styled differently from its siblings today — an existing inconsistency to resolve deliberately, not accidentally.
- `.is-busy` is applied to .schedule-list-view while a write is in flight but has no CSS rule in any stylesheet — a dead hook that looks like a busy state in the JSX.
- The five-item status legend is duplicated verbatim in ListPage.tsx, KanbanPage.tsx and MatrixPage.tsx (and the other four pages) — three copies to keep in step, and it lists five statuses while the filter offers ten.
- Kanban's KPI row reports the shared week while the board itself ignores the week (no week stepper, no week in the link). Any visual redesign that puts the week range near the KPIs on this page will read as a bug.
- Kanban's Export uses `weekIso` for "Print week sheets" even though the board is week-less, so the printed sheets cover the shared week, not the board.
- prefers-reduced-motion handling is spread across several separate blocks in schedule.css (auroras, dx-dot, .is-pending, .is-live, .sched-kan-card) — a new motion layer needs its own guard added in each place or reduced-motion coverage regresses.
- The three .dx-aurora blobs are large blurred radial gradients rendered on every schedule page; MEMORY notes the HUD is paint-bound and blur radii were already reduced once. Adding more blurred/animated layers to these boards risks the same regression.
- schedule.css is 128 KB of concatenated former stylesheets with duplicated selectors at different specificities (e.g. `.sched-rx .sched-matrix.sched-matrix` at L2187 exists to out-specify an earlier rule, and .schedule-list-view is styled in both styles.css and schedule.css). Edits need to account for later-wins ordering and schedule-phone.css loading after it.
- Per the project's CSS pitfall note: a `*/` inside a CSS comment closes it early and silently drops the next rule — a real hazard when editing these long banner-commented sections.
- Matrix is the only board in the area with no drag, but it visually resembles the Week board (which is draggable). A redesign that unifies their look must keep the affordance difference legible (Matrix cells are `cursor: pointer`, Week/List/Kanban are `cursor: grab`).
- Cell heat uses only four levels with the load capped at 3, so a crew with 3 and one with 9 bookings look identical — a known information loss worth revisiting rather than reproducing blindly.
- The tooltip element sits inside the button's accessible-name computation, so its text is already part of the aria-label string; any redesign that makes the tooltip richer will lengthen every cell's spoken name.

### Gantt Chart page (whole page shell)

**Route:** #schedule/gantt (Page id "gantt"; hash built by scheduleHash('gantt', context) in useScheduleContext.ts; rail nav item 'Gantt Chart' with the lucide ChartGantt icon, App.tsx L647; inside the 'schedule' rail category with schedule/month/week/list/kanban/matrix, App.tsx L676)  
**Entry:** `schedule/pages/GanttPage.tsx:151 (export function GanttPage) — rendered from App.tsx:2871`

The Schedule hub's timeline view: every dated job is a bar on one shared calendar, grouped by project, coloured by the shared status palette. Dragging a bar or an edge rewrites the job's planned dates through the shared re-book/PATCH path; the page also carries the CPM readout, the critical path, baseline ghosts and the dependency network.

**Information displayed** (14)

- [ ] Page title 'Gantt Chart' as an h1 (.hs-index-title, id gantt-index-title, data-tutorial-id="gantt-page-title")
- [ ] Release pill after the title: <PageReleaseTag page="gantt"> renders .hs-page-tag with text 'New' / 'Beta' (App.tsx:812) — the Gantt's own release entry is version 3.8, 2026-09-06, spotlight 'gantt-page-title'
- [ ] Shared 4-card KPI grid above the card (ScheduleKpiGrid, .kpi-grid.schedule-kpis inside a .sched-rx.gantt-shared wrapper): 'Active Crews' = count, delta 'of N crews · X% of crew-days'; 'Scheduled Activities' = count, delta 'N hrs · $cost'; 'At-Risk Items' = count, delta 'conflicts & blockers'; 'Milestones This Month' = count, delta 'due in <Mon>'. Each card has a tooltip from kpis.definitions (crews / activities / atRisk / milestones); AT_RISK_DEFINITION = 'Bookings with a conflict note, plus jobs that are At Risk, DelayIQed or missing materials.'
- [ ] Timeline range segmented control labels: Week / Day / Month / Quarter (RANGES, GanttPage.tsx:52)
- [ ] Week window label when range === 'week': '<MMM d> – <MMM d, yyyy>' in a <strong>, plus aria-label 'Selected week …'

- [ ] Notice line (.gantt-status, role=status aria-live=polite) — e.g. '<Job>: MMM d – MMM d, yyyy' after a move, '<Job> marked complete', '<A> → <B> linked (FS, 2d lag)', '<A> and <B> unlinked', 'Baseline saved — slip is now measured against today's plan.', 'Exported N rows to buildflow-gantt.csv', 'Link copied — it opens this view on this week with these filters.', and error variants (.is-error) 'Could not save <job>: …' / 'Could not link the jobs: …' / 'Could not save the baseline: …'
- [ ] CPM readout band (ScheduleCpmSummary, .sched-cpm): 'Project finish' = formatted date or '—'; 'Critical path' = <n> 'of <total>' tasks; 'vs baseline' = 'On plan' / '+Nd' / '-Nd' / '—' with .is-late/.is-early/.is-on colouring; 'Negative float' = count of tasks with totalFloat < 0 (only when > 0). Icon = lucide GanttChartSquare
- [ ] Row cap note (.gantt-status.gantt-cap-note, role=status) when more than GANTT_ROW_CAP (300) jobs match: 'Showing the 300 jobs nearest today of <N> — filter by project, crew or week to see the rest.'
- [ ] Footer help paragraph (.gantt-note), verbatim: 'Drag a bar to move a job, drag either edge to change its dates, right-click a bar for actions — including linking it to the job that follows it. Arrows are dependencies — red on the critical path; a faint striped bar behind a job is its baseline. Flags mark each project's target completion and the workspace's holidays.'
- [ ] Schedule Alerts panel under the chart (ScheduleAlertsPanel … under, aria-label 'Schedule alerts'): heading 'Schedule Alerts', then per alert an icon, bold title, detail line and a relative time — 'Double-booked crew' / '<Crew> conflicts on <date>.' / '10m ago'; the open DelayIQ's own title / '<Project> · N day impact' / '22m ago'; 'Weather delayIQ expected' / '<Project|All sites> · <title>' / '45m ago'; 'Missing materials' / '<Job> · <phase> not confirmed' / '2h ago'
- [ ] Filter row (ScheduleFilters, .sched-filters, data-tutorial-id="schedule-filters"): current Project / Crew Type / Crew / Region select values, a 'Statuses' button with an <em> counter '<kept>/<total>', and one chip per active filter
- [ ] Saved views bar (SavedViewsBar, .sched-views-bar, aria-label 'Saved views', data-tutorial-id="schedule-saved-views"): a 'Views' label with a Pin icon, one chip per saved view (title '<description> · opens <page>'), and '+ Save view'

**Actions supported** (23)

- [ ] 'Today' button (lucide Crosshair, title 'Scroll to today') — sets scrollRequest {date: startOfDay(now), nonce: Date.now()} so GanttProvider scrolls that day a third of the way into the viewport
- [ ] 'Export' menu button (ScheduleExportMenu, buttonClassName hs-btn, aria-haspopup=menu) — see the Export menu screen
- [ ] 'Schedule' button (lucide CalendarDays, title 'Back to the Schedule overview') — onOpenSchedule() → App page 'schedule'
- [ ] Range segmented buttons Week / Day / Month / Quarter (aria-pressed, .active) — set `range`; persisted to localStorage key 'gantt:range'. 'week' maps to the chart's 'daily' range plus fit={start: weekStart, days: 7}
- [ ] Week stepper (only in Week range): 'Previous week' / 'Next week' icon buttons step the SHARED schedule week by ±7 days (setWeekStart); a 'This week' button (hidden when isThisWeek, title 'Back to the current week') jumps to mondayOf(today)
- [ ] Zoom out / Zoom in icon buttons (lucide Minus / Plus, aria-labels 'Zoom out'/'Zoom in') step through ZOOM_STEPS; both disabled while range === 'week' and at the ends; persisted to localStorage 'gantt:zoom'
- [ ] Filters: Project select, Crew Type select (clears Crew), Crew select, Region select, 'Statuses' toggle button (opens the status panel), per-status toggle chips, 'All statuses' reset, 'Clear filters', and each active-filter chip clears itself on click. All write the shared ScheduleContext, so the filter carries to every schedule page
- [ ] Saved views: click a view chip to apply its filters (and open its page if different), 'Remove saved view <name>' X per chip, '+ Save view' → inline name form (input maxLength 40, 'Save' submit, 'Cancel')
- [ ] Drag a bar body (pointer capture, 4px threshold) — moves the job: onMove → handleMove → patchJob {startDate, endDate}; the bar is optimistically overridden (overrides state) and rolled back if the save is refused
- [ ] Drag the LEFT edge handle — changes the start date only (clamped to at least one day before the end)
- [ ] Drag the RIGHT edge handle — changes the finish date only (clamped to at least one day after the start)
- [ ] Click a bar (a press that never moved) — onSelect → openJob(id) → JobDrawer
- [ ] Enter / Space on a focused bar (role=button, tabIndex 0) — opens the job drawer
- [ ] Right-click (contextMenu) a bar — the bar context menu (see modals)
- [ ] Click, or Enter / Space, on a sidebar row (role=button, tabIndex 0) — opens the same job drawer; row is .is-selected while its drawer is open
- [ ] Hover a bar — reveals the two edge resize handles (opacity 0 → 1)
- [ ] Horizontal scroll of the chart — pans time; hitting scrollLeft 0 prepends a year of timeline (and shifts scrollLeft so the view does not jump) and hitting the right end appends a year (infinite timeline). Disabled (overflow-x hidden) in fitted Week mode
- [ ] Vertical scroll — drives row windowing (useGanttRowWindow: viewport rows + 6 overscan; skipped rows become .gantt-row-spacer of the exact height)
- [ ] Keys 1–6 anywhere on the page switch schedule views (useScheduleViewKeys / SCHEDULE_VIEW_KEYS: 1 Month, 2 Week, 3 List, 4 Gantt Chart, 5 Kanban, 6 Matrix); suppressed while typing in a field, with a modifier held, or while any visible [role=dialog] is up
- [ ] Escape closes the job drawer — but only when no link dialog / alertdialog sits above it (JobDrawer checks for .schedule-dialog-backdrop, [role=alertdialog])
- [ ] Click an alert in the Schedule Alerts panel — openAlert(): sets the shared week when the alert carries one, then opens the page that owns the problem (week / delayIQs / materials / map)
- [ ] 'Re-baseline' button in the CPM band — saveBaseline() → setScheduleBaseline; shows 'Saving…' while busy and disabled meanwhile
- [ ] Hover a marker pill — reveals its date (.gantt-marker-date max-height/opacity transition)

- [ ] Sidebar group row (per project): project name (title attr = full name) + trailing count = number of job rows in that project
- [ ] Sidebar job row: status dot (STATUS_PALETTE[status].color) | job name (ellipsised, title attr = name) | meta line = crew names joined ', ' plus 'critical' or '<n>d float' (joined ' · ') | trailing = duration 'N days' / '1 day' from formatDuration(startAt, endAt)

- [ ] Bars grouped into project bands (GanttFeatureListGroup, one .gantt-feature-group per project, top-padded by one row for the group header)
