- [ ] Critical-path series: .gantt-bar.is-critical — red border + inset red ring + a 4px red left cap (--hsx-red)
- [ ] Baseline ghost series: .gantt-ghost — a dashed, 135° repeating-striped bar behind the real one, drawn only when baselineStart/baselineEnd differ from the plan; title 'Baseline: MMM d – MMM d, yyyy'
- [ ] Dependency-arrow overlay (GanttDependencyLinks): an absolutely positioned <svg class="gantt-links"> of orthogonal elbow paths, one per link with both ends on the chart; grey (rgba(87,85,80,.55), 1.5px) normally, red (--hsx-red, 2px) when both ends are critical; arrowheads from <marker id="gantt-arrow"> / <marker id="gantt-arrow-critical">; each path carries a <title> '<Pred> → <Succ> (FS +2d)'
- [ ] Vertical grid columns (.gantt-columns / .gantt-column, weekend columns .is-secondary)

**Empty states** (10)

- Chart empty (.gantt-empty, replaces the whole GanttProvider): bold 'Nothing to chart yet.' + either 'Add jobs from the Schedule page and they show up here as bars.' (when data.jobs.length === 0) or 'No jobs match these filters.' (when jobs exist but none pass the filters / have both dates)
- Status legend is omitted entirely when no visible job has a status
- CPM band is omitted when buildScheduleCpm returns null (no jobs at all)
- Saved views empty: 'Pin a filter set and your morning view is one click.'
- Schedule Alerts empty (.cc-empty-line): 'No schedule alerts for what is in view.'
- Job drawer links empty: 'No links yet. A link makes the other job wait for this one.'
- Job drawer 'Crews' fact falls back to 'Unassigned'
- Link dialog with no candidates: .form-error 'Every job on the chart already follows this one.' and a disabled select
- Calendar feeds with no crews: 'Add a crew first.'
- GanttSidebarEmptyRow exists in the component (a row-height placeholder for an empty group) but GanttPage never renders an empty group

**Loading states** (7)

- No page-level skeleton — the page is rendered from an already-fetched BootstrapPayload (App.tsx bootstrap gate is upstream)
- Re-baseline button text swaps to 'Saving…' and disables while page.busy
- Job drawer submit button swaps to 'Saving…' and disables while its own busy flag is set
- Notice Undo button swaps to 'Undoing…' and disables while the undo runs
- Calendar feeds dialog shows .helper-text 'Loading…' until fetchCalendarFeeds resolves
- Row windowing 'first paint' state: before the chart is measured (viewportHeight <= 0) exactly DEFAULT_VISIBLE_ROWS (24) rows are drawn; skipped rows are .gantt-row-spacer blocks of the exact pixel height
- Optimistic state: a dragged bar is repainted from `overrides` before the server answers (and the override is deleted if the save is refused)

**Error states** (6)

- .gantt-status.is-error notice (red) for: 'Could not save <job>: <message>', 'Could not link the jobs: <message>', 'Could not unlink <label>: <message>', 'Could not save the baseline: <message>', 'Could not copy the link — copy the address bar instead.', 'Add a crew before scheduling work.'
- CPM cycle state (.sched-cpm.sched-cpm-error, role=alert, lucide AlertTriangle): bold 'Circular dependency — the network can't be scheduled.' and the cycle as '<id> → <id> → …'. While a cycle exists no bar is marked critical and no float is shown
- Refused move: the notice reads '<Job> stays on <date>.' (or '<name> stays where it was.') and the optimistic override is reverted
- Job drawer validation (.gantt-drawer-error, role=alert): 'Both dates are required.' and 'The finish cannot be before the start.'
- Calendar feeds fetch failure: .form-error with the error message or 'Could not load the feed links'
- Link dialog: the server refuses a loop-making link and the failure surfaces as the red notice

**Animations and transitions** (12)

- @keyframes hsg-rise (schedule.css ~L4362) — opacity 0 + translateY(10px) → none; plays on .gantt-frame (0.5s), each .gantt-page .hs-kpi (0.5s with a 0.05s-per-card stagger via --i on nth-child 2/3/4) and .gantt-status (0.36s). Easing var(--hsx-ease) = cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)
- @keyframes hsg-lift (~L4715) — the pick-up spring on .gantt-feature.is-dragging .gantt-bar: scale(1) → scaleY(1.12) scaleX(1.01) → scaleY(1.06), 0.3s, plus a deep drop shadow and a blue border. Same tween the Deals board plays on a card in flight
- @keyframes hsg-land (~L4730) — the landing pulse on .gantt-feature.is-landing .gantt-bar: 0.75s scale 0.97 → 1.02 → 1 with an expanding blue ring (box-shadow 0 0 0 0 → 10px rgba(47,107,255,…) → none). Driven by a 1100ms setTimeout in GanttFeatureItem
- @keyframes hsg-fade (~L4988) — the job-drawer backdrop, 0.2s ease-out
- @keyframes hsg-slide-in (~L4995) — the job drawer itself, 0.32s var(--hsx-ease), opacity 0 + translateX(40px) → none
- @keyframes hs-pop (app-shell-hubspot.css L335) — reused by .gantt-drag-tip (0.16s) and by the .hs-menu/.gantt-menu entrance
- CSS transitions: .gantt-seg button (background/color .16s), .gantt-handle span (opacity .15s, revealed on .gantt-feature:hover or while dragging that edge), .gantt-marker-pill hover reveals .gantt-marker-date, .gantt-feature has a transition that reduced-motion turns off
- Cursor feedback: .gantt.is-dragging and every descendant get cursor: grabbing !important; the edge handles are cursor: col-resize
- Live drag tooltip .gantt-drag-tip under the bar showing '<MMM d> – <MMM d, yyyy>' while a drag is in flight
- KPI cards use the shared DxTilt pointer-following perspective tilt (--rx / --ry on .dx-tilt)
- @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) (schedule.css L5189) kills the animation on .gantt-frame, .hs-kpi, .gantt-status, .gantt-drawer, .gantt-drawer-backdrop, the dragging and landing bars, .gantt-drag-tip, .gantt-menu and .gantt-add-helper button, and the .gantt-feature transition
- No framer-motion anywhere in this area — all motion is CSS keyframes plus imperative class toggles; no data-reveal convention on this page

### Timeline chart body (the ported roadmap-ui Gantt)

**Route:** #schedule/gantt (inner region .gantt-frame > .gantt, data-tutorial-id="gantt-timeline")  
**Entry:** `components/ui/gantt.tsx:929 (GanttProvider) / :1147 (GanttTimeline); composed in GanttPage.tsx:530-620`

The scrolling two-pane chart: a sticky sidebar of job rows on the left and an infinitely extending time grid on the right, with the bars, the arrows and the markers drawn over it. A dependency-free port of the roadmap-ui / 21st.dev Gantt (no Tailwind, no shadcn, no jotai, no dnd-kit, no date-fns).

**Information displayed** (8)

- [ ] Composition, matching the original 1:1: GanttProvider > GanttSidebar (+GanttSidebarHeader, GanttSidebarGroup, GanttSidebarItem, GanttSidebarEmptyRow) + GanttTimeline > GanttHeader, GanttFeatureList > GanttFeatureListGroup > GanttFeatureItem, GanttMarker, GanttToday, GanttContextMenu, GanttColumns/GanttColumn, GanttAddFeatureHelper, GanttCreateMarkerTrigger, GanttRowSpacer
- [ ] Geometry props the page sets: sidebarWidth 300 desktop / 160 on a narrow viewport, rowHeight 36 desktop / 46 on a narrow viewport (useNarrowViewport, max-width 640px), headerHeight 56 (default)
- [ ] Column widths: 150px in Month range, 100px in Quarter, 50px in Day, all multiplied by zoom/100; in fitted Week mode columnWidth = (viewportWidth - sidebarWidth) / 7 so exactly seven days fill the pane
- [ ] CSS custom properties published on the root .gantt element: --gantt-zoom, --gantt-column-width, --gantt-header-height, --gantt-row-height, --gantt-sidebar-width
- [ ] Root classes: .gantt is-daily|is-monthly|is-quarterly, plus is-dragging while a bar is in flight, is-fitted in Week mode, is-auto-height when autoHeight (not used by this page)
- [ ] Timeline data model: an array of years, each 4 quarters × 3 months × days-in-month; seeded as last year / this year / next year and widened to cover the data span (earliest start -31d to latest end +31d)
- [ ] Bar tooltip (title attr): '<job name> · <MMM d> – <MMM d, yyyy>'
- [ ] The component re-declares the --hsx-* token set on .gantt and .gantt-menu (schedule.css L5217) so it reads the same outside .hs-index pages: ink #14203a, mut #575550, faint #8a877e, line #e6e8f0, card #fff, paper #f5f6fa, hover #f6f8fc, blue #2f6bff, blue-soft #e8f0fe, green #188038, amber #b45309, red #c5221f, ease cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)

**Actions supported** (11)

- [ ] Pointer drag on a bar's body / left handle / right handle — one pointer-capture drag with three zones (the original's three nested DndContexts collapsed into one). 4px movement threshold, then setDragging(true) and the bar renders from a local draft until pointerup
- [ ] Day-granular snapping: in Day range the delta is round(dx / columnWidth); in Month/Quarter it is the difference in days between getDateByMousePosition at the current and starting x
- [ ] pointercancel reverts the draft and clears dragging
- [ ] Enter / Space on a bar or a sidebar row — select

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- One page hook: every schedule page (including this one) stands on useSchedulePage (schedule/page.tsx). It supplies data (with the page's optimistic overrides applied), the shared ScheduleContext (week, month, project, crew type, crew, region, status set — persisted per user and reflected in the URL hash), the live-reload feed, keys 1–6, the work calendar and holiday map, the KPIs, the alerts, the lookup maps (jobsById / projectsById / crewNamesForJob), the notice + Undo, the conflict ask, the one job save, the dependency list and linkJobs/unlinkJobs, and saveBaseline. boundary.test.ts fails the build if a page derives any of these itself.
- GanttPage is the ONE schedule page that does NOT render <SchedulePageFrame> — it keeps the index-page chrome (.page-stack.gantt-page.hs-index > .hs-index-main > .hs-index-card.gantt-card) and re-assembles the shared pieces itself. boundary.test.ts encodes that exception explicitly, so a redesign that moves the Gantt into the frame (or moves the others out) breaks that test.
- components/ui/gantt.tsx is not Gantt-page-private: toIsoDate / parseIsoDate / startOfDay / addDays / formatDate are imported by schedule/week.ts, schedule/alerts.tsx, schedule/parts/JobDrawer.tsx, schedule/page.tsx and others. The file is the schedule area's date library as well as its chart.
- hs-gantt.css does not exist. Its whole content was inlined into schedule.css (128KB, ~4900 lines) under a '=== hs-gantt.css ===' banner at L4232. Several file headers still name hs-gantt.css.
- .gantt-status is the shared schedule NOTICE class, not a Gantt-only class: hooks.tsx ScheduleNotice renders it on every schedule page, and schedule.css carries .sched-rx .gantt-status (L1438) plus .week-page/.kanban-page/.matrix-page/.month-page .schedule-board .gantt-status overrides (L5458-5500). Renaming it touches all seven pages and the pages.test.tsx notice() helper.
- .gantt-drawer-* is likewise the shared JobDrawer class set used by all seven pages, but it is only defined under .gantt-page (schedule.css L4962+) plus a few .sched-rx overrides — a redesign must keep both scopes in step.
- Local preferences: localStorage 'gantt:range' and 'gantt:zoom' (read through readPreference/writePreference with a try/catch for private mode). Everything else (week, filters, statuses) lives in the shared ScheduleContext.
- Optimistic writes: GanttPage owns an `overrides: Record<jobId, Partial<Job>>` map that is merged over the server's jobs by useSchedulePage and cleared whenever liveData.jobs changes; a refused save deletes just that job's override.
- Scale guards: GANTT_ROW_CAP = 300 bars (upcoming first, then most-recent past), chartLinks filtered to links with both ends on the chart, and row windowing (useGanttRowWindow, DEFAULT_VISIBLE_ROWS = 24, overscan 6) with GanttRowSpacer standing in for skipped rows on BOTH panes via the WindowedGroups helper.
- Phone behaviour: useNarrowViewport(640) switches sidebarWidth 300→160 and rowHeight 36→46 in JS; schedule-phone.css enforces 40px tap targets on the toolbar, the drawer and the CPM baseline button, and wraps the index head.
- Tutorial anchors on this page: data-tutorial-id="gantt-page-title" (the release spotlight for v3.8) and data-tutorial-id="gantt-timeline" (the guided-tour stop 'Gantt Chart: bars, links and the critical path'), plus the shared "schedule-filters", "schedule-filters-button", "schedule-saved-views" and "schedule-alerts" anchors.
- The Home page carries a dismissible promo card 'Try the new Gantt Chart' → setPage('gantt') (App.tsx ~L26724, localStorage key 'bf:home:promo:gantt').
- No framer-motion, no data-reveal, no data-reveal-stagger in this area — all motion is CSS keyframes (hsg-rise / hsg-lift / hsg-land / hsg-fade / hsg-slide-in / hs-pop) plus imperatively toggled classes.

### Omission check

**Verdict:** INCOMPLETE — the inventory is unusually strong on the chart mechanics, but it misses 6 reachable surfaces, ~22 information items (including 5 exact copy value-sets and every bar hover/focus/selected state), ~9 actions, and it states one geometry number wrongly (narrow-viewport sidebarWidth is 104, not 160). A redesign built from it alone would silently drop the multi-clash list in the conflict dialog, the status-filter panel's heading and helper copy, the printed crew week sheet, and the bar's hover/focus/selected treatments.

One page per crew (page-break-after: always): h1 = crew name; sub = '<specialty> · foreman <lead> · <Mon d – Mon d>'; a 7-row table, each row '<Day, Mon d>' | either job blocks (bold job name, '<project> · <phase>', '<startTime> – <endTime> · <location>', and the booking's conflicts in red) or '—' when the crew is free; footer '<sheetTitle> · printed <M/D/YYYY>'. It has its own inline stylesheet (@page margin 14mm, Inter 13px, #14203a ink, #c5221f conflicts, #a5adbf for the free dash). The inventory lists 'Print week sheets' as an action but never inventories what it prints.
- [ ] GUIDED-TOUR COACH MARK OVER THIS PAGE (App.tsx ~L21360). The inventory records only the anchor data-tutorial-id="gantt-timeline". **Information the first pass missed** (22)

- [ ] WRONG NUMBER: the narrow-viewport sidebar is 104px, not 160px — GanttPage.tsx renders sidebarWidth={phone ? 104 : 300} (rowHeight 46/36 is correct).
- [ ] DEFAULT STATES are never stated: range defaults to 'monthly' on a desktop and 'week' on a narrow viewport (readPreference('gantt:range', narrowViewport() ? 'week' : 'monthly')); zoom defaults to 100.
- [ ] NOTICE AUTO-DISMISSES — useScheduleNotice clears it after 4000ms, or 8000ms when it is an error or carries an Undo. The notice is therefore a transient element, not a persistent band.
- [ ] NOTICE VALUE SET INCOMPLETE. Also: a save where nothing actually changed still says the done text and returns true (useJobSave early return).
- [ ] CONFLICT DIALOG EXACT COPY (conflicts.ts clashSentence): '<CrewName> is on <JobName> that day', plus ' (and N more)' when there is more than one clash, with the no-clash fallback 'That crew is already booked that day'. The body then appends ' — book <Job> on <date> anyway?'. The buttons are literally 'Cancel' and 'Book anyway' (the latter autoFocus) plus an X with aria-label 'Keep the schedule as it is'. The inventory only says 'the clash sentence (which crew, which day)' and 'Answer yes / Answer no'.
- [ ] FILTER CHIP VALUE SET (filters.ts scheduleFilterChips): project name / crew type / crew name / region, and for statuses either '<A> · <B>' when 2 or fewer are kept or '<N> of 10 statuses' otherwise. Each chip carries title='Clear <label>' and an X icon; the row is aria-label 'Active filters'. The inventory says only 'one chip per active filter'.

### Redesign risks in this area

- boundary.test.ts asserts App.tsx contains NO /className=[^\n]*gantt-/ and that GanttPage is the only page without <SchedulePageFrame>. Any redesign that hoists Gantt markup into App.tsx, or that normalises the Gantt into the shared frame, fails the suite as written.
- Renaming .gantt-status breaks the notice on all seven schedule pages and the pages.test.tsx notice() helper; renaming .gantt-drawer-* breaks the shared JobDrawer everywhere; renaming .gantt-frame, .gantt-cap-note, .gantt-sidebar, .gantt-sidebar-item, .gantt-row-spacer, .gantt-ctx, .gantt-marker or .gantt-links breaks scale.test.tsx, pages.test.tsx and GanttDependencyLinks.test.tsx selectors.
- GanttDependencyLinks measures real DOM: it queries '.gantt-feature[data-feature-id="…"]' inside '.gantt-feature-list' and reads getBoundingClientRect + list.scrollWidth/offsetHeight. Changing the bar wrapper structure, the feature-list class, or the header offset (the svg is positioned at top: var(--gantt-header-height)) silently mis-draws every arrow.
- Bar positioning is absolute pixel maths from getOffset/getWidth against --gantt-column-width; switching to a CSS grid or flex layout for bars would invalidate the drag maths, the arrow overlay, the markers and the fitted Week mode all at once.
- The three drag zones are one pointer-capture handler with a 4px threshold and an 1100ms landing timer; the handles are 12px wide and sit at -6px outside the bar (.gantt-handle.is-left/.is-right). Restyling bar padding, radius or overflow can swallow the handles or the hit area.
- Fitted Week mode computes columnWidth from clientWidth - sidebarWidth and hides overflow-x. Changing the sidebar width, adding a scrollbar gutter, or putting the chart in a differently sized container makes the seven-day fit drift.
- .gantt-frame height is a hard clamp(420px, calc(100vh - 336px), 900px) — the 336px is the sum of the current header/KPI/toolbar/CPM/note chrome. Any change in that chrome's height silently mis-sizes the chart on every screen.
- The row-window contract is that the sidebar and the timeline render the SAME window from the SAME layout (WindowedGroups + rowLayout, group header counted as one row). If the two panes ever compute rows differently, or if a group header stops being exactly one rowHeight tall, the two sides de-sync — and scale.test.tsx asserts sidebar rows === bar count.
- Row height is a hard 36/46px in JS (rowHeight prop) and echoed as --gantt-row-height, and the ghost bar is height: calc(var(--gantt-row-height) - 18px) with top: 9px. Variable-height rows are not supported by the windowing maths.
- STATUS_PALETTE is shared by the bars, the legend, the badges and the Schedule board cards — restyling bar colours here changes the other views' colours too, and the fill/edge/ink triple is consumed through the --gantt-bar-* custom properties set inline on each bar.
- The critical-path and float readout come from a CPM run over the WHOLE plan on a working-day axis (buildScheduleCpm with the workspace work calendar), not the filtered subset; a cycle turns the readout into an alert band and drops all critical marking. A redesign must keep the cycle state as a distinct visual state.
- Two dormant affordances exist in the component and are styled but never mounted by this page: GanttAddFeatureHelper (the hover '+' in a column, needs onAddItem) and GanttCreateMarkerTrigger, plus the marker tone-amber / tone-red / tone-green classes and the marker onRemove context menu. Easy to delete by mistake, or to accidentally 'discover' as a feature.
- Only .gantt-page scopes most of the page CSS while the component re-declares its own --hsx-* tokens on .gantt/.gantt-menu — the context menu is portalled to document.body, so it must keep its own tokens or it loses every colour.
- The chart's infinite horizontal scroll mutates timelineData on scroll and compensates scrollLeft with pendingShift; any new sticky/overlay chrome inside the scroller, or a change of scroll container, can cause a visible jump at the year boundaries.
- user-select: none is set on the whole .gantt (and grabbing !important while dragging) — job names in the chart cannot be selected or copied today; a redesign that 'fixes' this can break the drag threshold.
- Comments in three files still say 'styled by hs-gantt.css'; anyone following that trail will not find the stylesheet.

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- Class stack on the page root is `page-stack projects-page proj-rx hs-index` — the page is styled by TWO competing systems: hs-index.css (the live HubSpot index look: --hsx-* tokens, Inter, 10px radii, #e6e8f0 hairlines) and projects-redesign.css (the older Antigravity reskin: --wx-*/--cc-* tokens, Iowan Old Style serif display, 20px radii, warm paper). Only the .proj-rx tokens, the aurora/cursor background, .badge overrides, .cc-stat-ico tones, .cc-list/.cc-alert*/.cc-empty-line and the .proj-mile*/.proj-health* rail blocks are still reachable from projects-redesign.css.
- Design tokens actually in play — hs-index.css :11-40: --hsx-sans Inter, --hsx-ink #14203a, --hsx-text #1c1c1a, --hsx-mut #575550, --hsx-faint #8a877e, --hsx-line #e6e8f0, --hsx-line-soft #eef0f4, --hsx-card #fff, --hsx-paper #f5f6fa, --hsx-hover #f6f8fc, --hsx-blue #2f6bff / soft #e8f0fe, --hsx-green #188038 / #e2f1e6, --hsx-amber #b45309 / #fdf0dc, --hsx-red #c5221f / #fbe4e2, --hsx-violet #6d28d9 / #efe8f8, --hsx-ease cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). projects-redesign.css :9-42 adds a parallel --wx-*/--cc-* set with the SAME colour values under different names.
- Page-frame hack: .proj-rx uses `margin: -22px -28px -34px` to bleed outside the app shell's padding, plus `overflow: clip` and `isolation: isolate` — the isolation is what forces both dialogs to be portalled to <body> (documented at App.tsx:27155). Any new page frame must preserve or consciously replace this.
- Layout: .hs-index .hs-index-grid = `minmax(0,1fr) 330px`; every track in the chain carries minmax(0,·)/min-width:0 with a comment explaining that otherwise the nowrap table's intrinsic width blows the card to ~1900px (hs-index.css:36-45). The rail is `position: sticky; top: 74px`. The table scrolls horizontally inside .hs-table-wrap (overflow-x:auto). Breakpoints: 1240px collapses to one column and puts the rail in 3 columns / KPIs in 3; 860px stacks the rail, KPIs go 2-up, and the footer centers. projects-redesign.css adds its own now-mostly-dead 1200/1080/820/720/560px rules.
- Icon set is lucide-react: Building2, CheckCircle2, AlertTriangle, Gauge, ClipboardCheck, CalendarDays, CloudSun, Truck, Search, SlidersHorizontal, ChevronDown, ChevronLeft, ChevronRight, Plus, FileUp, Download, MapPin, Sparkles, Trash2, X.
- Charts come from recharts (PieChart / Pie / Cell / ResponsiveContainer) — only the Portfolio Health donut. There is no recharts anything in the table or KPI strip.
- No framer-motion, no Tailwind, no shadcn anywhere in this area. All motion is CSS keyframes/transitions plus the useHudMotion pointer-variable hook.
- Data source: the single `data: BootstrapPayload` prop (data.projects, data.users, data.jobs, data.phases, data.delayIQs, data.weatherAlerts, data.materials, data.activeUser) plus ONE extra fetch, fetchScheduleStatus() → GET /api/schedule/status, kept in a Record<projectId, ScheduleStatusProject> and used only for forecastFinish and daysAhead.
- Mutations: createProject (POST /api/projects), updateProject (PATCH /api/projects/:id), deleteProject (DELETE /api/projects/:id) — each followed by the page-level `reload()` which re-fetches /api/bootstrap. There is no optimistic update anywhere.
- Shared helpers a redesign must keep honouring: statusTone() (schedule/scheduleUtils.ts:48 — lowercases and hyphenates), formatDate() (formatDate.ts:3 — "Dec 18, 2026", passes through the literal "Pending"), formatScheduleDate() (schedule/week.ts:9 — "Dec 18"), projectInitials() (App.tsx:39169), projectName() (App.tsx:39165 — falls back to "Unassigned"), projectAvatarThemes (App.tsx:882), projectStatusOrder (App.tsx:891), projectEditableStatuses = [...JOB_STATUSES] (App.tsx:902), projectScheduleHealthOptions (App.tsx:904), initialProjectInput (App.tsx:914), useModalDialog (App.tsx:22979), useHudMotion (useHudMotion.ts).
- The Project type (shared/src/index.ts:111) is the field contract: id, name, slug, location, address, type, contractType, managerId, targetCompletion, percentComplete, scheduleHealth (On Track|Monitor|At Risk|Complete), status (Status), value?, image, latitude, longitude. UpdateProjectInput/CreateProjectInput exclude id/slug/image/lat/long, so the dialog cannot set the avatar theme or coordinates.
- ScheduleStatusProject (api.ts:526 + shared/src/progress.ts:96) offers plannedFinish, forecastFinish, daysAhead, percentComplete, reportingJobs, totalJobs, name, daysAheadDelta, percentDelta — the page currently surfaces only forecastFinish and daysAhead, leaving plannedFinish, reportingJobs/totalJobs (the evidence behind the forecast) and both week-over-week deltas unused.
- The .pdx dialog system is SHARED: project-dialog-redesign.css also styles the Crew add/edit dialog and its remove-confirm (it carries .crew-size-preview, .labor-mix-toolbar, .labor-mix-row, .pdx-add-role, .pdx-role-remove blocks) and is reused as the shell by schedule/ScheduleImportDialog.tsx (.sim-*). Restyling .pdx changes Crews and the schedule importer too.
- hs-index.css is SHARED by Projects, Crews, Equipment, Materials, Field Updates, Bookmarks (App.tsx:20445), Contacts (App.tsx:30430) and the Gantt page (schedule/pages/GanttPage.tsx:379). Anything changed there ripples across all of them.
- Accessibility already in place and worth preserving: aria-labelledby on the index section, role=tablist/tab + aria-selected on the saved views, aria-label on every filter select and checkbox, aria-current="page" on the active pagination button, aria-modal + labelled/described dialogs, role="alert" on both form errors, and the useModalDialog focus trap that prefers the first form field over the close button.

### Redesign risks in this area

- Roughly half of projects-redesign.css (1219 lines) is DEAD for this page: the whole card-grid era — .projects-hero, .dx-hero-copy, .dx-eyebrow, .dx-dot, .dx-title, .dx-sub, .new-project-button, .project-select-control, .project-search-control, .project-card-grid, .dx-tilt, .project-card(.selected), .project-initials, .project-card-title/-meta/-header, .project-progress-summary, .project-health(.monitor/.delayIQed/.complete), .project-progress-track, .project-empty-state, .card-open, .card-delete, .cc-stat-grid/.cc-stat/.cc-stat-top/-mid/-foot/.cc-stat-value/.cc-stat-label/.cc-stat-note/.cc-spark*/.cc-trend, .proj-grid/.proj-main/.proj-rail/.proj-panel/.proj-panel-head/.proj-rail-link, .cc-hero/.cc-eyebrow/.cc-hero-head/-icon/-title/-sub, and .project-days/.project-forecast. Verified: grep for `project-card|card-delete|projects-hero|project-days|dx-tilt|project-initials|new-project-button` in App.tsx returns ZERO hits. Do not port these; but do not delete blindly either — .cc-* names are shared vocabulary with dashboard-redesign.css and the crew/equipment pages.
- The prompt's brief mentions a 'cc-* command-center hero', 'project cards' with per-card meta cells (health pill, forecast date, ±days chip, percent bar, contract value, location, manager) and 'hover-reveal delete' on cards. Those are the PREVIOUS design. The page was rebuilt as a HubSpot index on 2026-09-04: there is no hero and no card grid; every one of those meta cells is now a table COLUMN, and the hover-reveal delete is now .hs-row-action on table rows. Any redesign must decide explicitly whether to bring cards back — the four index-pages tests all query a `role="table"` and a row-scoped `Edit <name>` button and would break.
- The KPI strip's trends are FABRICATED: the delta strings "+2", "+3", "-1", "+6%", "+2" and the notes "vs last month" / "this quarter" are hard-coded literals with no data behind them, and the per-tile `spark` arrays and `trend` values are computed but never rendered. The real week-over-week numbers exist (ScheduleStatusResponse.history and each project's daysAheadDelta/percentDelta) and are unused. A redesign that renders sparklines would be showing invented history unless it re-wires to that source.
- The Project Alerts panel's timestamps "10m ago", "45m ago", "2h ago" are hard-coded literals bearing no relation to the underlying records. The Dashboard's equivalent panel does use real `time[datetime]` elements (App.test.tsx:1308) — the Projects rail does not.
- Existing CSS bug: `.proj-rx .badge.delayIQed` (projects-redesign.css:434) can never match. statusTone() lowercases, so the DOM class is `delayiqed`, and class selectors are case-sensitive in HTML documents. DelayIQed status badges therefore fall through to the neutral #ebedfb base instead of the red tone. Same suspect pattern to check elsewhere in the repo.
- Token naming trap: `--wx-amber: #0032b0` in projects-redesign.css:22 is BLUE, not amber, and the .badge.planned/.monitor/.ready-to-start group uses it over a #d2defb blue-lilac ground. Anyone 'fixing the amber' will silently change those badges.
- The 'Filter' toolbar chip and the 'Advanced filters' link both only call clearProjectFilters() — neither opens any filter surface. The chip's own title even reads "Use the filters below". A redesign should either build the promised panel or relabel; the tests do not touch either control, so behaviour is free.
- The h1's ChevronDown button looks like a view dropdown but only resets projectView to "all" (aria-label "Show all projects"). Same trap in reverse: it will read as a broken menu in any new design.
- Sorting is string-based for Status and Schedule health (localeCompare on the raw label), so 'At Risk' < 'Complete' < 'Monitor' < 'On Track' alphabetically — the sorted order is meaningless as a severity ranking. Only the default 'status' key uses the real projectStatusOrder severity map.
- Three columns are deliberately un-sortable (Forecast finish, Contract, Location) while the other eight are — an inconsistency that will look like a bug in a cleaner table. Forecast finish is the one users would most want to sort.
- Row selection is a dead end: checkboxes, select-all and the 'N selected' footer text all work, but there is no bulk-action bar, no bulk delete and no bulk export (Export always exports the full filtered set, ignoring selection). A test pins the unchecked initial state of one checkbox, nothing more.
- The CSV export uses `URL.createObjectURL` + a synthetic `<a download>.click()`. That is fine in the app, but the same pattern is inert inside a published Artifact sandbox — relevant only if any of this is ever mirrored into one.
- The Contract Value input strips all non-digits, so it silently discards cents and cannot express a negative or a decimal; the label's accessible name includes the literal '(optional)', which a redesign that moves the optional marker out of the <span> would break for `getByLabelText("Contract Value")`-style queries (no current test uses that label, but four tests use getByLabelText for the other fields).
- The '% Complete must be a whole number from 0 to 100.' error renders whenever the value is invalid — including the instant a user clears the field to retype. Every other required field fails silently by only disabling submit, so the form gives no indication of WHICH field is blocking. Fixing that is a behaviour change beyond visual redesign.
- The Project Manager select silently renders zero options when no user has role 'Project Manager' or 'Superintendent', permanently disabling submit with no message.
- The forecast columns appear only after an async fetch and only for projects that have jobs, so the same table can show 'Forecast finish' populated for some rows and '—' for others; a design that gives Forecast finish visual prominence will look broken on a fresh workspace.
- ProjectThumb (App.tsx:27013) is confirmed dead code. imageThemes (App.tsx:874) is still used by four other call sites — remove the component, keep the map.
- Two headings collide with other areas: 'Project Alerts' also exists as a Dashboard dash-block (App.test.tsx:1304-1374 asserts on THAT one, including a role=region named 'Project Alerts contents'), and 'Upcoming Milestones' also exists on the Schedule landing page (schedule/pages/SchedulePage.tsx:102). Global text queries in any new test will be ambiguous.
- Restyling .pdx touches the Crew dialogs and the schedule import dialog; restyling hs-index.css touches Crews, Equipment, Materials, Field Updates, Contacts, Bookmarks and the Gantt page. Neither stylesheet can be treated as Projects-only.
- The min-width:0 / minmax(0,1fr) chain in hs-index.css exists for a reason documented in a comment: removing any link of it makes the 13-column nowrap table blow the card out to ~1900px and push the header and footer off-screen. Preserve it in any new layout.
- The page has no data-reveal nodes yet the reveal machinery is still wired (useHudMotion adds .dx-ready and queries for them). If a redesign adds [data-reveal] with a DYNAMIC className, the known repo trap applies: a dynamic className wipes the imperatively-added .in class and the element stays at opacity:0.

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- All three in-app pages are the SAME component skeleton: `<div className="page-stack {crews|equipment|materials}-page {crew|equip|mat}-rx hs-index">` → .dx-bg with 3 auroras + .dx-cursor → .hs-kpis (4 tiles) → .hs-index-main > .hs-index-card (title+Add, .hs-views tabs, .hs-toolbar, .hs-quickfilters, .hs-table-wrap > .hs-table, .hs-index-foot) → dialogs. Redesigning one without the others will immediately look broken; they are effectively one template with three data bindings. The Projects and Field Updates pages (other agents' areas) use the same hs-index template.
- hs-index.css is the real design surface. .crew-rx / .equip-rx / .mat-rx now only contribute the page background (paper colour, 3 blurred auroras, the negative -22px/-28px/-34px bleed margin, min-height calc(100vh - 87px), isolation:isolate, overflow:clip) plus dialog re-skins. Their token blocks (--wx-*, --cc-*) are duplicated verbatim across the three files.
- Every table is `white-space: nowrap` with `min-width: 720px` inside an `overflow-x: auto` .hs-table-wrap, and thead th is `position: sticky; top: 0`. The whole grid chain uses minmax(0,1fr) + min-width:0 to stop the nowrap table blowing the card to ~1900px (comment at hs-index.css:38-42) — do not remove those constraints in a redesign.
- Utilization / readiness percentages on Equipment and Materials are NOT real data — they are pure functions of the status enum (equipmentUsageProgress 78/38/12 at App.tsx:36428; materialReadinessProgress 100/68/42/12 at App.tsx:39083). Only Crews has a genuine per-crew utilization number from the backend. A redesign that leans harder on these meters will be amplifying fake precision.
- 'Advanced filters' is a lie on all three pages: the link just calls clearXFilters(); there is no advanced-filter panel behind it.
- The 'Sort by <key>' toolbar chip hard-codes ONE key per page (crews → utilization, equipment → status, materials → delivery) even though it displays whichever key is live; the real multi-key sorting is only reachable from the column headers.
- Hover-reveal row actions: .hs-row-action starts at opacity 0 and only appears on tr:hover / :focus-visible, with `@media (hover: none) { opacity: 1 }` for touch. Crews has one (delete), Equipment has two (.hs-cell-actions.two: pencil + trash), Materials has none.
- CSV export is identical machinery on all three (build rows → quote-escape → Blob text/csv → object URL → synthetic anchor click → revokeObjectURL), always exporting the FILTERED set, filenames buildflow-crews.csv / buildflow-equipment.csv / buildflow-materials.csv.
- Two different dialog systems coexist. Crews uses the pdx system (project-dialog-redesign.css): portalled to document.body, aurora glow, backdrop-in/dialog-in/field-in keyframes, useModalDialog focus trap + Escape. Equipment and Materials use the plain styles.css .crew-dialog shell re-skinned per page: rendered inline, NO entrance animation, NO focus trap, NO Escape handler. Unifying them is the single biggest visual win available in this area.
- data-tutorial-id anchors that must survive: crews-page-title, crew-add-button, crew-dialog (App.tsx:1698/1708 tutorial steps + validation via targetExists), equipment-page-title (App.tsx:1784, the Equipment Tracking product lesson), materials-page-title. The 'What's new' update modal also spotlights crews-page-title (App.tsx:17291, v3.3) and materials-page-title (App.tsx:17266, v3.4).
- Equipment is an add-on-locked page (ADD_ON_PAGE_LOCKS.equipment = 'equipment-tracking', $9/user/month, included in business + enterprise). setPage() intercepts navigation and shows the add-on prompt; tests must seed selectedProducts: ['equipment-tracking'] to reach it.
- Navigation: navItems (App.tsx:654/659/660) gives the labels+icons (Crews/Users, Equipment/Wrench, Materials/Boxes); navHubs (App.tsx:678-682) puts Crews in the 'operations' hub with Projects and Equipment+Materials in the 'resources' hub. The top-bar 'Create new' menu has a 'Crew' entry (App.tsx:20917) that only navigates — unlike Contacts/Companies/Deals it passes no createSignal, so the Add Crew dialog does NOT auto-open.
- Materials is create-only: api.ts exposes createMaterial (line 473) but no updateMaterial or deleteMaterial, and there is no material edit or delete UI anywhere. Crews and Equipment are full CRUD (crews POST/PATCH/DELETE at api.ts:432-450 with the DELETE cascading to assignments; equipment POST/PATCH/DELETE at api.ts:453-471).
- Every mutation is followed by `await reload()` (a full /api/bootstrap refetch) — there is no optimistic update, so a redesign cannot assume instant row changes.
- useHudMotion (useHudMotion.ts) runs on all three pages: rAF-throttled pointermove writing --mx/--my/--px/--py, plus adding the 'dx-ready' class and observing [data-reveal]/[data-reveal-stagger]. Since none of the three pages carries a data-reveal attribute any more, the reveal half is inert and the pointer half only feeds the .dx-cursor glow (styled on equip-rx/mat-rx, NOT on crew-rx).

- [ ] The locked-Equipment path as a set of actions: clicking the Equipment flyout row calls onRequestAddOn('equipment-tracking') INSTEAD of navigating; the resulting AddOnPrompt offers 'Purchase in Billing' (-> Settings, view 'billing', with settingsFocusAddOn set so the Equipment Tracking add-on row is highlighted), 'Not now', an X labelled 'Close', Escape, and a Tab focus trap. Closing Settings returns to settingsReturnPage.
- [ ] Clicking the Resources rail hub icon (conditional destination: Equipment if unlocked, else Materials) and the Operations hub icon (always Projects). Also: the flyout opens on onFocus as well as hover, so all three pages are reachable by keyboard without a pointer.
- [ ] Focus RETURN on dialog close: useModalDialog's cleanup calls opener?.focus?.(), so closing the Add/Edit Crew or Delete-crew dialog puts focus back on the row link, row trash or Add Crew button that opened it. Not recorded anywhere in the inventory (and it is a behaviour Equipment/Materials dialogs do not have, since useModalDialog is not wired there).
- [ ] Row selection has NO consumer anywhere in the area. There is no bulk edit, bulk delete, bulk assign or export-selected: the checkboxes and the ' . N selected' footer pill are the only readers of crewSelected / equipmentSelected / materialSelected, and Export always writes the FILTERED set, never the selection. Worse, the selection Sets are never cleared by a view tab, quick filter, search or page change, so 'N selected' can count rows that are not on screen. A redesign should be told this is a dead-end affordance rather than reproducing it as if it drove something.
- [ ] The page number is only clamped for rendering (crewCurrentPage = Math.min(crewPage, crewPageCount)) - the crewPage / equipmentPage / materialPage state is not reset - so narrowing a filter and then widening it again snaps back to the previously held page rather than page 1.
- [ ] The four KPI tiles on each page are inert: plain <div class='hs-kpi'> with no onClick, no role and no href, so 'Available Now' is NOT a shortcut to the Available saved view even though the saved-view tab beside it is. Worth stating explicitly so a redesign neither drops an affordance that exists nor invents one that does not.
- [ ] The Equipment remove-confirm button has no per-item accessible name: it is just 'Remove Equipment', identical to the dialog's own h2, while the row action that opens it is 'Remove <name>'. Crews' equivalent is aria-label 'Confirm delete <crew name>'. tests/index-pages.test.tsx:419 resolves the collision by scoping with within(dialog).

**States or motion the first pass missed** (4)

- [ ] Reduced motion diverges across the three pages: Equipment and Materials freeze the parallax auroras with transform: none !important, Crews has no aurora reset (it has no parallax to stop) and instead only shortens the dead [data-reveal] transitions and the dead .crew-utilization-track transition.
- [ ] hs-index.css:822 @media (hover: none) { .hs-row-action { opacity: 1 } } is recorded, but not that it applies to BOTH equipment row actions (pencil and trash) and that Materials has no row action for it to apply to - so on touch the three pages present 1, 2 and 0 always-visible row controls respectively.
- [ ] The 'is-selected' row tint doubles as an 'editing this record' indicator (selectedCrewId / selectedEquipmentId), so on Crews and Equipment a row stays highlighted for the whole life of its edit dialog even with no checkbox ticked.
- [ ] crews-redesign.css:92 `.crew-rx > *:not(.dx-bg):not(.dx-cursor)` is the rule that stacks page content above the background; .dx-cursor is excluded there but given no visual rule of its own, which is why the Crews cursor glow is invisible (the inventory's finding is correct - noting the mechanism so a redesign does not 'fix' it by accident).

**Corrections** (7)

- WRONG - Materials 'Job' column: the inventory says jobForMaterial matches the project's job whose materialsStatus mirrors the material status 'else Project stock'. It actually falls back to `data.jobs.find(job => job.projectId === material.projectId)` (App.tsx:39097), so a non-matching status still names the project's FIRST job. 'Project stock' appears only when the project has no jobs at all.
- WRONG - Equipment 'Current job' column: the inventory says activeJobForProject returns 'the first non-Complete job on that project, else Ready for assignment'. It falls back to `data.jobs.find(job => job.projectId === projectId)` (App.tsx:36440), so the cell can name a COMPLETE job. 'Ready for assignment' appears only when the equipment is unassigned or the project has no jobs.
- WRONG - Crews 'Current job' column: the inventory says activeAssignmentForCrew takes 'the crew's earliest non-DelayIQed assignment, else Unassigned'. It uses `activeAssignments.length > 0 ? activeAssignments : assignments` (App.tsx:35682), so a crew whose only assignments are DelayIQed still shows that job. 'Unassigned' appears only when the crew has no assignments at all.
- WRONG - initial dialog focus on the Crews page. The inventory states as a blanket rule that 'focus lands on the first .pdx-form field, not the close button'. useModalDialog (App.tsx:22999) queries '.pdx-form input, .pdx-form select, .pdx-form textarea' and falls back to focusables()[0]; the delete-crew dialog has NO .pdx-form (its content is .pdx-body), so focus there lands on the X CLOSE button. True only of the add/edit dialog.
- OVERSTATED - Materials avatar tinting. There is no .hs-avatar.tone-blue rule in hs-index.css, so an Ordered material's avatar renders as the untoned default. Only Ready (green), Waiting on Delivery (amber) and Missing (red) are actually tinted.
- INCOMPLETE - aurora motion. Described as static for Crews (correct) but left unqualified for Equipment and Materials, where the blobs translate with the pointer via --px/--py and carry will-change: transform. This is the paint-cost hotspot on those two pages, alongside the 480px .dx-cursor glow.
- INCOMPLETE - the 'Sort by' chip's active state. The inventory notes Materials defaults to sort key 'delivery', but not that the chip's `active` class is tested against that same per-page default (`crewSortKey !== 'name'`, `equipmentSortKey !== 'name'`, `materialSortKey !== 'delivery'`), so the chip's rest appearance is not consistent across the three pages.

### Redesign risks in this area

- MASSIVE DEAD CSS. crews-redesign.css (747), equipment-redesign.css (848) and materials-redesign.css (796) were written for a card-directory layout that no longer exists. Confirmed unused in App.tsx: .crew-directory-grid, .crew-card-open, .card-delete, .crews-hero/.equipment-hero/.materials-hero, .crew-search-box, .crew-utilization(-track), .crew-detail-list, .crew-current-job, .crew-search-empty/.equipment-search-empty/.material-search-empty, .crew-stat-card/.crew-stat-grid, .crew-card-icon/.equipment-card-icon/.material-card-icon, .equipment-card-actions, .dx-tilt/.dx-title/.dx-sub/.dx-eyebrow, .crew-status-pill.*. (.crew-directory-card and .crew-status-pill survive only because the Field Updates page reuses them at App.tsx:37852/37861 — deleting those rules will break Field Updates, not Crews.) Roughly 1,800 lines can be retired, but only after auditing cross-page reuse.
- The brief's KpiStatCard component does NOT exist in the codebase (grep returns nothing). The KPI tiles are inline .hs-kpi markup, duplicated verbatim four times per page across three pages (12 copies). Any redesign should factor them, and tests reference their label text ('Total Crews', 'Total Equipment', 'Total Materials', 'Ready Now') so the strings must survive.
- The brief's 'crew click-to-edit / hover-reveal delete / directory cards' describes the PREVIOUS design. The live Crews page has no cards at all — it is a table with a name-cell link (aria-label 'Edit <name>') and a hover-revealed trash cell. The 'hover-reveal delete' now lives in hs-index.css (.hs-row-action opacity 0→1), not in crews-redesign.css (.card-delete).
- CrewStatusLegend advertises five statuses but Crew['status'] only has three ('Available' | 'Scheduled' | 'Overbooked'). 'In Progress' and 'Unavailable' can never appear in a row, yet App.test.tsx:749-751 asserts all five labels — so a redesign cannot simply trim the legend without touching that test.
- The Crews table relabels the stored status 'Scheduled' as 'On Job' for display and sorting (crewStatusLabel), while the quick-filter select uses value='Scheduled' with the label 'On Job' and the saved-view id is 'on-job'. Three names for one state; easy to break during a rewrite.
- The Crews page renders <div class='dx-cursor'> but crews-redesign.css never styles it — an invisible always-mounted node. Equipment/Materials do style it as a 480px pointer-following radial gradient, which is a paint-cost hotspot on this codebase (see the HUD paint-perf memory).
- Equipment and Materials dialogs have NO focus trap and NO Escape-to-close (useModalDialog is only wired on the Crews page). Any redesign should fix this, but it changes keyboard behaviour the tests do not currently cover.
- The Equipment name column and the pencil row action share the identical accessible name 'Edit <name>' — tests/index-pages.test.tsx:352 works around it with getAllByRole(...)[0]. Renaming either label will break those tests; consolidating them is safe only if the tests are updated.
- Materials rows have no addressable control at all beyond the row checkbox, and tests/index-pages.test.tsx:487 locates rows via `getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select Ready Mix Concrete' })`. Removing or relabelling the per-row checkboxes breaks that test.
- Delivery dates are shown through formatDate() but SORTED and SEARCHED on the raw ISO string (materialSortKey 'delivery' compares a.deliveryDate.localeCompare, and the search haystack includes material.deliveryDate raw). A redesign that formats earlier in the pipeline will silently change both sort order and search hits. Also note the sentinel value 'Pending' passes through formatDate untouched.
- The Crews table's Equipment and Current-job columns are computed with fuzzy string matching (equipmentForCrewJob does substring matching between job.requiredEquipment and equipment name/type; activeAssignmentForCrew picks the earliest non-'DelayIQed' assignment). These values are guesses, not joins — presenting them more prominently would overstate their reliability.
- Both marketing product pages (#materials-readiness, #equipment-tracking) share the .cs-page/.wx-footer chassis with five sibling product pages, so their CSS overlaps the landing area's ownership. Coordinate before touching crew-scheduling-redesign.css shared classes. Their materials-readiness-redesign.css and equipment-tracking-redesign.css files are the only page-specific parts (teal + MatRing / amber + eq-mix).
- The 'Filter' chip both displays the active count and acts as the clear-all button, with the meaning conveyed only through a title attribute ('Clear filters' vs 'Use the filters below'). That is an accessibility and comprehension problem worth fixing in the redesign.
- Pagination renders one button per page with no ellipsis (Array.from({length: pageCount})), so a workspace with hundreds of records produces a page-button flood.
- Three copies of the exact same ~230-line index scaffolding (state hooks, filter/sort/paging/selection/export helpers) live inline in App.tsx at 34872, 35701 and 36449, and three more elsewhere for Projects/Field Updates. Any structural redesign that is not factored into a shared component will have to be made six times.

- @keyframes dx-pulse (2.6s ease-in-out infinite) on .dx-dot eyebrow dot — opacity 1 -> .35

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- The .hs-index system is SHARED between Field Updates and DelayIQs (and Projects / Crews / Equipment / Materials / Contacts). hs-index.css owns .hs-kpis/.hs-kpi/.hs-kpi-ico(tone-blue|green|violet|amber|red)/.hs-index-grid/.hs-index-main/.hs-index-rail/.hs-index-card/.hs-index-head/.hs-index-title/.hs-index-actions/.hs-btn(.hs-btn-primary)/.hs-views/.hs-view/.hs-view-count/.hs-toolbar/.hs-search/.hs-chip/.hs-toolbar-right/.hs-quickfilters/.hs-qf/.hs-qf-link/.hs-table-wrap/.hs-table/.hs-cell-check/.hs-cell-name/.hs-cell-muted/.hs-cell-wrap/.hs-cell-num/.hs-cell-actions/.hs-row-name/.hs-avatar/.hs-link/.hs-name/.hs-row-sub/.hs-badge/.hs-progress/.hs-progress-track/.hs-thumbs/.hs-row-action/.hs-empty/.hs-index-foot/.hs-count-pill/.hs-pagination/.hs-page-btn/.hs-perpage. Restyling any of it hits SIX pages at once, not two.
- Field Updates uses ONLY hs-index-main (single column); DelayIQs uses hs-index-grid + hs-index-rail (two columns). Both pages otherwise share the identical KPI-strip + index-card + footer skeleton.
- The per-page rx wrappers .field-rx and .delayIQ-rx are near-identical clones: the same --wx-* token block, the same negative margin -22px -28px -34px (they bleed out of the shell padding), the same overflow:clip + isolation:isolate, the same .dx-bg/.dx-aurora-1..3/.dx-cursor markup, the same dx-pulse keyframe and the same [data-reveal]/[data-reveal-stagger] ladder. Two files duplicate ~200 lines of it.
- isolation:isolate on .field-rx is the reason the edit dialog is portalled to document.body — any fixed overlay authored inside the page would be trapped in its stacking context. Same trap applies to anything a redesign adds.
- Both index pages carry the SAME hand-rolled CSV export pattern (build a quoted-cell CSV string, Blob, URL.createObjectURL, synthetic <a download>.click(), revokeObjectURL) — buildflow-field-updates.csv and buildflow-delayiqs.csv — and they export the FILTERED set, not the page.
- Reports is the odd page out: no .rx wrapper, no aurora background, no useHudMotion, no reveal animation, and it is the only one of the three still on styles.css/redesign.css rather than a dedicated redesign stylesheet. It also gets its own shell class (reports-shell) and its own top-bar mode (reportsMode) with duplicate element ids.
- The field-progress loop spans FOUR surfaces and must stay coherent: (1) FieldUpdatesPage composer posts a percent -> (2) the .fp-raised banner tells the crew a variance was raised -> (3) the Schedule page .sv-drawer VarianceReviewCard shows the priced proposal with Accept/Reject -> (4) the Dashboard 'Pending Approvals' panel offers the same decision. A redesign that touches only one of the four splits the loop.
- The DelayIQ early-warning payload is rendered TWICE with different vocabulary: DelayEarlyWarning.tsx as a rich .diq-* card list on the DelayIQs page, and the Dashboard 'AI Recommendations' panel (App.tsx:26105/26574) as compressed .cc-rec rows. The Dashboard version has a 'Try again' retry; the DelayIQs version does not.
- There is a THIRD field-update surface: the Map & Field Ops page's 'Field Updates' panel with its own inline note composer (tests/map.test.tsx:164, styles .map-field-updates-panel). It shows reporter name, 'Crew Lead - Crew 2 - Riverside Office Building'-style role/job line, status and the note, and an 'Add Field Update' button that toggles a composer whose label becomes the save action.
- Status vocabulary is shared and inconsistent across the app: the Field Updates composer offers only 'On Site' / 'Ready to Start' / 'DelayIQed' / 'Complete', but the shared Status type and fieldUpdateProgress also handle 'In Progress', and the map test fixture uses 'Ready'. Any redesigned status chip must render values the composer cannot produce.
- 'DelayIQ' is a case-preserving rebrand of 'Delay' applied by perl across the codebase, which is why copy reads 'Inspection delayIQ', 'DelayIQed', 'that forecastIQs the project', 'Impact ForecastIQ' and 'Backlog ForecastIQ'. Rewriting labels risks either re-breaking or accidentally 'fixing' brand strings the tests assert on verbatim.
- Panel / ResourceRow / InlineEmptyState / Badge / PageTitle (App.tsx:26969-27027, 39026+) are shared primitives used by the DelayIQ rail and the Reports title; restyling them reaches every panel-based page.
- The 'spin' class + @keyframes spin live in styles.css:13647 and are used by DelayEarlyWarning's Loader2 icons; CloudLoader (quantum-cloud-loader) is used by the field dropzone AND the BuildFlow AI panel.
- Both marketing pages sit on the shared .cs-page product-page system (crew-scheduling-redesign.css) and re-implement the SAME pointer-tween + IntersectionObserver effects inline instead of using useHudMotion — three copies of that logic in the area.

The inventory records that the export exists and is filtered, but not what is in it.
- [ ] DelayIQ CSV export column set (App.tsx:38574-38592): ['Title','Description','Project','Category','Severity','Status','Impact days','Reported'] — includes the full Description (the table shows it only as a truncated .hs-row-sub) and the raw reportedAt. 'Impact days' as a header string is absent from the inventory.
- [ ] formatTime (App.tsx:39190) formats hour+minute ONLY: 'Posted' on every Field Updates row, and the edit dialog's 'Filed by <name> on <time>', print as e.g. '9:15 AM' with NO date, however old the report is — while sorting uses the full ISO createdAt. The inventory says 'posted time via formatTime' without the value set, which reads as a date+time.
- [ ] The complete fieldUpdateProgress fallback table (App.tsx:39063-39081), which the inventory truncates with an ellipsis: percentComplete when present, else Complete=100, 'On Site'/'In Progress'=55, 'DelayIQed'/'At Risk'=35, 'Ready to Start'/'Ready'/'Confirmed'=15, anything else=8. The 35 / 15 / 8 tiers and the extra Status values ('At Risk', 'Confirmed') matter because the CSV and the sort both use this number.

**Corrections** (5)

- Screen 10 (Reports) 'Report period' select + 'Export' button: correctly flagged as dead controls, but the missing half of the story is that the #production-reports marketing page SELLS exactly them — a 'Weekly review' mock with a '.pr-period' chip reading 'Last 6 Months' and a '.pr-export-btn' Download 'Export' (App.tsx:13348-13355), under the heading 'Export the weekly review in a click' and the copy 'Pick a period — last six months, last quarter, year to date — and export a clean production summary'. The two CSV exporters next door are the working model; a redesign that keeps the dead pair prominent keeps a promise the app does not deliver.
- Screen 0's Export description says the CSV is 'of the FILTERED rows' (true) but the inventory nowhere states that neither Export honours row SELECTION, and that the Reports page has no export at all despite being the page whose marketing promises one.
- Screen 5's note that the DelayIQs sort chip 'sorts by IMPACT even though its label prints the current key' is right; add that its .active styling is keyed off delaySortKey !== 'reported' while its chevron only rotates when delaySortKey === 'impact' (App.tsx:38489-38495) — so after sorting by Severity the chip reads 'Sort by severity', looks active, and points down.
- Screen 6 lists 'Fetch happens once on mount ... there is NO retry control' — worth pairing with the fact that the Dashboard mirror DOES have 'Try again', so the same failure is recoverable on Home and terminal on the DelayIQs page.
- keyLineRanges is accurate but two entries are worth widening for a redesign: 'Dashboard Pending Approvals panel' should also name railBodies.alerts (26538-26571) and railBodies.recommendations (26574-26625) as siblings in the same record, and 'page routing' should include App.tsx:613-615 (the two solution hashes) and 20402-20404/822-826 (ADD_ON_PAGE_LOCKS — confirmed: none of field/delayIQs/reports is add-on gated, so there is no locked state to design).

### Redesign risks in this area

- Reports 'Export' button has NO onClick and the 'Report period' select has NO onChange — both are decorative. A visual redesign will make two dead controls look more prominent and more trustworthy. Decide now whether to wire them (the two CSV exporters next door are the obvious model) or remove them.
- Reports mixes computed and fabricated data in one visual language: the six KPI cards are genuinely derived from data.jobs/crews/equipment/projects/timecards and carry honest 'basis' provenance lines, while both charts and all four Crew Efficiency rows are hardcoded demo arrays (plannedActualHours, backlogForecastIQ, crewEfficiency). If the redesign unifies the card and chart styling, invented numbers will read exactly as authoritative as real ones. App.test.tsx:1024 already forbids /Production Trend \(Backlog\)/ on the Dashboard for this reason.
- The 'basis' line is a deliberate anti-pattern fix: styles.css:16788 overrides .reports-kpi-card em to neutral grey 12.5px weight 500 precisely because the base rule is green weight 900 (it used to hold a fake '+3% vs Q1' trend). A redesign that re-derives KPI card CSS from scratch will silently turn every provenance note back into what looks like a positive delta.
- The em-dash '—' is load-bearing on Reports: it is how an empty workspace refuses to state a confident 0%. Any redesign that treats the value slot as always-numeric (big-number typography, sparkline pairing, a unit suffix) breaks that contract.
- Reports has no reveal/motion system at all while Field Updates and DelayIQs have a full aurora + stagger system. Giving Reports the same treatment means adding useHudMotion and a .reports-rx wrapper — and note that ScheduleStatusBand already emits data-reveal, which currently never receives .in on this page (it renders visible only because no .dx-ready class scopes the opacity:0 rule). Adding .dx-ready-style CSS without an observer would make the status band invisible.
- The DelayIQs page has no row interaction whatsoever: rows are not clickable, there is no edit dialog, no delete, and no way to change a delayIQ's severity, status, impactDays or category after creation. The create form only takes project + title and hardcodes category = tradeProfile.delayIQCategories[0], impactDays 2, severity 'Medium', status 'Open', description 'Logged from the delayIQ management hub.'. A redesign that makes rows look interactive (hover affordance, chevron, link styling) will promise editing that does not exist.
- submitDelayIQ (App.tsx:38234) has no try/catch, no pending state and no error surface — a failed POST is silent. The Field Updates composer next door has all three. Don't copy the DelayIQ panel's visual confidence without the states behind it.
- The DelayIQs 'Sort by <key>' chip prints delaySortKey but always calls toggleDelaySort('impact') — the label and the behaviour disagree. The Field Updates equivalent correctly toggles 'posted'. Preserve or fix deliberately; don't just re-skin the mismatch.
- The 'Impact ForecastIQ' chart reads data.delayIQs directly, so it ignores the index card's view tabs, search and quick filters, and truncates every label to 12 characters. Placing it visually adjacent to the filtered table in a redesign implies a linkage that isn't there.
- fieldUpdateProgress() falls back to a status-derived percent (Complete=100, On Site/In Progress=55, …) when no number was reported. The comment is explicit that the fallback is 'a reading of the status, not a measurement'. A redesign that makes the progress meter more prominent, adds a numeric axis, or colours it as a performance metric will present an inference as data. Consider a visual distinction between reported and inferred.
- MAX_FIELD_ATTACHMENTS = 8 and MAX_FIELD_ATTACHMENT_BYTES = 15MB are baked into user-facing copy ('You can attach up to 8 files per update.', 'larger than 15.0 MB and was skipped'), and images are silently downscaled to 1600px and re-encoded to JPEG q0.72. Photos are stored as data: URLs in the record, so a photo-heavy gallery redesign multiplies payload size on every bootstrap.
- FieldPhotoThumb renders THREE different things from one string field: a data:/http/blob image, a non-image file as a clickable FileText link, or a seed 'imageThemes' colour swatch for demo data. A redesigned photo strip must handle all three or seeded workspaces will show broken images.
- The two CSV exporters are the only working export in the area and they depend on synthetic <a>.click() plus URL.revokeObjectURL called immediately after click. This is fragile and will not survive being moved into a sandboxed/iframed context.
- Test coverage is lopsided. Field Updates is well pinned by exact strings: 'Add Field Update', the 'Field update views' tablist and its tab names (/^All updates/, /^On site/, /^Complete/), 'Search field updates', 'Filter field updates by reporter', 'Edit field update from <name>', 'Correct field update from <name>', 'No photos attached', the role=dialog named /^Correct this report/, and the labels 'Field update project' / 'Field update job' / 'Update' / 'Status'. Renaming any of those breaks tests/index-pages.test.tsx and App.test.tsx. DelayIQs and Reports have essentially NO assertions, so a regression there will be silent.
- The 'Add Field Update' label is used by BOTH the index card button and the composer submit button on the same page — App.test.tsx:604 relies on getAllByRole(...).at(-1) to pick the submit. Renaming one and not the other, or reordering the DOM, breaks that test.
- Every accept/reject aria-label is templated from the job's phase name ('Approve the <title> variance'); those labels are asserted verbatim in App.test.tsx:987/1032/1336.
- The 'field' page id sits in the rail group alongside 'map' and 'delayIQs' while 'reports' is alone in a 'reporting' group (App.tsx:681-682). Regrouping these pages in a redesigned navigation changes the flyout structure the landing/menu tests cover.
- Reports is the only page with a bespoke shell (reports-shell grid-template-columns 260px/72px + #f5f8fb background in styles.css, --hs-paper in app-shell-hubspot.css) and a bespoke top bar mode with duplicated element ids ('reports-notifications-panel', 'reports-account-menu'). App.test.tsx:623 asserts the reports username button. Collapsing that special case is a shell-level change, not a page-level one.
- The DelayIQ category list is trade-dependent (shared/src/tradeProfiles.ts, per business type read from localStorage) with a hardcoded six-item fallback. A redesign that gives categories fixed icons or fixed colours will break for any of the ~15 trade profiles whose category names differ.
- delayiq.css has no dark-mode or theme handling and hardcodes #ffffff plus var(--line, #e6e8ec) fallbacks; field-variance.css scopes .fp-* under .field-rx and .sv-* under .sched-rx, so moving the variance card to a new page (a Field Updates tab, say) leaves it unstyled.
- CSS pitfall recorded for this repo: a '*/' inside a CSS comment closes it early and silently drops the next rule, making tokens resolve empty. These five stylesheets are heavily commented in exactly that style.

- Pin drop: scale 0 & y -20 -> scale 1 & y 0, spring {stiffness:400, damping:20, delay:.3}; SVG teardrop filled with var(--lm-accent) + white center dot; drop-shadow glow via color-mix
- Grid pattern (20px path pattern, #14203a) animates opacity 0.05 -> 0 on expand, duration .3
- Job count fades out on expand (opacity 1 -> 0, .3)
- Coordinates line: AnimatePresence opacity/y/height (-10 -> 0, height 0 -> auto), duration .25
- Title x-slide on hover: spring {stiffness:400, damping:25}
- Accent rule: scaleX 0.3 <-> 1, originX 0, duration .4 ease-out
- Live chip: scale 1 -> 1.05 on hover, duration .2
- Hint: opacity + y 4->0, duration .2
- CSS: .lm-surface border-color/box-shadow 0.16s ease; @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) kills only those CSS transitions — the framer springs are NOT reduced-motion gated

### Map & Field Ops — "Route Optimization" panel (truck route planner + destination autocomplete + optimizer)

**Route:** page "map", left column bottom grid  
**Entry:** `App.tsx:29585 (Panel title="Route Optimization"); createTruckerRoute App.tsx:29127; helpers App.tsx:28497 createSavedMapRoutes, 28626 summarizeOptimizationPlan, 28659 geocodeAddress, 28723 searchAddressSuggestions, 28758 getFastestDrivingRoute`

Two coexisting route features in one panel: (1) a real trucker destination -> fastest driving route via OSRM with Nominatim autocomplete, and (2) a synthetic multi-stop optimization plan over the visible job sites. Both are persisted to localStorage and deliberately never clobber each other.

**Information displayed** (13)

- [ ] Panel action button reads "Optimize all routes" -> "Optimized" once a plan is saved; the action is omitted entirely when hasRouteData is false
- [ ] Trucker form: labeled field "Trucker destination", placeholder "Enter delivery address"
- [ ] Autocomplete dropdown (role=listbox, id trucker-destination-suggestions): up to 6 role=option rows, each a MapPin + a bold street line and an italic context line (e.g. "1 Old Ferry Road" / "Bristol, Rhode Island"), deduped by label|context
- [ ] Submit button text "Create Traffic Route" -> "Finding Route..." while loading (Route icon)
- [ ] Truck route result card (.trucker-route-result with a traffic-status class): header "Fastest truck route" with a Truck icon; a status Badge mapped Heavy->"At Risk", Moderate->"In Progress", Light->"Ready"; a definition list From / To / Drive Time / Distance; a footer line "<Light|Moderate|Heavy> traffic • live road route|estimated route"
- [ ] Origin label is the SELECTED job site's shortened name (shortMapLabel: "Office Building"->"Office Bldg", "Apartments"->"Apts"), falling back to "Austin Dispatch Yard" / "Austin, TX" / lat 30.2672 lng -97.7431
- [ ] Coexistence note (only when a plan is also saved): "Your optimized plan is saved underneath — clear this route to return to it."
- [ ] Optimizer stat block (.route-optimizer-grid.reference-route-optimizer): "Estimated total drive time" + the figure + "↓ <n>% <drive time|fuel burn|time & fuel> vs current routes"
- [ ] Optimizer definition list: First Stop / Last Stop / Total Distance (distance reads the literal "Pending" when there is no geometry)
- [ ] Goal control (role=group aria-label "Optimization goal"): three aria-pressed buttons Fastest Time / Least Fuel / Balanced. Profiles (App.tsx:28598): Fastest Time 33mph & 18% saved on "drive time"; Least Fuel 25mph & 15% on "fuel burn"; Balanced 29mph & 13% on "time & fuel" — so the goal genuinely changes the drive-time figure
- [ ] Distances are haversine * 1.28 road factor; formatRouteDistance shows 2dp under 10mi else 1dp; formatRouteDuration shows "<n> min" under an hour else "<h>h <mm>m"
- [ ] Traffic classification by average mph: <18 Heavy, <30 Moderate, else Light
- [ ] Plan geometry: up to 4 saved routes, one per ordered project pair, colored route-blue / route-green / route-orange / route-purple; single-project case draws one offset arc

**Actions supported** (11)

- [ ] Type >=3 chars in the destination field -> 280ms debounced Nominatim search (format jsonv2, addressdetails, countrycodes=us, limit 6); skipped when the field still holds an already-picked suggestion
- [ ] Focus the field with existing suggestions -> reopens the listbox; blur closes it after a 150ms grace
- [ ] ArrowDown / ArrowUp -> wrap-around move through the suggestion list (activeSuggestionIndex, aria-selected)
- [ ] Enter with an active suggestion -> selects it; Escape -> closes the list
- [ ] Mouse enter a suggestion -> becomes the active option; mousedown is preventDefault'd so the click lands before blur
- [ ] Click a suggestion -> fills the field with "<label>, <context>", clears the list and the error, and stores the picked point so submitting does NOT re-geocode
- [ ] Submit "Create Traffic Route" -> geocode (skipped for a picked suggestion) then OSRM /route/v1/driving with overview=full, geometries=geojson, alternatives=true; picks the lowest-duration alternative; compacts the polyline to 48 points; saves a `trucker-route-<ts>` SavedMapRoute (label "Truck route to <dest>", vehiclePoint at 35% along the polyline, stopPoint at the destination), force-enables Traffic, and stamps lastSynced. On any failure it falls back to estimatedDrivingRoute (haversine*1.28 at 26mph) tagged source "estimated".
- [ ] "Clear" (X) on the result card -> drops ONLY the trucker route from savedMapRoutes, clears the result/error/input/picked suggestion, stamps lastSynced; the optimization plan survives
- [ ] Click a goal chip -> setOptimizationGoal, live-recomputes drive time / savings / savings label
- [ ] "Optimize Routes" (Sparkles) and the panel's "Optimize all routes" action -> optimizeRoutes(): rebuilds plan routes from the visible projects + filtered jobs, KEEPS any trucker route, sets optimized=true, stamps lastSynced
- [ ] Persistence: a useEffect writes savedMapRoutes to localStorage key "buildflow:map-field-ops:saved-routes:v1" on every change; readSavedMapRoutes() rehydrates and normalizes on mount (drops routes with <2 points or an unknown class)

- [ ] submit button: "Create Traffic Route" (disabled while truckRouteLoading)
- [ ] 3 toggle buttons: Fastest Time / Least Fuel / Balanced
- [ ] button: "Optimize Routes"

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- Add-on gating is the front door to BOTH pages: ADD_ON_PAGE_LOCKS (App.tsx:822) locks map -> "map-field-ops" and timecard -> "time-cards"; isAddOnUnlocked checks selectedProductIds or a plan in ["business","enterprise"]. Any redesign must keep the page unmounted while locked — a test asserts "Job sites" is absent.
- Shared app components both pages lean on: Panel (App.tsx:26969 — section.panel + header h2 + one optional action button with aria-pressed), InlineEmptyState (App.tsx:27001 — icon + strong + em), Badge (App.tsx:39049 — span.badge with statusTone()), FieldPhotoThumb (App.tsx:37125), imageThemes gradients (App.tsx:872), formatTime (App.tsx:39190). Restyling .panel / .badge / .inline-empty-state touches many other pages.
- The map page hides the standard page header: `.map-ops-page .page-title, .map-page-tabs { display: none }` (styles.css:14924) while the JSX still renders neither — so the map is the only app page with no H1 and no visible title, and instead ends with its own marketing-style footer.
- styles.css contains THREE overlapping generations of .map-ops-page rules (~L3693-4600, ~L9142-11330, ~L14919-16800). Later blocks win by source order, and much of the earlier CSS targets markup that no longer exists.
- Large blocks of DEAD map CSS (no matching JSX anywhere in App.tsx): .map-primary-grid, .map-panel.live-map, .map-scale-layer, .map-city-label, .route-lines + .route-blue/.route-green/.route-orange/.route-purple/.route-traffic, .map-marker* (dot/label/status variants), .map-legend, .map-reference-stop*, .map-pin-kind, .map-pin-tag, .crew-pin.one/.two/.three, .map-route-card, .live-tracking-panel, .map-route-empty, .map-weather-editor, .map-page-tabs. The savedMapRoute geometry (points/vehiclePoint/stopPoint/className) is still computed and persisted but is never drawn — only its distance/duration/label are shown.
- Motion inventory for the whole area is small: framer-motion lives ONLY in components/ui/expand-map.tsx (the tilt, expand, road draw, building stagger, pin drop, count fade, coords slide, accent rule, live-chip scale, hint fade); CSS keyframes are exactly one — tcRowIn in timecard.css:644. Everything else is a hover/state transition. Neither page uses the data-reveal / data-reveal-stagger scroll-reveal convention (only the TimeCard *dashboard* section does).
- prefers-reduced-motion is honored in expand-map.css (kills the .lm-surface CSS transitions) and in map-field-ops-redesign.css (marketing), but NOT for the LocationMap framer springs and NOT anywhere in timecard.css.
- Third-party network calls from the map page (no API key, direct from the browser): Nominatim /search for autocomplete and geocoding, OSRM router.project-osrm.org for driving routes, api.zippopotam.us for ZIP -> city. Tests stub global fetch by URL substring, so a redesign must not change which host is called or the tests' stubbing breaks.
- localStorage: "buildflow:map-field-ops:saved-routes:v1" holds the saved routes (normalized on read, filtered to trucker + plan routes); "buildflow.selectedProducts" is the add-on unlock the tests write.
- TimeCard's data is entirely synthetic and deterministic: buildTimecardModel(_data) IGNORES the BootstrapPayload. Only IntegrationsTab reads real data (data.fieldUpdates.length, data.delayIQs.length). Constants that appear as UI copy: OVERTIME_MULTIPLIER 1.5, OVERTIME_THRESHOLD 8, BURDEN_RATE 0.31 (rendered as "31%").
- TimeCard is completely untested. There is no timecard test file; the tab switch, the approval chain advance, the OT clear, the audit-trail prepend and the export flip have zero regression protection.
- "ForecastIQ" and "DelayIQ" are the result of a case-preserving global rename, so the map page's weather feature is literally named "forecastIQ" in classes, copy, aria-labels and identifiers (e.g. "View full forecastIQ", "Add ForecastIQ", .map-local-forecastIQ-list, the recharts gradient id "tcForecastIQ"). Renaming any of it in a redesign changes user-visible copy.
- Dead / non-functional controls to decide about before redesigning: map footer Privacy Policy / Terms of Service / Help Center; "Travel Time Overview" action labelled "View details" that only re-stamps the sync time; the map's inline job editor which never saves; "Save Field Update" which only closes the composer; the TimeCard header "Export"; the 4 "Jobsite quick add" chips; "Generate WH-347"; "Statement of compliance"; the 4 payroll format chips (non-interactive spans).

### Omission check

**Verdict:** MOSTLY COMPLETE for the two page bodies — the panel-by-panel information and actions are accurate and unusually deep. Gaps are (a) everything that surrounds the pages: the tutorial coach-mark, the What's-new spotlight, the locked-state chrome in the rail/bookmarks, the Cmd+K palette entry, the Settings unlock card; (b) value sets and copy inside two TimeCard cards; (c) responsive states and internal scrollers, which are absent for BOTH pages; (d) two rendered-but-broken badge tones. 22 findings; none invalidate the existing 19 screens.
