**Corrections** (5)

- Today's Field Jobs avatar stack: the faces come from data.users (the workspace user list), sliced to Math.min(3, Math.max(1, (crew.size ?? 3) - 1)) — NOT from the crew's members, so the same 1-3 avatars repeat on every row and the count is crew.size-1 (capped at 3), with the '+n' chip = crew.size-3. The inventory's 'up to 3 user emoji avatars' hides both facts.
- The Cost-composition overtime pill reads '1.5×' with a multiplication sign (U+00D7), not '1.5x' — same class of detail as the '↓' and '·' the inventory pinned elsewhere.
- The Approve-OT audit detail is '<worker> · <n> hrs OT cleared for payroll' (worker-prefixed, hours via formatHours), not just '<n> hrs OT cleared for payroll'.
- 'TimeCard is completely untested' is right for the page, but the area is not entirely test-free outside tests/map.test.tsx: App.test.tsx:242 pins the tutorial lesson title 'Map & Field Ops lesson', and App.test.tsx:160-213 pins the onboarding product label 'Map & Field Ops' and the stored id 'map-field-ops'.
- The add-on gate is enforced in TWO places, not one: openAppPage (App.tsx:2445) and the setPage wrapper itself (App.tsx:2278, which calls setPageRaw). That is why the Dashboard's TimeCard widget — which is handed the raw-looking `setPage` — still raises the prompt; the inventory's claim is correct but the mechanism is worth recording, because extracting either page must keep going through the wrapper (setPageRaw is the only ungated setter).

### Redesign risks in this area

- Deleting or renaming the H2 "Job sites" breaks EVERY test in tests/map.test.tsx — openMap() awaits that heading as the page-ready signal, and the section's aria-label "Job sites" scopes most assertions.
- The site-card accessible name is load-bearing: tests query role=button named "Riverside Office Building, 2 jobs" / "…, 1 job". Changing the card to a real <button>, splitting the count out of aria-label, or altering the singular/plural breaks them.
- The sub-line format "<n> site|sites · <m> job|jobs in view" is asserted with a whitespace-tolerant regex /1 site · 2 jobs in\s*view/. The middot separator and the "in view" wording must survive.
- aria-expanded on the LocationMap card and the coordinate string "30.2672° N, 97.7431° W" (4 decimals, degree sign, N/S + E/W suffix from formatGeoCoordinates) are asserted on expand/collapse. Keeping the coordinates always visible would break the test.
- The filter <select>s are found by aria-label "Priority filter" / "Status filter" (built as `${label} filter` in MapFilterSelect). Swapping native selects for a custom listbox, or moving Status out from behind "More Filters", breaks tests — and the suggestion test deliberately scopes getAllByRole("option") to the listbox because the filter selects also emit options.
- The trucker input must stay role=combobox with aria-label "Trucker destination address", aria-expanded and a role=listbox with role=option children — three tests read that ARIA contract, including the exact option count.
- Exact strings pinned by tests: "Create Traffic Route", "Optimize Routes", "Optimized", "Fastest truck route", "Least Fuel", "Estimated total drive time", the /drive time vs current routes/ and /fuel burn vs current routes/ suffixes, "No route data yet", "No sites match these filters.", "Add Field Update", "Save Field Update", "Update note", and the full sentence "Your optimized plan is saved underneath — clear this route to return to it." (with its em dash).
- The optimizer's drive-time <strong> is read positionally: driveTimeLabel.parentElement.querySelector("strong"). Re-nesting the stat block so the label and figure are no longer siblings inside one parent breaks the goal-change assertion.
- The truck-route origin label is asserted as the SHORTENED site name "Riverside Office Bldg" (shortMapLabel). Showing the full project name breaks it.
- The trucker/plan coexistence rule is subtle and tested: optimizeRoutes keeps routes matching isTruckerRoute, createTruckerRoute keeps everything else, and the id prefixes "trucker-route-" / "saved-" (excluding "saved-reference-") are the ONLY discriminators. Any id-scheme change silently makes the two features clobber each other and drops the coexistence note.
- The field-update meta line is asserted verbatim including its hyphen separators: "Crew Lead - Crew 2 - Riverside Office Building". Switching to a middot or a different order breaks it.
- The add-on prompt is queried as role=dialog named "Get Map & Field Ops" with the close button named exactly "Close", and its pitch text /Live vehicle and equipment locations, traffic routing/ comes from ADD_ON_CATALOG. Restyling the dialog must preserve the accessible name, the Close label, and the pitch copy.
- The LocationMap card's framer heights are hardcoded pixel values (140 collapsed, 280 expanded) and the body is absolutely positioned inside them; any type-scale or padding change risks clipping, and the grid is a fixed repeat(auto-fill, minmax(248px, 1fr)) in expand-map.css.
- Six of the card's building blocks carry their fill alpha in a CSS custom property (--lm-fill) rather than opacity, precisely because framer animates opacity on mount — a redesign that moves them back to opacity will make them flash or vanish.
- The map's inline job editor writes to jobDrafts, and getJobDraft/getProjectDraft feed the filters, the site cards' status and the site accents. Reworking the editor into a real save path changes what the filters see mid-edit.
- redesign.css uses `border-radius: var(--r-md) !important` on .map-today-jobs-panel / .map-field-updates-panel / .map-weather-card — a new radius token will not take effect without editing that rule.
- TimeCard's tab state is a plain useState with no URL/hash persistence: any redesign that adds deep links or bookmarking has to introduce routing that does not exist today, and a reload always returns to Time Entry.
- TimeCard uses recharts (BarChart, LineChart, AreaChart, PieChart, sparkline) with hardcoded hex colors (#0a233a, #fb8500, #1568c9, #20b15a, #7cc39a, #6d45d8, grid #dde6ef, ticks #94a4b8) and hardcoded pixel heights (260/220/180/40) plus two fixed Y domains ([1200,1800] and [0,1.1]). Retokenizing the palette means editing TimeCard.tsx, not just CSS, and the fixed domains will clip if the seeded data changes.
- The timecard.css tone tokens are internally inconsistent: --tc-amber is #0b4ae8 (a blue) with --tc-amber-soft #dce5fd, so every 'amber' pill (OT approval, Overtime 1.5x, Apprentice, Conditional lien) currently renders BLUE. A redesign that fixes this changes the meaning of existing badges.
- TimeCard has zero tests, so a visual refactor there has no safety net — worth adding coverage for the tab switch and the approval chain before touching it.
- The 39,194-line App.tsx holds MapOpsPage (28981-29942) inline; extracting it during a redesign risks the concurrent-edit blank-preview failure mode noted in project memory, and `Map` is a lucide import in App.tsx so `new Map()` must be globalThis.Map inside that file.

**Route:** page === "deals", layout state 'board' (the default)

A seven-lane drag-and-drop deal pipeline inside the same index card, driven by @dnd-kit (DndContext + pointerWithin + DragOverlay). Dropping a card writes the new stage optimistically, PATCHes the deal, then reloads. Root: <div className="page-stack contacts-page deals-page hs-index">.

**Information displayed** (14)

- [ ] KPI 'Open pipeline' = currency sum of non-closed deals (Handshake, tone-blue)
- [ ] KPI 'Weighted pipeline' = sum of amount × stage probability / 100 over open deals (Gauge, tone-violet)
- [ ] KPI 'Closing this month' = '<count> · <currency>' of open deals whose close date is in the current month, or '0' (CalendarClock, tone-amber)
- [ ] KPI 'Closed won' = currency sum of Closed won deals (CircleDollarSign, tone-green)
- [ ] KPI 'Win rate' = won / (won + lost) as a percent, or '--' when nothing is closed (CheckCircle2, tone-teal)
- [ ] Title 'Deals' (h1#deals-index-title, data-tutorial-id=deals-page-title) with a purple 'Beta' pill
- [ ] Saved-view counts: All deals, My deals, Open deals, Closing this month, Won, Lost
- [ ] Board lanes, in order: Appointment scheduled (blue, 20%), Qualified to buy (teal, 40%), Presentation scheduled (violet, 60%), Decision maker bought-in (amber, 80%), Contract sent (orange, 90%), Closed won (green, 100%), Closed lost (red, 0%)
- [ ] Lane header: a tone dot, the stage name, and '<deal count> · <currency sum of that lane>'
- [ ] Lane aria-label '<stage> · <N> deals' (role=listitem inside role=list 'Deal pipeline')
- [ ] Card face: deal name (blue link button), the amount in large type, a meta row with the close label (CalendarClock + 'Closes in Nd' / 'Closes today' / 'Nd overdue' / 'Closed <date>' / 'No close date'), the company (Building2) and the contact (ContactRound), then a footer with a priority pill (Low/Medium/High) and the owner's initials (title = owner or 'No owner', '--' when none)
- [ ] Overdue close labels get .hs-cell-overdue (red)
- [ ] Drop hint in the footer: 'Drag a deal card to move it to another stage'
- [ ] Footer count pill '<N> deal/deals · <currency sum of the filtered set>' + ' · N selected'

**Actions supported** (17)

- [ ] Layout toggle (role=group 'Layout'): Kanban icon button (aria-pressed, title 'Board') and Table2 icon button (title 'Table') switch between the board and the table view
- [ ] Drag a card between lanes: PointerSensor with a 6px activation distance; useDraggable per card, useDroppable per lane keyed 'stage-<stage>'; on drop moveDeal() sets an optimistic stageOverride, marks the card 'landed' for 1200ms, PATCHes updateSalesDeal({stage}), reloads, then clears the override
- [ ] Card title button → opens DealRecordPanel
- [ ] Refresh (RotateCcw, title 'Refresh deals')
- [ ] Export (header Upload / footer Download) → buildflow-deals.csv of the filtered deals

- [ ] Saved-view tabs: All deals / My deals / Open deals / Closing this month / Won / Lost
- [ ] Search (aria-label 'Search deals', placeholder 'Search deal, company, contact, owner') → matches deal name, stage, owner, priority, company name, contact name and contact email
- [ ] Filter chip → clearFilters(); Sort chip → toggles direction
- [ ] Quick filter 'Deal owner' → all / No owner / each rep
- [ ] Quick filter 'Deal stage' → all / each of the seven stages
- [ ] Quick filter 'Close date' → any / This month / Next 30 days / Overdue
- [ ] Quick filter 'Priority' → all / Low / Medium / High
- [ ] Quick filter 'Company' → all / each company by id
- [ ] 'Advanced filters' / 'Clear filters' link
- [ ] Reacts to createSignal (Create new → Deal) and openRecordRequest (a contact's or company's deal)

- DealRecordPanel drawer
- Create / Edit Deal .pdx dialog
- Delete-deal .pdx-confirm

**Empty states** (5)

- Whole page (deals.length === 0): 'No deals yet' + 'Create your first deal to start tracking the pipeline.'
- 'Loading deals…' before the first fetch resolves
- 'Deals could not be loaded' + error + 'Try again'

- hsc-row-in 0.36s on every .hs-deal-card as it mounts
- .hs-deal-card.is-dragging: animation none, opacity 0.38, dashed blue border, grabbing cursor — the ghost left behind in the lane
- @keyframes hs-deal-lift 0.3s on .hs-deal-overlay (the DragOverlay card scales to 1.06 and rotates 1.8deg, settling at 1.03/1deg) with a deep double shadow
- @keyframes hs-deal-land 0.75s (delay 0.32s) on .is-landing — a blue ring pulse from scale .96 → 1.025 → 1
- DEAL_DROP_ANIMATION = { duration: 340, easing: cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) } passed to dnd-kit's DragOverlay dropAnimation
- @keyframes hs-dropslot-in 0.22s scaleY(0.6)→1 on .hs-board-dropslot ('Move to <stage short>' appears in the hovered foreign lane)
- .hs-board-col.is-over gets a blue border + 3px blue ring, and its header turns light blue
- .hs-deal-card:hover raises a 6px/16px shadow
- @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) disables the overlay lift, the landing pulse and the drop slot

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- All three pages read ONE endpoint: GET /api/sales/bootstrap (fetchSalesBootstrap, api.ts:896) returning { leads, tasks, activities, meetings?, companies?, deals? }. Contacts has its own inline loader; Companies and Deals share the useSalesData() hook (App.tsx:32143-32161). Contacts' loader is a duplicate of that hook — worth unifying but behaviorally identical.
- Mutations: POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/sales/leads[/:id], POST /api/sales/activities, POST/PATCH /api/sales/tasks[/:id], POST /api/sales/leads/:id/email, /text, /calls, /meetings, and POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/sales/companies[/:id] and /api/sales/deals[/:id] (api.ts:896-978).
- Email and SMS are real: sendContactEmail returns MailDelivery { ok, mode: log|ethereal|smtp, previewUrl? } and sendContactText returns SmsDelivery + { delivered, configured }. The record panel's copy changes per mode, so the redesign must keep three distinct notice tones (success / info / error) and an outbound preview link.
- Cross-page record linking: onOpenRecord(page, id) → openSalesRecord (App.tsx:2256) sets salesOpenRequest {page, id, nonce} and switches the page; each page has a useEffect that opens the matching drawer. A nonce is used so opening the same record twice still fires.
- Top bar 'Create new' (+) menu contributes Contact / Company / Deal items (App.tsx:20918-20920); choosing one navigates AND fires createRequest, so the target page opens with its create dialog already up (createSignal effect on each page).
- Every index page shares the identical control vocabulary from hs-index.css: .hs-kpis/.hs-kpi, .hs-index-card, .hs-index-head/.hs-index-title (+ .hs-page-tag), .hs-index-actions, .hs-views/.hs-view/.hs-view-count, .hs-toolbar/.hs-search/.hs-chip, .hs-quickfilters/.hs-qf/.hs-qf-link, .hs-table (+ .hs-cell-check/.hs-cell-name/.hs-row-name/.hs-avatar/.hs-link/.hs-row-sub/.hs-cell-muted/.hs-cell-num/.hs-badge/.hs-cell-actions/.hs-row-action), .hs-empty, .hs-index-foot/.hs-count-pill/.hs-pagination/.hs-page-btn/.hs-perpage/.hs-foot-right. Those same classes are used by Projects, Crews, Equipment, Materials and Field Updates — restyling hs-index.css touches five other areas.
- hs-contacts.css is scoped to .contacts-page — and Companies (companies-page) and Deals (deals-page) BOTH also carry the contacts-page class, so the page ground, the 5-across KPI grid and the entrance stagger are shared through it.
- The record drawer language (.hs-record*, .hs-timeline*, .hs-task-pill, .hs-record-assoc-grid, .hs-record-list) is defined unscoped in hs-contacts.css and reused by all three drawers.
- Tone vocabulary is string-keyed and spread over both CSS files: badges/avatars/timeline icons/board dots need blue, green, violet, amber, teal, slate, orange and red variants (LEAD_STATUS_TONE, DEAL_STAGE_META.tone, contactTone, CONTACT_ACTIVITY_META.tone).
- Both .pdx dialogs and .pdx-confirm come from project-dialog-redesign.css, shared with the Project and Crew dialogs — the sales forms only add .pdx-contact / .contact-form / .contact-form-wide / .pdx-save.pdx-danger overrides at hs-contacts.css:170-193.
- useModalDialog (App.tsx:22979) gives every dialog AND every record drawer Escape-to-close, a wrapping Tab focus trap, focus-on-first-field (it looks for '.pdx-form input, select, textarea'), and focus restore to the opener. Renaming .pdx-form would silently break the initial-focus rule.
- useHudMotion (useHudMotion.ts) is what turns data-reveal into .in; there is NO framer-motion in this area — every animation is CSS keyframes plus dnd-kit's own transforms.
- Row stagger relies on style={{ '--i': index }} written per row/tile/timeline item; the CSS delay is calc(0.025s * var(--i)) (rows) / 0.05s (tiles, timeline).
- CSV export is client-side: exportContactsCsv inlines the blob logic in ContactsPage, while Companies and Deals use the shared downloadCsv() helper (App.tsx:32163-32171). Filenames: buildflow-contacts.csv, buildflow-companies.csv, buildflow-deals.csv. Exports always follow the FILTERED list, not the selection.
- Row selection (Set of ids) currently drives nothing but the footer count — there is no bulk-action bar on any of the three pages.
- Release pills: Contacts shows 'New' (UPDATE_ENTRIES v3.7 dated 2026-09-05, within NEW_TAG_DAYS=30), Companies and Deals show 'Beta' (BETA_PAGES, App.tsx:802).
- The ⌘K command palette lists Contacts / Companies / Deals as 'Pages' entries built from navItems (App.tsx:2607-2612).
- Pages can be bookmarked from the Sales rail flyout (the shared bookmarks system, App.tsx ~L690).

### Redesign risks in this area

- ZERO test coverage for this whole area. tests/index-pages.test.tsx pins Projects / Crews / Equipment / Materials / Field Updates on the SAME hs-index classes and copy patterns ('saved views, search and quick filters', row-link edit, row-action delete + confirm). A redesign that renames hs-index structure or the accessible names ('Select all X on this page', 'Open <name>', 'Edit <name>') will break those five suites even though no sales test exists.
- hs-index.css is shared by six areas — any token or structural change ripples into Projects, Crews, Equipment, Materials and Field Updates.
- hs-contacts.css keys the page ground off .contacts-page, a class Companies and Deals also carry. Renaming it (e.g. to .sales-page) must be done in three JSX class strings and ~30 CSS selectors at once, or the pages lose their background, the 5-column KPI grid and the entrance motion.
- The negative-margin page ground (.hs-shell .contacts-page { margin: -22px -28px -34px; padding: 22px 28px 34px; min-height: calc(100% + 56px) }) is hard-coded to the current app-shell content padding. Changing shell padding silently misaligns all three pages.
- The deal drag choreography is a three-part illusion: optimistic stageOverrides so dnd-kit's dropAnimation flies to the card's NEW position, the .is-dragging ghost left in the old lane, and the .is-landing pulse delayed 0.32s to start exactly when the 340ms drop animation ends. Changing any duration in isolation breaks the effect. Note also the comment on .hs-deal-card.is-dragging: the mount animation's `both` fill would pin opacity at 1, so `animation: none` there is load-bearing.
- Deal cards are draggable on the whole <article> (listeners spread on the element) while the title is a real button — the 6px PointerSensor activation distance is what keeps clicking the title from starting a drag. Making the whole card clickable, or lowering that distance, will make opening a deal unreliable.
- .hs-deal-card sets touch-action: none for dragging; the board strip itself scrolls horizontally, so touch behavior is delicate.
- Row actions are opacity:0 until tr:hover / :focus-visible, with an @media (hover: none) override. A redesign that always shows them changes row density; one that drops the hover:none override makes Edit/Delete unreachable on touch.
- Only the record DRAWERS and the .pdx dialogs are focus-trapped. The index pages' hover-only controls and the board's drag are keyboard-inaccessible today: there is no keyboard path to move a deal between stages (dnd-kit is configured with PointerSensor only, no KeyboardSensor) — a redesign should not advertise keyboard drag it does not have.
- The board branch never renders the 'No deals match that view' empty state — filters that match nothing leave seven empty lanes each reading 'Drop a deal here'. Easy to mistake for a bug and 'fix' in a way that removes the lanes users drag into.
- The Contacts page duplicates useSalesData inline instead of using the hook; refactoring during a visual pass risks changing its error copy ('Contacts could not be loaded.' vs 'Sales data could not be loaded.').
- Notice copy carries real operational meaning (smtp vs ethereal test inbox vs log-only, carrier-connected vs Messages hand-off). Shortening it in a redesign would make the app claim it sent something it did not.
- The 'Open in Mail app' / 'Open in Messages' affordances are plain anchors to mailto:/sms:, and sendText() may set window.location.href to an sms: URL. Any change to how these are rendered can break the un-configured-server fallback path.
- @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) blocks exist in both hs-contacts.css (two of them) and project-dialog-redesign.css; new keyframes must be added to those lists or the pages regress on accessibility.
- Per the project memory note: a `*/` inside a CSS comment closes it early and silently drops the next rule — both hs-*.css files are heavily commented.
- Sales tone classes are generated from data strings (`tone-${meta.tone}`, `p-${priority.toLowerCase()}`), so no CSS purge / rename tool can see them; a token rename must be done by hand in both the TS maps and the CSS.

- [ ] Per-tile: the page label from navItemByPage (e.g. 'Dashboard', 'Schedule', 'Gantt Chart', 'Month', 'Week', 'List', 'Kanban', 'Matrix', 'Projects', 'Crews', 'Contacts', 'Companies', 'Deals', 'TimeCard', 'Equipment', 'Materials', 'Field Updates', 'Map & Field Ops', 'DelayIQs', 'Reports'), single-line with ellipsis overflow
- [ ] Per-tile lock affordance: a CircleArrowUp icon (15px, --hsx-violet) when the page belongs to an add-on the workspace has not bought (ADD_ON_PAGE_LOCKS: map→map-field-ops, equipment→equipment-tracking, timecard→time-cards, gated by isAddOnUnlocked against selectedProductIds + selectedPlanId)
- [ ] Per-tile star state: filled amber (#e8a33d, svg fill:currentColor) when starred; the tile border turns amber-tinted rgba(240,179,84,0.55) via .bm-tile.is-starred
- [ ] Tooltips: 'Open <label>' on the tile body; 'Remove bookmark' / 'Bookmark for quick access' on the star
- [ ] aria-label on the star: 'Remove <label> from bookmarks' / 'Bookmark <label>'; aria-pressed reflects starred state

**Actions supported** (5)

- [ ] Click a tile body (.bm-tile-open) → open() → setPage(target) via openAppPage; if the page is a locked add-on it calls onRequestAddOn(productId) instead, which opens the 'Get <add-on>' prompt (setAddOnPrompt)
- [ ] Click a tile's star (.bm-tile-star) → onToggleBookmark(page) → useBookmarks.toggle → localStorage 'bf:nav:bookmarks:<userId>' rewritten; the tile disappears from this card immediately (starred groups are derived) and the top-bar star count updates
- [ ] Hover a tile → border darkens to #c9d0dc, shadow 0 6px 16px rgba(20,32,58,0.10), translateY(-1px)
- [ ] Hover a star → background --hsx-hover, icon → --hsx-blue
- [ ] No search, no filter, no sort, no pagination, no bulk select, no export on this page — it is the only .hs-index page without the toolbar/footer chrome

**Opens (modals, drawers, popovers)** (1)

- Add-on upsell prompt (setAddOnPrompt) when a locked page tile is opened — shows the add-on title, price ($12 / $9 / $8 per user/month), included plans and pitch from ADD_ON_CATALOG (App.tsx:828)

**Empty states** (2)

- When zero pages are starred AND zero Schedule views are pinned: .bm-empty — a 22px amber Star icon, strong 'No bookmarks yet', then 'Star any page below, or hover a category in the sidebar and use the star there. Bookmarks show up in the star menu at the top of every screen.' Dashed 1px --hsx-line border, 12px radius, centered, max-width 460px on the body copy
- QUIRK: when zero pages are starred but at least one Schedule view IS pinned, the branch returns null — neither the groups nor the empty block renders, so the card shows only its title/count and the Schedule-views tiles (App.tsx:20472 `: links.length > 0 ? null :`)

**Loading states** (1)

- None local. The page only renders after the app bootstrap resolves (App-level loading/error screens own that); bookmarks themselves are read synchronously from localStorage in useState initialiser

**Error states** (1)

- None surfaced. readBookmarks() swallows JSON/localStorage throws and returns []; the toggle's localStorage.setItem is wrapped in try/catch with the comment 'private mode: the stars just do not persist' — a private-window user silently loses persistence with no notice

**Animations and transitions** (5)

- @keyframes bm-rise (bookmarks-page.css:64) — every .bm-tile fades in from opacity 0 / translateY(8px) over 0.4s with --hsx-ease cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), `both` fill. NOTE: it is not staggered and it replays on every render pass that remounts tiles
- Tile hover transition: border-color 0.16s ease, box-shadow 0.16s ease, transform 0.16s var(--hsx-ease)
- Star hover transition: color 0.16s ease, background 0.16s ease
- @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) kills bm-rise, the tile transition and the hover translate (bookmarks-page.css:167)
- This page does NOT use useHudMotion / [data-reveal] / dx-bg auroras — unlike Projects, Crews, Equipment, Materials, Field Updates and Contacts, it has no scroll-reveal and no cursor-parallax background

### Shared index-page chrome (.hs-index) — the HubSpot index pattern

**Route:** Applied by 10 pages: Bookmarks (App.tsx:20445), Projects (27700), Contacts (30430), Companies (32510), Deals (33747), Crews (35126), Equipment (35943), Materials (36652), Field Updates (37488), DelayIQs (38372). Projects is the fullest instance and is the archetype described here.  
**Entry:** `hs-index.css:1 (the sheet); archetype markup App.tsx:27700-28180`

One reusable index-page language — KPI strip, white index card, saved-view tabs, search/filter/sort toolbar, quick-filter dropdowns, a checkbox table, and a pagination/count/export footer — so every record list reads the same.

**Information displayed** (19)

- [ ] Token block on .hs-index (hs-index.css:11): --hsx-sans (Inter stack), --hsx-ink #14203a, --hsx-text #1c1c1a, --hsx-mut #575550, --hsx-faint #8a877e, --hsx-line #e6e8f0, --hsx-line-soft #eef0f4, --hsx-card #fff, --hsx-paper #f5f6fa, --hsx-hover #f6f8fc, --hsx-blue #2f6bff, --hsx-blue-soft #e8f0fe, --hsx-green #188038 / soft #e2f1e6, --hsx-amber #b45309 / soft #fdf0dc, --hsx-red #c5221f / soft #fbe4e2, --hsx-violet #6d28d9 / soft #efe8f8, --hsx-ease cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)
- [ ] KPI strip .hs-kpis / .hs-kpi: auto-fit minmax(170px,1fr); each card = a 34×34 tinted icon square (.hs-kpi-ico tone-blue|green|amber|red|violet|orange), a 11.5px muted label (.hs-kpi-label), a 20px 750-weight tabular-nums value (.hs-kpi-value, with an optional 12px <small> unit), and a 11.5px faint note (.hs-kpi-note) that on Projects prints '<delta> <note>'
- [ ] Page grid .hs-index-grid = minmax(0,1fr) + a 330px sticky rail (top:74px); collapses to one column under 1240px. Used only by Projects and DelayIQs; the other eight pages use the bare .hs-index-main single column
- [ ] Index card .hs-index-card: 1px --hsx-line, 14px radius, white, padding 18/22/16, shadow 0 1px 2px rgba(20,32,58,0.04)
- [ ] Card head .hs-index-head: .hs-index-title h1 (22px, 650, -0.015em, --hsx-ink) + a 26px square ChevronDown button that resets the saved view to 'all' (present on all 9 record pages, aria-label 'Show all <things>'; ABSENT on Bookmarks) + .hs-index-actions on the right
- [ ] Release pill .hs-page-tag styled ONLY as `.hs-index .hs-index-title .hs-page-tag` — 11px uppercase, 999px radius, blue #2f6bff, or .beta violet #7c3aed
- [ ] Buttons: .hs-btn (36px min-height, 8px radius, white, 13.5px/600, 1px --hsx-line), .hs-btn-primary (blue fill + shadow 0 6px 16px rgba(47,107,255,0.28), hover #245ae0), .hs-btn-icon (36px square, muted, .active = blue-soft + blue border), :disabled opacity .55
- [ ] Saved-view tabs .hs-views (role=tablist, bottom-bordered, horizontally scrollable) / .hs-view (role=tab, aria-selected, 13.5px/600, 2px transparent bottom border → blue when .active) / .hs-view-count (999px pill, line-soft → blue-soft when active). Tab sets in use: Projects 'All projects / Active / At risk / Completed'; Contacts 'All contacts / My contacts / Unassigned contacts / Open leads / Customers'; Companies 'All companies / My companies / Unassigned / With open deals / Customers'; Deals 'All deals / My deals / Open deals / Closing this month / Won / Lost'; Crews 'All crews / Available / On job / Overbooked'; Equipment 'All equipment / Available / In use / Maintenance'; Materials 'All materials / Ready / Ordered / Waiting on delivery'; Field Updates 'All updates / On site / Ready to start / DelayIQed / Complete'
- [ ] Toolbar .hs-toolbar: .hs-search (999px pill, min 280px, magnifier + input, :focus-within blue border + 3px rgba(47,107,255,0.14) ring, styled kbd slot that no index page actually renders), .hs-chip pills for 'Filter · <n>' and 'Sort by <key>' (.active = blue-soft), and .hs-toolbar-right holding a muted '<filtered> of <total>' count
- [ ] Quick filters .hs-quickfilters: borderless .hs-qf select pills with an absolutely-positioned ChevronDown, .is-set turning the label blue; then a .hs-qf-link that reads 'Clear filters' when any filter is set and 'Advanced filters' when none is. Projects' four are Status, Project manager, Schedule health (On Track / Monitor / At Risk / Complete), Type
- [ ] Table .hs-table-wrap (overflow-x auto, 10px radius, bordered) → .hs-table (min-width 720px, separate borders, 46px rows, nowrap cells, sticky #fafbfd thead at 42px)
- [ ] Sortable header helper (App.tsx:27690 sortHeader): a <th> that gets .sorted and holds a button with the label + a ChevronDown rotated 180° for desc; .sorted button svg goes full-opacity blue
- [ ] Cell primitives: .hs-cell-check (44px, 16px checkbox, accent-color blue), .hs-cell-name (min 240px) with .hs-row-name → .hs-avatar (30px circle, initials, tone-green|amber|red|violet) + .hs-link (blue 700 button, underline on hover) + .hs-row-sub (12px faint meta, max 340px, ellipsised), .hs-cell-muted (13px --hsx-mut), .hs-cell-num (tabular-nums 600 ink), .hs-cell-wrap (wrapping 260–420px), .hs-name (13.5px/700 ink), .hs-thumbs (28px photo/file chips)
- [ ] Status badge .hs-badge: 999px pill with a 6px currentColor dot ::before, 11.5px/700, tones green/amber/red/blue/violet (+ tone-teal and tone-slate added by hs-contacts.css)
- [ ] Progress cell .hs-progress: 6px track (.hs-progress-track, tone-amber/red/green swap the gradient; default gradient #4285f4→#9b72cb) plus a bold tabular-nums percentage
- [ ] Forecast delta pill .hs-delta.ahead (green-soft) / .behind (red-soft) printing ±Nd
- [ ] Row hover state (background --hsx-hover) and .is-selected row state (#f2f6ff)
- [ ] Footer .hs-index-foot (1fr auto 1fr): .hs-count-pill on the left ('<N> projects · <M> selected'), .hs-pagination in the middle (Prev / numbered .hs-page-btn with aria-current="page" / Next / a .hs-qf.hs-perpage select of 10 · 25 · 50 per page), and .hs-foot-right holding the Export button
- [ ] Rail panels .hs-panel / .hs-panel-head h2 / .hs-panel-link (blue text button) — on Projects the three rails are 'DelayIQs' → DelayIQs page, a schedule panel → Schedule page, and a reports panel → Reports page

**Actions supported** (14)

- [ ] Click a saved-view tab → sets the page's view state and resets the page number to 1
- [ ] Click the title ChevronDown → resets the view to 'all'
- [ ] Type in .hs-search → filters and resets to page 1
- [ ] Click the 'Filter' chip → clears all filters (when any are set) or is a no-op pointer to the quick-filter row
- [ ] Click the 'Sort by <key>' chip → toggleSort(key) (also asc/desc toggle from any sortable column header)
- [ ] Change any .hs-qf select → applies that quick filter and resets to page 1
- [ ] Click 'Clear filters' / 'Advanced filters' link → clears every filter
- [ ] Header checkbox 'Select all <things> on this page' → toggleAllRows; per-row 'Select <name>' → toggleRow (drives the '· N selected' suffix)
- [ ] Click a row's name .hs-link → opens the record editor dialog (aria-label 'Edit <name>') or, on Contacts/Companies/Deals, the record drawer
- [ ] Hover a row → .hs-row-action buttons fade in (opacity 0→1): a Trash2 delete (red hover) and, where present, an .edit variant (blue hover). @media (hover:none) pins them visible
- [ ] Prev / page number / Next → paginate; per-page select → changes page size and resets to page 1
- [ ] Export → builds a CSV client-side and triggers a download link (Projects: 'buildflow-projects.csv')
- [ ] Primary action button per page, e.g. 'Add project' (+ 'Import schedule' on Projects), 'Add Equipment', etc.
- [ ] Rail .hs-panel-link buttons navigate to another page

**Table columns** (2)

- [ ] Projects (the archetype): [checkbox] · Name (avatar + Edit link + MapPin location sub-line) · Status (Badge) · Schedule health (hs-badge + ±Nd hs-delta) · Progress (hs-progress bar + %) · Target completion (formatted date) · Forecast finish (Sparkles + date, '—' when absent) · Project manager · Type · Contract · Value (USD currency, '—' when absent) · Location (address || location) · [row actions]
- [ ] Sortable keys on Projects: name, status, health, progress, target, manager, type, value (Forecast finish, Contract and Location are NOT sortable)

**Charts** (1)

- [ ] No true chart in the shared chrome — the visual data marks are the .hs-progress bar (percent) and the .hs-delta ± pill; the KPI strip is figures only (no sparklines)

**Form inputs** (4)

- [ ] Search text input (aria-label 'Search <things>')
- [ ] Quick-filter <select>s (one per facet, each with an aria-label 'Filter <things> by <facet>')
- [ ] Per-page <select> (10 / 25 / 50, aria-label '<Things> per page')
- [ ] Select-all header checkbox + one checkbox per row

**Opens (modals, drawers, popovers)** (4)

- Record editor dialogs opened from the name link (ProjectEditorDialog and the per-page equivalents, styled by project-dialog-redesign.css .pdx)
- Delete-confirm dialogs opened from the row Trash2 action
- ScheduleImportDialog from Projects' 'Import schedule'
- Contacts/Companies/Deals record drawers (.hs-record, hs-contacts.css) with their own .hs-btn / .hs-badge overrides

**Empty states** (2)

- .hs-empty block (28px icon, 15px/700 title, 13px faint body, 44px vertical padding) used by all index pages, and it distinguishes 'nothing yet' from 'nothing matches': Projects prints 'No projects added yet' + 'Create your first project to start building the schedule.' when data.projects is empty, and 'No projects found' + 'Adjust the search or filters to see more projects.' when filters hide everything
- hs-contacts.css:162 styles an .hs-empty .hs-btn, so some empty states carry a call-to-action button

**Loading states** (1)

- None inside the chrome — no skeleton rows, no spinner, no shimmer. Index pages render only after the App-level bootstrap resolves (retryTransient backoff at App.tsx ~26949 covers the fetch)

**Error states** (1)

- None inside the chrome. Failures surface on the App-level data-error screen (styles.css:13621 comment 'Actions on the data-error screen. "Back to log in" is the escape hatch')

**Animations and transitions** (8)

- .hs-btn transition background/border-color/box-shadow 0.16s + transform 0.16s var(--hsx-ease)
- .hs-view transition color/border-color/background 0.15s ease; hover adds a 6px 6px 0 0 radius
- .hs-search :focus-within border + 3px ring, transitioned 0.16s
- .hs-chip background/border 0.16s ease
- tbody tr background 0.12s ease on hover
- .hs-row-action opacity/background/color/border-color 0.16s ease hover-reveal
- hs-index.css has NO prefers-reduced-motion guard and NO dark-mode block — every colour is a hardcoded light-theme hex
- The per-page reveal motion is NOT in hs-index.css: Projects/Crews/Equipment/Materials/Field Updates run useHudMotion (dx-ready + [data-reveal] + [data-reveal-stagger] + .dx-bg auroras + .dx-cursor), and Contacts fades .hs-kpis / .hs-index-main in via its own .in rules (hs-contacts.css:47-61)

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- Two independent bookmark stores, both localStorage and both per-user-per-device, never synced to the backend: page bookmarks at 'bf:nav:bookmarks:<userId>' (useBookmarks, App.tsx:705, plain useState — no cross-component event, so two mounted consumers can drift) and Schedule-view links at 'bf:nav:links:<userId>' (useLinkBookmarks, schedule/linkBookmarks.ts:92, kept in step by the 'bf:nav:links' CustomEvent).
- userId falls back to the literal string 'anon' when there is no active user (App.tsx:2436/2438), so a signed-out session writes bookmarks under bf:nav:bookmarks:anon.
- Three consumers of the same page-bookmark store must stay visually consistent: the rail flyout star (.hs-flyout-star), the top-bar star menu (.hs-bookmarks-menu) and the Bookmarks page tiles (.bm-tile-star). All three use the same amber #e8a33d filled-star convention (and the top-bar trigger uses #f0b354).
- The --hsx-* index token block is DECLARED THREE TIMES with duplicated literal values: hs-index.css:11 on `.hs-index`, schedule.css:5217 on `.gantt, .gantt-menu` (comment: 'Same values as hs-index'), and expand-map.css:9. bookmarks-page.css consumes the tokens but declares none, so it only works because the Bookmarks page root carries the `hs-index` class.
- CSS load order in main.tsx: styles.css (1st) → redesign.css (2nd) → … → hs-index.css (49th) → bookmarks-page.css (57th) → app-shell-hubspot.css (61st, 'loads last so it wins'). redesign.css's own header comment claims it is 'Loaded LAST (after styles.css + overrides) so it wins at equal specificity' — that is now FALSE and its overrides lose to ~55 later sheets.
- The page catalogue is a single source of truth used by the rail, the flyouts, the star menu, the Bookmarks page tiles and the ⌘K palette: navItems (App.tsx:643, 21 pages), navHubs (App.tsx:673, 9 hubs), navItemByPage (App.tsx:726).
- Release pills come from one helper — pageReleaseTag()/PageReleaseTag (App.tsx:~800-815) driven by UPDATE_ENTRIES[].introduces + NEW_TAG_DAYS and BETA_PAGES — and are rendered in four places with three different class names: .hs-page-tag (index titles), .hs-flyout-tag (rail flyout), the hub aria-label/title, and the releaseTag prop the schedule pages accept.
- Add-on locking is cross-cutting through every navigation surface: ADD_ON_PAGE_LOCKS + ADD_ON_CATALOG + isAddOnUnlocked gate map / equipment / timecard, drawing a CircleArrowUp on the tile, the flyout row and openAppPage(), which diverts to the add-on prompt instead of navigating.
- The scroll-reveal convention is per-page, not shared: useHudMotion (useHudMotion.ts) adds .dx-ready then observes [data-reveal] and [data-reveal-stagger] at threshold 0.12 / rootMargin '0px 0px -5% 0px' and adds .in; under reduced motion or without IntersectionObserver it adds .in to everything immediately. Each page's own sheet declares the opacity:0 start state, so a page that forgets the rule gets no animation and a page whose className is computed dynamically loses the imperative .in class.
- Light theme only. Nothing in this area has a dark-mode block; hs-index.css, bookmarks-page.css and redesign.css are all hardcoded light hexes.
- styles.css (16,793 lines) is still the base sheet and still governs: the :root token set and the reset (box-sizing, body min-width 320px, button cursor/:disabled, font inheritance); the whole marketing/welcome site (.welcome-page, .welcome-nav, .welcome-mega-menu, .product-menu-*, plans toggle, startup/FAQ/roadmap blocks); onboarding/account (.account-*); the app shell (.app-shell + its reports-shell/settings-shell variants, .sidebar, .topbar, .search-box, .main-panel/.content-scroll); the shared page primitives listed above (.page-stack, .page-title, .kpi-grid/.kpi-card, .panel/.panel-header, .badge, .empty-state, .inline-empty-state, .table-head/.table-row, .resource-row/.resource-card, .legend-list, .panel-note, .data-table, .progress-line, .project-thumb); the dashboard feed panel; the notification/support-chat popovers; the demo/kanban marketing mocks; the data-error screen; and by far the largest single block, the legacy Map & Field Ops page (137 .map-ops-page rules plus .map-marker/.map-city-label/.map-legend/.map-route-card etc.).

### Redesign risks in this area

- findIndexCard() in tests/index-pages.test.tsx does `getByRole('heading', {level:1, name: /^<Page>/}).closest('section')`. A redesign that demotes the index h1 to an h2, moves the title out of the <section class=hs-index-card>, or prefixes it with anything breaks all 12 index-page tests at once.
- The Projects test pins exact ARIA strings the shared chrome generates: tablist name 'Project views', tab names starting 'All projects'/'Active'/'At risk', name links 'Edit <record>', row checkboxes 'Select <record>', the search label 'Search projects', the quick-filter labels 'Filter projects by schedule health' / 'Filter projects by manager', and the empty copy 'No projects found'. Renaming any of those in a redesign is a test break, not a cosmetic change.
- Zero tests render the Bookmarks page, the top-bar star menu or the rail star. The redesign can silently break all three; only the pure hooks (schedule/linkBookmarks.test.ts) are covered.
- The global focus ring is `:where(a, button, input, …):focus-visible` — the :where() zero-specificity trick means ANY authored focus rule beats it, and per the project's own memory note :where() is unreliable in jsdom, so tests cannot see it. It is also still ORANGE (--focus rgba(251,133,0,0.3)) against a product that is now entirely blue (--orange is literally defined as #2f6bff).
- ::selection and --shadow-accent are likewise still orange (rgba(251,133,0,…)) while .primary-button is a blue gradient — the 'refined' layer contradicts the current palette and a redesign must decide the accent once, in one place.
- redesign.css:295-341 uses `border-radius: var(--r-md) !important` across ~28 unrelated module card classes. Any new radius scale has to fight !important on a class list that spans crews, equipment, materials, field, reports, forecast, map, schedule and settings.
- .hs-page-tag is styled ONLY under `.hs-index .hs-index-title`. The same PageReleaseTag component is rendered by the Gantt/Week/Month/List/Kanban/Matrix schedule page frames, where no sheet styles it — a 'New'/'Beta' pill there renders as bare unstyled text. Verified: grep 'page-tag' across all 60 CSS files hits only hs-index.css.
- hs-index.css has no @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block at all, and neither does redesign.css. Only bookmarks-page.css guards its own animation. Any motion added to the shared index chrome inherits that gap.
- The Bookmarks page's .hs-index-title has no ChevronDown 'Show all' button while all nine record index pages do, and it alone omits the toolbar/footer chrome — so it reads as a different family of page even though it opts into .hs-index.
- Bookmarks page branch bug to preserve or fix deliberately: with 0 starred pages but >=1 pinned Schedule view, the first card renders neither the groups nor the .bm-empty block (App.tsx:20472 `: links.length > 0 ? null :`), leaving a title, a count line and the views tiles with no explanation.
- The top-bar star button's aria-label is 'Bookmarks (<pages only>)' while its visible badge counts pages + views — screen-reader and visual counts disagree.
- data-tutorial-id="bookmarks-page-title" (and contacts/companies/deals-page-title) are NOT members of the TutorialTargetId union (App.tsx:1519) — they are raw string attributes with no tutorial step pointing at them. They look load-bearing but are dead hooks; do not assume the tutorial depends on them, and do not assume it does not without grepping tests/tutorial.test.tsx.
- Dead CSS in the shared sheet that a redesign should not port blindly: .hs-view-add and .hs-qf-mini have zero markup consumers, and .hs-search kbd is styled but no index page renders a kbd inside the index search (only the top-bar .search-box does).
- .hs-index-grid + .hs-index-rail (the 330px sticky right rail) exist for only 2 of the 10 index pages (Projects, DelayIQs). Treating the rail as part of the shared pattern will change 8 pages that never had one.
- hs-contacts.css and schedule.css both reach into the shared chrome (.contacts-page .hs-kpi/.hs-table/.hs-empty .hs-btn, .gantt-page .hs-index-card/.hs-kpi/.hs-index-head, plus schedule-phone.css:293 `.hs-shell .content-scroll:has(.gantt-page.hs-index)`), so restyling hs-index.css has blast radius into Contacts, the Gantt page and the phone layout.
- The Bookmarks page is not hash-routed (openAppPage strips the hash for non-schedule pages), so it cannot be deep-linked or bookmarked in the browser — an obvious redesign ask that would require touching pageFromHash() at App.tsx:~560-641.
- Badge tones are a hardcoded status-string allow-list in styles.css:12448-12492 keyed on statusTone() (lowercased, spaces→dashes). Any status not in one of the three lists falls through to the blue default with no visual warning — a redesign that reorganises status colour must re-derive that list rather than re-theming the classes.

- .settings-row hover: background var(--wx-bg) (0.18s)

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- SettingsToggle (App.tsx:22930) is the ONLY toggle primitive: a <button type=button aria-pressed> with a single <span> knob; class 'settings-toggle' / 'settings-toggle active'. 13 toggles use it.
- selectControl(label, options) (App.tsx:22693 area / App.tsx:22694) builds an UNCONTROLLED <select aria-label={label}> with no value/onChange — 17 selects across the static views therefore do not persist anything.
- actionButton(label) builds a <button className=settings-action-button> with NO onClick — 7 placeholder buttons (Manage, Upload, Import, Add file, Connect, Configure, Open, View log).
- renderSettingsSections() maps a SettingsSection[] to <section className=settings-section> with an h2 whose id is a slug of the section title, and one .settings-row per row (title <strong>, description <p>, control).
- Only 4 views carry a real API-backed 'feature' panel: profile (AccountSettingsPanel), general (WorkspaceSettingsPanel), workCalendar (WorkCalendarPanel), people (TeamSettingsPanel); billing carries two (SettingsBillingPanel + SettingsBillingPlans). The other 9 views are static rows.
- Form/typography primitives are shared with the onboarding/login flow via account-redesign.css: .acct-field, .acct-input, .acct-input-wrap, .acct-select, .acct-field-error, .acct-hint, .acct-error, .acct-success, .acct-primary, .acct-link-btn, .acct-sr-only, .acct-invite-rows, .acct-invite-row, .acct-invite-remove, .acct-invite-add, .business-context-verify. Restyling settings must not break onboarding, and vice versa.
- The Monthly/Yearly toggle CSS (.plans-billing*) lives in styles.css:4832-4886 and is shared with the public Plans page; settings-redesign.css:1265 only strips its centring margin.
- The legacy pre-reskin Settings styling (~133 .settings-* rules starting at styles.css:12686, navy + orange) is still in styles.css and is beaten purely on specificity by the .settings-rx prefix. Removing the .settings-rx wrapper would resurrect the old design.
- The app shell adds .settings-main-panel / .settings-content-scroll (styles.css:12678-12685) so the settings page owns full-height scroll instead of the normal content scroller.
- settings-redesign.css contains a whole profile-editor block that NOTHING renders: .settings-profile-section, .settings-avatar-edit, .settings-avatar-preview, .settings-avatar-actions, .settings-avatar-buttons, .settings-avatar-file, .settings-bio-field/.settings-bio-label/.settings-bio-count, .settings-profile-role, .settings-role-readonly, .settings-primary-action, .settings-workspace-line, .settings-invite-fields, .settings-invite-status. Only .settings-avatar-img is referenced from App.tsx (and only via an always-null profileImage state).
- settings-redesign.css declares `color-scheme: light` on .settings-rx specifically so native <select> popups stay light regardless of the OS theme — a redesign that removes it will get dark OS dropdowns.
- Reduced-motion is handled once, at settings-redesign.css:1126-1137 (kills sx-rise on the 4 staggered groups and freezes the aurora); it does NOT cover sx-plan-in, sx-addon-pulse or the framer PriceCounter tween.
- Responsive breakpoints: 900px collapses the two-pane grid to one column and turns the rail into a horizontal, scrollable strip; 560px stacks .settings-row / .settings-team-heading / .settings-workspace-line; 720px stacks the plan cards; 820px stacks the add-on grid; 640px collapses the holiday list; a 620px container query collapses .settings-invite-fields.
- APIs Settings talks to: GET /api/team, POST /api/team/invites, POST /api/team/invites/<id>/resend, DELETE /api/team/invites/<id>, PATCH /api/team/users/<id>, DELETE /api/team/users/<id>, GET /api/auth/me, PATCH /api/auth/account, PATCH /api/org, POST /api/business-profile, PUT /api/schedule/work-calendar, POST /api/billing/checkout, POST /api/billing/portal.
- Analytics events fired from Settings: EVENTS.invitesSent {count, held, source:'settings'} and EVENTS.checkoutStarted {plan, seats, source:'settings'}.

### Omission check

**Verdict:** INCOMPLETE — the screen list is right (all 14 SettingsView ids + shell + the 3 Billing parts are accounted for) and the per-row copy is close to exhaustive, but the pass missed a whole class of items: the shell's chrome removal, the only keyboard shortcut that works on the page, the per-status pill/tag colour value sets that live in account-redesign.css (not settings-redesign.css), the real default state of the Work calendar, the absence of any confirmation on the three destructive actions, the missing email-confirm action, and it mis-counts three of the four control primitives.

**Screens the first pass missed** (1)

- [ ] Settings shell — narrow (<=900px) layout is a materially different screen and no screen entry describes it: .settings-page collapses to one column, the rail goes position:static / flex-direction:row / flex-wrap:wrap, .settings-nav-groups becomes grid-auto-flow:column with overflow-x:auto (a horizontally scrolling strip of 4 labelled groups with NO scroll affordance), the account card loses its bottom rule, the AI button loses its top margin, and the panel padding drops to 34px / clamp(20px,5vw,44px) / 60px (settings-redesign.css:1080-1106). The close X stays position:absolute in the panel, which now starts below the whole rail.

**Information the first pass missed** (17)

- [ ] SHELL: while page === 'settings' the TopBar is not rendered at all (App.tsx:2809 `{page !== "settings" && (<TopBar …>)}`) AND the icon Sidebar is not rendered at all (App.tsx:2828). The shell class becomes `settings-shell`, and BOTH .app-shell.settings-shell (styles.css:7534) and .hs-shell.settings-shell .hs-body (app-shell-hubspot.css:44) collapse grid-template-columns to `minmax(0,1fr)` so no rail column exists. The inventory only notes the Ask-AI/Breeze suppression and the .settings-main-panel/.settings-content-scroll classes — it never says Settings replaces the entire app chrome. Consequence: the page has no global search, no notifications, no Create, no account menu, no page rail and no breadcrumb.
- [ ] BILLING PILL VALUE SET: .settings-status-pill is NOT a 'static blue pill'. It has four visual states driven by the data-status attribute on .settings-billing-panel, and they live in account-redesign.css (1796-1820), not settings-redesign.css: default grey (background #f0f1f4 / colour #47505f) for status 'free' and 'enterprise'; amber (rgba(224,162,60,.16) / #a8721b) for 'trial'; red (rgba(217,101,112,.16) / #b4404b) for 'trial_expired'; green (rgba(47,158,107,.14) / #1f8a58) for 'active'. 12px/700 weight, 0.02em tracking, 999px radius, margin-left 10px, vertical-align middle.

**Actions the first pass missed** (12)

- [ ] KEYBOARD SHORTCUT (the prompt's 'keyboard shortcuts' bucket, entirely absent from the inventory): Cmd+K / Ctrl+K opens the CommandPalette ON the Settings page. The listener is a bare window keydown registered unconditionally (App.tsx:2596-2606) and <CommandPalette> is rendered OUTSIDE the `page !== 'settings'` guard (App.tsx:2807). So the palette is the only keyboard exit and the only navigation affordance besides the X. Inside it: type to filter, ArrowUp/ArrowDown to move, Enter to run, Escape to close (components/CommandPalette.tsx). paletteCommands() contains every non-schedule nav page plus the schedule view commands — and NO 'Settings' command, so the palette can leave Settings but never open it.
- [ ] STALE DEEP LINK: leaving Settings via the palette calls openAppPage(), which does NOT clear settingsInitialView / settingsFocusAddOn (only closeSettingsPage() does, App.tsx:2724-2728). SettingsPage unmounts, so the next gear click remounts it on the stale initialView — e.g. Settings reopens on Billing with the add-on card pulsing instead of on Preferences.
- [ ] NO EXIT ONCE SCROLLED: the close X is position:absolute inside .settings-panel (not sticky/fixed), and the sticky rail contains no back/close control. On the long Billing view (status panel + two plan cards + four add-on cards + footnote) the only exit scrolls off screen; with the TopBar and Sidebar unmounted the person must scroll back up or know Cmd+K.
- [ ] MISSING EMAIL-CONFIRM ACTION: Settings surfaces the unverified-email blocker twice — the profile panel's '<email> is not confirmed yet.' and the People panel's 'Invites go out once you confirm your own email. New ones are held until then.' (plus a disabled Resend on every held invite) — but offers no way to resend or confirm. The only resend control is VerifyEmailBadge (App.tsx:7663-7687: aria-label 'Confirm <email>: resend the confirmation email', title 'Confirm <email> to unlock team invites and billing', labels Confirm email / Sending… / Sent / Try again, calls apiRequestEmailVerification), and it lives in the TopBar, which Settings unmounts. The .business-context-verify pattern already styles an inline action button (account-redesign.css:1609-1623, used by the Dashboard's .is-billing variant's 'Choose a plan') — the slot exists and is empty.
- [ ] NO CONFIRMATION ON ANY DESTRUCTIVE ACTION: the area's three destructive actions — Remove <name> (DELETE /api/team/users/<id>), Withdraw invite for <email> (DELETE /api/team/invites/<id>), and Remove <holiday> — all fire immediately on click. There is no window.confirm and no dialog anywhere in App.tsx 21400-22960, which is why every screen's `modals` field is empty. This contrasts with the .pdx remove-confirm dialogs used for Projects/Crews. There is also NO danger zone at all: no delete-workspace, no leave-workspace, no delete-account, no remove-a-real-teammate (the Trash2 renders only for user.isSample), and no change-password (AccountSettingsPanel edits name + email only).
- [ ] SILENT NO-OPS: clicking the last remaining weekday chip does nothing and says nothing (toggleDay returns current.workingDays when the set would empty); 'Add holiday' on a date already in the list silently REPLACES that entry (holidays.filter(h => h.date !== date) then append) with no warning; the '+ Add another' invite link simply disappears at 20 rows with no explanation.
- [ ] CROSS-WIRED DISABLE: every member's role <select> is `disabled={busy}` where busy is the INVITE-FORM busy flag — pressing 'Send invites' greys out the whole roster's role controls (App.tsx:21734).
- [ ] UNCONTROLLED SELECTS RESET ON NAVIGATION: .settings-panel-inner is keyed by activeSettingsView (App.tsx:22905), so switching category remounts the whole subtree. The 15 selects have neither value nor defaultValue, so any choice is lost and they snap back to their first option on every category switch — while the 14 toggles survive because their state lives in SettingsPage. Everything static resets completely when Settings is closed (SettingsPage unmounts with the page).
- [ ] EMPTY ACTION ROW: `(status === 'trial' || status === 'trial_expired' || status === 'active')` gates .settings-billing-actions, but every button inside is further gated on `paid` (currentPlan pro|business). A workspace on 'trial'/'trial_expired' with currentPlan free or enterprise renders the wrapper as an empty flex div (margin-top 16px, gap 12px 18px, account-redesign.css:1821) containing nothing.
- [ ] STICKY ERROR: TeamSettingsPanel.act() clears `notice` but never clears `error` (App.tsx:21663-21674), and load() only clears it on a successful GET — so a failed role change / remove / resend / revoke leaves a red role='alert' line sitting above subsequent green successes.
- [ ] EMPTY NOTICE: the invite notice is assembled from up to three clauses and joined; if a response carries only statuses other than sent/held/skipped, all three are falsy and setNotice('') renders an empty role='status' paragraph.
- [ ] changeBusinessType (App.tsx:2712-2715) already calls applyBusinessProfile + setData, and WorkspaceSettingsPanel then awaits reload() as well — 'Apply trade' does two full bootstrap round trips.

**Corrections** (7)

- '.settings-status-pill and .settings-owner-summary are static blue pills' (Billing part 1, animations) is wrong: the status pill has four data-status-driven colour variants (grey/amber/red/green) and the default is GREY, not blue.
- '17 uncontrolled selects' → 15. '13 toggles' → 14. '7 action buttons' → 8 (the list of 8 labels was right, the count was not). These numbers appear in crossCutting and again in risks.
- Work calendar default is not 'a six-day week' alone — it also carries 14 seeded holidays (this year + next year), which flips the disabled state of two of the three Add-year buttons and makes the documented empty state unreachable in practice.
- Holiday names: "New Year's Day" and 'Christmas Day' (not 'New Year' / 'Christmas'); the skip-set of four federal days was omitted.
- The responsive list credits 'a 620px container query collapses .settings-invite-fields', but .settings-invite-fields is one of the orphan classes nothing renders — the invite form actually lays out with .acct-invite-row from account-redesign.css. The container-type:inline-size on .settings-invite-form is live; the @container rule it feeds is dead.
- crossCutting says the app shell 'adds .settings-main-panel / .settings-content-scroll'. It also adds .settings-shell to the shell root, and the substantive effect is that TopBar and Sidebar are not rendered and both shell grids collapse to a single column.
- The route note for the shell ('page === "settings" … not a hash route') is right, but should add that openAppPage() pushes a history entry that CLEARS any marketing hash on the way in, and that category changes push no history at all — browser Back from Settings goes to whatever preceded the app page, not to the previous category.

### Redesign risks in this area

- The rail account card hardcodes 'Liam Santos' / 'Project Manager' (App.tsx:22864-22865) while the panel and rail label use data.activeUser — a redesign should wire it to the real user, but tests/settings.test.tsx deliberately signs in as Liam so the bug is invisible under test.
- tests/settings.test.tsx pins ALL 14 rail labels, the 4 group headings, each h1 title AND one h2 inside each panel. Renaming a category, a section heading, or moving a heading level breaks that single test 14 ways.
- App.test.tsx asserts the Preferences rail button has literal class 'active' (not just aria-current) — a redesign that switches to data-attributes or a different class name breaks it.
- Panel entrance animation depends on `key={activeSettingsView}` on .settings-panel-inner plus nth-child delays 1-6. A wrapper element, a different DOM order, or more than 6 top-level children silently loses the stagger.
- sx-rise uses fill-mode `backwards` on purpose so the finished state releases and hover transforms still work; switching to `both`/`forwards` would clobber the card hover lift.
- 17 uncontrolled selects and 13 local-only toggles look functional but persist nothing. A visual redesign that makes them look 'saved' (checkmarks, saved-state chips) would be actively misleading; they should keep looking inert or be wired up.
- 7 action buttons (Manage / Upload / Import / Add file / Connect / Configure / Open / View log) have no handlers — same caveat.
- Two rail controls target the same view ('BuildFlow AI' nav item + the bottom spotlight button) and the test asserts EXACTLY 2 aria-current='page' buttons for that view; dropping or duplicating either breaks it.
- The 'Default role' select offers Member/Admin/Visitor while the real roster roles are Project Manager/Superintendent/Crew Lead (TEAM_ROLE_OPTIONS) — inconsistent vocabulary that a redesign will surface.
- The Billing status pill, its paragraph and the action row are all switched on data.billingStatus ('free' | 'trial' | 'trial_expired' | 'active' | 'enterprise') — five states plus the derived trial-days copy. All five need to be re-checked visually; only 'trial' and 'free' are covered by a test.
- 'Switch to Free instead' uses a setTimeout(0) + applyPlanWith(next) workaround because the plan state has not flushed yet (App.tsx:22110-22114 / 22167). Refactoring the panel must preserve that fresh-value path.
- The billing plan CARD CTAs ('Downgrade to Pro', 'Manage plan', 'Contact sales') have no handlers, while the panel above has real Update plan / checkout / portal buttons. Two competing plan-change affordances sit in one view — a redesign risks making the dead ones look primary (the Business card's CTA is already the blue 'primary' one).
- SETTINGS_PLAN_CARDS hardcodes `current: true` on Business regardless of the org's actual plan, so the 'current' card highlight can contradict the status panel above it.
- Work calendar 'Discard changes'/'Save' both hinge on a JSON.stringify dirty check against normalizeWorkCalendar(data.workCalendar); reordering fields in the draft would make the panel permanently dirty.
- WorkCalendarPanel lives in schedule/ and is styled from settings-redesign.css (.settings-rx .wc-*) with hardcoded colour fallbacks (#dfe3ec, #e8f0fe, #1a3f9e, #188038, #fbe4e2, #c5221f) that bypass the token set — retokenising must catch these.
- The three .dx-aurora blobs use blur(50px) over up to 50vw — this was already tuned down once for paint performance (see the HUD paint-perf note); a redesign that enlarges or re-blurs them regresses scroll performance.
- Invite validation copy ('Enter a valid email address.', 'Already in the list.') and the joined invite notice string are asserted verbatim; the notice is assembled by joining up to three clauses with a space, which is fragile to re-wording.
- Settings suppresses the Ask-AI floating button and the Breeze assistant while open (App.tsx:2988-2996) — a redesign that renders Settings as a modal/drawer instead of a page must keep that suppression or the assistant will float over it.

### BuildFlow AI assistant panel (BreezeAssistant) — docked + expanded

**Route:** overlay on every in-app page except Settings (React portal to document.body); opened by the top-bar sparkle, the floating 'Ask AI' FAB, or a dashboard quick action  
**Entry:** `client/src/App.tsx:24707 (component) / App.tsx:2990 (mount) / App.tsx:25205 (createPortal JSX)`

HubSpot-Breeze-style AI chat embedded in the app. Answers from real Claude when the server has a credential (POST /api/ai/ask), otherwise from a large built-in grounded simulation over the live bootstrap payload. Also runs the photo/video schedule migration and voice input. Always mounted so the conversation survives closing the panel.

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- REAL vs NOT — what actually exists as UI: BuildFlow AI assistant panel (real, wired to POST /api/ai/ask with a large client-side fallback simulation); AI schedule import from photos/video (real, POST /api/ai/import-schedule + real createProject/createJob/assignJob writes); P6/MSP schedule import dialog with health check + ForecastIQ + confidence band (real, /api/import/schedule/preview|commit); DelayIQ early warning (real, /api/delayiq/early-warning + /notify); dashboard AI Recommendations (real, same endpoint); field variance proposal loop (real, /api/schedule/variances/{id}/accept|reject); CPM readout (real, computed client-side from @buildflow/shared); Schedule Status band forecast (real, /api/schedule/status); Settings → BuildFlow AI (real UI, but only cosmetic — no consumer reads the values).
- NON-EXISTENT as modules despite the naming convention: SequenceIQ, CrewIQ, RouteIQ, MaterialIQ, BidIQ, CostIQ — zero occurrences anywhere in the repo. Do not invent them.
- 'ForecastIQ' is NOT a module. There is no ForecastIQ page, panel or endpoint. The name exists only because a case-preserving perl rebrand replaced the word 'forecast' everywhere: shared/src/progress.ts:67 exports forecastIQFinish(), the import dialog has a ForecastIQPanel + 'ForecastIQ completion' heading, the variance card says 'ForecastIQ finish', and a great deal of unrelated marketing prose now reads 'the forecastIQ turns' / 'weather forecastIQs'. The only ForecastIQ-branded UI is: the import dialog's ForecastIQ panel, the variance card's 'ForecastIQ finish' metric, and the Schedule Status band's Sparkles 'Forecast finish'.
- 'DelayIQ' is BOTH a real module (the early-warning panel + server/src/delayiq.ts + the DelayIQ Detection marketing page) AND a rebrand of the plain word 'delay' (526 occurrences of the token 'delayIQ' in client/src, many of them in nouns like 'DelayIQed' status, 'log a delayIQ', 'Material delivery delayIQed', and even an animation data field named `delayIQ` in automationParticles). The DelayIQ index page itself belongs to the index-pages area; only its rail panel (DelayEarlyWarning) is inventoried here.
- Single AI entry point by design: the top-bar sparkle (.hs-ai-button), the floating 'Ask AI' FAB and dashboard quick actions all converge on the one always-mounted BreezeAssistant, which is suppressed entirely on the Settings page (App.tsx:2989/2993).
- Cross-surface bridge via module-level mutable globals: `assistantOpener` and `dashboardAiAsk` (App.tsx:19696-19700) let non-React callers open the panel and submit a question; BreezeAssistant registers them in an effect and clears them on unmount.
- Model naming is visible in the UI (Tools menu): Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Opus 4.8 — and the server defaults to `claude-opus-4-8` (server/src/ai.ts:18). A redesign must not silently drop or rename these strings.
- Demo vs live is a first-class product state: every AI call returns {mode:'live'|'demo'} and the client renders a built-in grounded answer/plan when Claude is not configured. The UI never tells the user which mode it is in.
- The whole AI story is honesty-constrained: DelayIQ early warning is explicitly read-only, the variance loop never moves dates on its own, and App.test.tsx has a hard assertion list that fabricated dashboard AI copy ('Lookahead Risk Scan', 'Active AI Workflows', 'Re-sequence drywall', 'Add 1 carpentry crew') must never come back.
- Motion vocabulary shared across AI surfaces: the quantum cloud loader (4 orbiting particles), TextShimmer sweep on 'Thinking…'/import steps, bfz-in / bfz-rise / bfz-pop / bfz-pulse in hs-breeze.css, sv-drawer-in for the variance drawer, and data-reveal / data-reveal-stagger everywhere else. Three of these have prefers-reduced-motion escapes (hs-breeze.css:872, quantum-cloud-loader.css:198, field-variance.css:296); TextShimmer's inline keyframes have NO reduced-motion guard.
- Iconography: Sparkles is the AI mark (top-bar button, panel mark, assistant bubbles, AI Recommendations heading, Schedule Status forecast, Settings rail). ShieldAlert marks the variance loop, TriangleAlert/AlertTriangle the DelayIQ severity, Gauge the field progress capture.
- Adjacent-but-not-AI (do not relabel): schedule/WeeklyDigest.tsx is a plan-vs-last-week diff emailer, not an AI feature; schedule/alerts.tsx and conflicts.ts are deterministic rule checks; components/CommandPalette.tsx has no AI entries.

**Information the first pass missed** (20)

- [ ] BreezeAssistant suggestion chips and Prompts library are CONFIG-DRIVEN PER TRADE, rendered in a loop: aiStartersFor(profile) = ['Switch from another scheduler', ...profile.aiStarters, 'Suggestions to optimize my week'] (App.tsx:24004-24006). shared/src/tradeProfiles.ts carries 14 trade profiles × 4 starters = 56 distinct prompt strings (Asphalt, Concrete, Roofing, General Contractor, Excavation, Utilities, Framing, Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, Masonry, Drywall, Landscaping, Painting), e.g. Concrete → 'Are we ready to pour tomorrow?' / 'Which pours are waiting on inspection?' / 'Is the pump booked for the slab?' / 'Any rebar packages still not released?'. The inventory mentions 'trade-specific AI starters' once and never names the mechanism, the count, or the fallback.
- [ ] GENERIC_AI_STARTERS (App.tsx:24002) is the no-trade fallback and is separate user-visible copy: "What's at risk this week?", "How's crew capacity?", 'Any material shortages?'. Also used at App.tsx:24260 as the suggestion set on the greeting/capabilities answer (sliced to 3).
- [ ] Each TradeProfile also carries `aiContext` — 'What the AI should know about running this trade before it answers' (tradeProfiles.ts:58-59) — sent with the question via askAi(question, readStoredBusinessType()), so the answer voice is trade-scoped. Not mentioned.

### Redesign risks in this area

- App.tsx is 39,194 lines and BreezeAssistant alone spans 24707-25598 (~890 lines) with a further ~500 lines of answer-engine data (AI_TOOLS, AI_FEATURE_HELP, buildOptimizationSuggestions, buildAiAnswer, buildScheduleImportPlan) at 24002-24700. Any restyle has to be done in place; extracting it risks breaking the module-level dashboardAiAsk/assistantOpener bridge.
- The assistant is a createPortal to document.body with position:fixed top:56px left:56px — it is geometrically coupled to the shell's 56px top bar and 56px icon rail (hs-breeze.css:16-18). Changing shell dimensions silently misaligns the panel.
- ai-film-redesign.css (897 lines) is dead: nothing renders .ai-film or .wx-demo-frame-film. It is still imported in main.tsx:31 and its comment claims it must load LAST. Deleting it is probably safe but should be verified rather than assumed; leaving it in place costs 897 lines of confusing precedent.
- The 'IQ' rebrand is textual and unreviewed. Hashes and ids carry it (#delayIQ-detection, id 'delayIQ-detection'), as do data fields (automationParticles' `delayIQ` property) and prose that now reads wrong ('the forecastIQ turns', 'weather forecastIQs', 'Material delivery delayIQed'). Fixing the copy during a redesign means touching route hashes and the landing-menu tests that pin them.
- Test-pinned exact copy that must survive verbatim: 'No jobs are trending behind. Nothing to recommend today.', 'No approvals waiting on you', 'Nothing has been resolved yet', the aria-labels 'Approve the {title} variance' / 'Reject the {title} variance' / 'View all early warnings' / 'View all approvals on the schedule page' / 'Ask BuildFlow AI' / 'Close schedule import', the Schedule AI page headings, and the settings triple ['BuildFlow AI','BuildFlow AI','AI assistance'].
- tests/settings.test.tsx:179 requires the Settings rail to have exactly two aria-current='page' controls for the BuildFlow AI category (the nav item plus the bottom .settings-ai-button). Consolidating those two buttons in a redesign breaks that test.
- The panel's thread auto-scroll deliberately type-checks `typeof threadRef.current?.scrollTo === 'function'` because jsdom lacks it — an effect that throws there unmounts the whole tree in tests. Any rewrite of the scroll behaviour must keep that guard.
- Attachment lifecycle is manual: object URLs are created per file and revoked on remove, on send, and in an unmount cleanup that reads attachmentsRef. Restructuring the composer risks leaking blob URLs or revoking a URL still needed by the base64 read in runImport (which must fetch the blob BEFORE the revoke).
- The import flow writes real data (createProject/createJob/assignJob in a loop) with partial-failure tolerance and no undo. Redesigning the confirmation UX must not make it easier to trigger accidentally — the isScheduleImportIntent regex already fires on loose phrasing like 'switching' + 'schedule'.
- Voice input depends on the vendor-prefixed Web Speech API and is feature-detected once via useMemo; the mic chip simply does not render when unsupported, so a redesigned composer must not reserve/assume that slot.
- The assistant hard-codes Claude model names in user-visible strings (Haiku 4.5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8) while the server default is claude-opus-4-8 — they can drift, and the Tools toggles are purely decorative (enabledTools is never sent to the server), which a redesign could easily make look functional.
- Settings → BuildFlow AI presents three controls of which only one has state and none has an effect. Making the panel look more capable without wiring it deepens the honesty gap the dashboard tests were written to close.
- ForecastIQ's confidence band (P10/P50/P80/P90 + on-time probability) is the most information-dense AI visual in the app and is only reachable after committing a real P6/MSP import — it is easy to miss when redesigning and has no fixture-driven page to preview it on.
- The AI marketing pages (Schedule AI, five automation pages, #ai-overview) overlap the landing/welcome area's ownership; the automation pages share one config-driven template and one stylesheet (weather-redesign.css, .wi-*) so a change to any one of them changes all five.
- Two #ai-overview module cards ('Readiness scoring', 'Recovery plans') and the assistant's post-import 'here's how I optimized the plan' bullets describe capabilities that do not exist as features — they are static copy. A redesign that gives them affordances would be inventing modules.

### App bootstrap: full-page loading screen, Dashboard skeleton, and the data-unavailable error screen

**Route:** any authenticated page (gate sits above the shell); the skeleton is dashboard-only  
**Entry:** `App.tsx:2765 (isLoading gate) / App.tsx:25601 (DashboardSkeleton) / App.tsx:2792 (error screen)`

The three states between 'user pressed enter the app' and 'the workspace is on screen'. Heading for the Dashboard the app paints the Dashboard's own shape; every other page falls back to a centred spinner. A failed bootstrap becomes a full-page error with two ways out.

**Information displayed** (8)

- [ ] Loading screen: Loader2 lucide icon spinning + the literal label 'Loading BuildFlow HUD'
- [ ] Dashboard skeleton: three greeting lines (widths 40% / 64% at 26px tall / 52%) standing in for eyebrow, greeting headline and the facts line
- [ ] Dashboard skeleton: one 128px-tall soft-blue strip standing in for the Schedule Status band
- [ ] Dashboard skeleton: one block per entry in DASH_LAYOUT_DEFAULT, each positioned on the real 6-column board grid (gridColumn x+1 / span w, gridRow y+1 / span h) so the skeleton is geometrically the same board
- [ ] Dashboard skeleton: three shimmer lines per block (40% / 80% / 64% width)
- [ ] Dashboard skeleton exposes role=status, aria-label='Loading your dashboard', aria-busy='true'
- [ ] Error screen: AlertTriangle icon + the server's error message, falling back to the literal 'BuildFlow data is unavailable.'
- [ ] Error screen reached when error is set, or data is null, or activeUser is null

**Actions supported** (3)

- [ ] Error screen → 'Try again' (primary-button) re-runs runBootstrap()
- [ ] Error screen → 'Back to log in' (.error-screen-back) calls returnToWelcome() — the deliberate escape hatch so a failed load is not a dead end
- [ ] No action on the loading screen or the skeleton (both are inert)

**Loading states** (5)

- .loading-screen (styles.css:13610) — grid, min-height 100vh, place-items center, background #f4f7fb, colour #173055, 12px gap
- .spin (styles.css:13649) — animation: spin 1s linear infinite; @keyframes spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg) } } — the app's ONLY spinner primitive
- .dash-skeleton (hs-home.css:2040-2073) — min-height 100vh; .dash-skel-board = 6-col grid, 40px auto-rows, 16px gap; .dash-skel-block = white card, 1px rgba(28,28,26,.07) border, 12px radius, 18px pad; .dash-skel-line = 12px tall, 6px radius, 3-stop linear-gradient at background-size 200% 100%
- @keyframes dash-skel-shimmer (hs-home.css:2068) — background-position 200% 0 → -200% 0 over 1.4s ease-in-out infinite
- retryTransient (App.tsx:39130) — invisible loading resilience: retries network failures and 5xx at 400ms / 900ms / 1600ms, never retries 4xx; wraps loadBootstrap and apiDemoLogin so a cold API costs a moment rather than the error screen

**Error states** (3)
