### Scroll-reveal engine — [data-reveal] / [data-reveal-stagger] / .dx-ready

**Route:** every command-center page: Dashboard, Projects, Crews, Equipment, Materials, Field updates, DelayIQs, Sales (contacts/companies/deals), Settings, Schedule landing  
**Entry:** `useHudMotion.ts:8 (shared hook) and App.tsx:25745-25811 (the Dashboard's own inlined copy, which adds a MutationObserver)`

The single scroll-in system for the whole app side. Elements marked [data-reveal] start hidden and get the class 'in' when they enter the viewport; [data-reveal-stagger] hides its children and releases them in a 40/80ms cascade. Progressive enhancement: the hidden start state only applies once the root has the class .dx-ready, so with JS off nothing is stuck invisible.

**Information displayed** (4)

- [ ] 270 [data-reveal] / [data-reveal-stagger] attribute usages inside App.tsx alone; 3 in schedule/page.tsx, 2 in schedule/pages/SchedulePage.tsx, 2 in schedule/ScheduleStatusBand.tsx, 1 in DelayEarlyWarning.tsx:165
- [ ] CSS rule counts per page stylesheet: dashboard-redesign 12, delayIQs-redesign 13, projects-redesign 13, crews-redesign 15, equipment-redesign 15, field-updates-redesign 15, materials-redesign 15, schedule.css 11, hs-home 1
- [ ] useHudMotion also writes cursor position onto the page root as CSS variables --mx / --my (px) and --px / --py (normalised -1..1), rAF-throttled on pointermove — consumed by the .dx-aurora parallax washes
- [ ] Consumers of useHudMotion: App.tsx:22379 (Settings), 27342, 30110 (Contacts), 32221, 33412 (Companies), 34874 (Deals), 35725 (Crews), 36472 (Equipment), 37256 (Field), 38226 (DelayIQs), schedule/page.tsx:593

**Actions supported** (1)

- [ ] None — driven entirely by IntersectionObserver { threshold: 0.12, rootMargin: '0px 0px -5% 0px' }; each target is unobserved once revealed (one-shot, never re-hides)

**Error states** (2)

- Known failure mode already fixed on the Dashboard only: panels that mount after their own fetch resolves (the Schedule Status band) miss the first querySelectorAll and would sit at opacity 0 forever — App.tsx:25798-25811 adds a MutationObserver on the root that observes new reveal targets as they arrive. useHudMotion.ts has NO such watcher, so late-mounting panels on Projects / Crews / Sales / Settings can still strand at opacity 0.
- Documented gotcha (memory note 'data-reveal needs static className'): a dynamic className on a [data-reveal] element wipes the imperatively-added .in class and the element goes back to opacity 0.

**Animations and transitions** (6)

- .dash-rx.dx-ready [data-reveal] — opacity 0 + translateY(28px) → transition opacity/transform 0.9s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), transition-delay calc(var(--i,0) * 90ms) [dashboard-redesign.css:103]
- .dash-rx.dx-ready [data-reveal-stagger] > * — opacity 0 + translateY(22px), 0.75s same curve; child delays 0.04 / 0.12 / 0.20 / 0.28 / 0.36 / 0.44s (nth-child 1-6) [dashboard-redesign.css:117-145]
- .sched-rx.dx-ready [data-reveal] — translateY(26px), 0.85s same curve, delay calc(var(--i,0) * 80ms); stagger children translateY(20px) 0.7s, delays 0.04/0.12/0.20/0.28 (only 4 defined) [schedule.css:749-782]
- .proj-rx / .crew-rx — translateY(28px) 0.9s; stagger children translateY(22px) 0.75s with delays 0.04→0.44 plus an nth-child(n+7) catch-all [projects-redesign.css:110-152, crews-redesign.css:98-149]
- .equip-rx / .mat-rx / .field-rx / .delayIQ-rx — same shape, 15 rules each
- Reduced motion: every page stylesheet clamps [data-reveal] and stagger children to transition-duration 0.3s (NOT 0) and clamps card hover transitions to 0.2s; the hook additionally adds .in to every target immediately when matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') matches or IntersectionObserver is undefined

**Pinned by tests** (2)

- test/setup.ts:57 stubs window.matchMedia to report matches:false so the non-reduced path is what tests exercise — any redesign that keys behaviour off matchMedia must keep working with this stub
- No test asserts on reveal classes directly; jsdom has no IntersectionObserver so the hook's reduce/undefined branch is what runs in tests (every reveal target is instantly .in)

**Entry:** `schedule/hooks.tsx:39 (useScheduleNotice) and schedule/hooks.tsx:56 (ScheduleNotice)`

There is NO toast system in this repo — the closest thing is this one inline status line under the board. Every drag, drawer save, re-book, sample-data action and digest send speaks through it, and most carry an Undo that reverses the write in one request.

The workspace is yours.', 'Digest emailed to N planners.', 'Could not send the digest: <reason>', 'Could not <what>: <reason>', '<name> back to <status>' (Kanban), '<job> back on <date>' (Month)

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- There is NO toast/snackbar/notification-queue system anywhere in the repo — grep for 'toast' across client/src returns zero hits in both TSX and CSS. Transient feedback is done three different ways: (1) the schedule's single inline .gantt-status strip with role=status aria-live=polite and a 4s/8s timer (schedule/hooks.tsx), (2) the Sales record drawer's coloured .hs-record-notice with tone-success/info/error, a 9s self-clear for non-errors and a manual X (App.tsx:31782), and (3) Settings' plain green .acct-success / .sx-addons-notice lines that clear when the next action starts. A redesign that introduces one real toast primitive would replace all three.
- Undo exists only on the schedule side, only through say(text, { undo }), and always as a single reversing request (rebookSchedule(inverse, { force: true }) or updateJob(id, was)). Nothing else in the app — no delete, no hide, no dismiss — offers undo.
- The house motion vocabulary is remarkably consistent: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) (220 uses, tokenised under six different names), entrances of 'opacity 0 + translateY(8–28px) → none' at 0.3–0.9s, and hovers at 0.15–0.2s. Drag has one grammar everywhere: lift with a spring overshoot + deep shadow, neighbours glide at 260ms, a dashed slot marks the target, and the dropped item fires a 0.75s expanding-blue-ring pulse (dash-land / hs-deal-land / hsg-land are the same animation at three scales).
- The 'eyebrow dot' pulse is declared eight separate times with an identical body: dx-pulse in dashboard-redesign / schedule / delayIQs / equipment / materials / field-updates / projects-redesign, crew-dx-pulse in crews-redesign, pdx-pulse in project-dialog-redesign (and wx-pulse / acct-dot-pulse on the welcome side). One shared token would remove ~8 duplicate keyframes.
- Empty states use FIVE unrelated visual languages: .hs-empty (icon + strong + span, 44px centred, index pages), .hs-home-empty / .cc-empty-line (small centred text + a pill button, dashboard), .schedule-empty-state (text only, no icon, no border, schedule boards), dashed-border slots (.sched-kan-empty, .hs-board-empty, .map-site-empty, .dashboard-feed-empty via redesign.css), and .empty-state / .inline-empty-state (legacy). Unifying them is the single highest-leverage empty-state change.
- Loading states are equally uneven: the Dashboard gets a real geometric skeleton, the Sales pages put 'Loading contacts…' inside the empty-state block, the schedule uses word labels ('Comparing snapshots…', 'Checking where the plan stands…'), the AI surfaces use the Quantum Cloud particle loader, and everything else uses one spinning lucide Loader2 with className='spin'. The six workspace index pages have no loading state at all because they render from already-loaded bootstrap data.
- Error+retry is implemented three times independently: the app-level error screen (Try again / Back to log in), .ss-strip.ss-failed (Retry), and the three Sales index errors (Try again with RotateCcw), plus the early-warning 'Try again' with RefreshCcw. Four different icons for the same affordance.
- retryTransient (App.tsx:39130) is invisible resilience worth preserving: 400/900/1600ms backoff on 5xx and network failures, never on 4xx. It only wraps loadBootstrap and apiDemoLogin — every other fetch in the app fails on the first attempt.
- Accessibility that must survive: role=status + aria-live=polite on the schedule notice, the dashboard's keyboard-drag announcer (.dash-board-live), the skeleton's role=status + aria-busy, aria-busy on every pending card, DashBlockBody's conditional role=region + aria-label + tabIndex driven by a ResizeObserver, and role=alert on every .form-error / .cc-appr-error / .sim-error / .sched-cpm-error.
- Every schedule surface carries a data-tutorial-id that the tutorial spotlight positions against (schedule-status-band, schedule-alerts, schedule-first-run, schedule-digest, matrix-grid, kanban-lanes, list-days, gantt-timeline, dashboard-production-context, tutorial-restart-button). schedule/pages.test.tsx:431 asserts every stop has its anchor on the page, so a redesign must move these attributes with the markup.
- Progressive-enhancement contract: the [data-reveal] hidden start state only applies under .dx-ready, added by JS. Two documented failure modes already bit this codebase — a dynamic className wiping the imperative .in class (memory: data-reveal-static-classname), and panels that mount after their own fetch never being observed (fixed on the Dashboard with a MutationObserver at App.tsx:25798, still unfixed in useHudMotion.ts).
- prefers-reduced-motion is handled by clamping rather than removing: the reveal transitions go to 0.3s and card transitions to 0.2s instead of 0. That is a deliberate, consistent choice worth keeping.

### Omission check

**Verdict:** INCOMPLETE — the motion catalogue and the notice/undo analysis are strong, but the inventory misses one whole page-level gate state (the paid add-on lock), the entire hover-reveal / focus-only control layer (12 index row actions + card deletes + panel handles), ~40 pieces of empty/zero-state copy on the Dashboard legacy panels, the Map page and Production Reports, the field-variance review card, the virtualization placeholders, the 1–6 keyboard shortcuts, and two large interactive motion families (DxTilt pointer tilt and the .dx-cursor / .dx-aurora parallax washes). Several counts are also wrong, including GANTT_ROW_CAP (300, stated as 200 twice).

### Redesign risks in this area

- Deleting a state string breaks a test. Literal copy pinned by assertions: 'No materials added yet', 'No projects added yet', 'No crews added yet', 'No equipment added yet', 'No jobs are trending behind. Nothing to recommend today.', 'No approvals waiting on you', "Schedule status couldn't load.", 'Drop a job here', and the accessible names 'Undo', 'Retry', 'Try again', 'Loading your dashboard'.
- The DashboardSkeleton mirrors the real board geometry by reading DASH_LAYOUT_DEFAULT and writing gridColumn/gridRow inline. Any change to the board's column count, row height or default layout silently desyncs the skeleton from the page it stands in for.
- recharts runs at its default animation (~1500ms bars/lines, ~400ms pie) with no isAnimationActive or animationDuration anywhere and no reduced-motion gate. Every chart in the redesign will animate unless this is set explicitly.
- components/ui/expand-map.tsx runs ~20 framer animations (springs, pathLength draws, six staggered building fades, a pin drop) that ignore prefers-reduced-motion entirely — expand-map.css:316 only kills a CSS transition. Same for TextShimmer's inline keyframe. These are the two real accessibility gaps in the motion layer.
- Motion the redesign must not silently drop because it carries meaning, not decoration: sched-pending (a write is in flight), sched-live-flash + the live pill (someone else changed this), dash-land / hs-deal-land / hsg-land (your drop landed HERE), tcRowIn (this row is the one you just added), hs-upd-pulse (the feature you asked to be shown), sx-addon-pulse (the deep-linked add-on), upd-target-flash (the deep-linked release entry).
- hs-index.css has zero keyframes and zero prefers-reduced-motion block, so the six workspace index tables have no entrance motion while the Sales contacts table does (hsc-row-in with a per-row 25ms stagger). The two families of index page already look different in motion; unifying them is a visible change.
- schedule-phone.css declares no transitions, no animations and no reduced-motion block — the phone schedule inherits desktop timings wholesale. Any new motion needs a phone pass or it will land on touch devices untuned.
- command-palette.css has no animation at all — the ⌘K palette hard-cuts in, which will look broken beside a redesigned system that animates every other overlay.
- The notification centre panel has no empty state; delayiq.css and timecard.css have no reduced-motion blocks; redesign.css and topbar-redesign.css define transitions with no reduced-motion coverage. These are pre-existing holes a redesign will make more visible.
- app-shell-hubspot.css is imported LAST in main.tsx specifically so it wins the cascade (comment at main.tsx:61). Reordering imports or renaming that file will change which shell rules apply.
- The house curve is duplicated as six differently-named CSS variables plus 220 literal cubic-bezier() strings. A redesign that introduces one token must rewrite all of them or the app will animate on two subtly different curves.
- sx-rise deliberately uses animation-fill-mode: backwards (settings-redesign.css:1064 comment) so the hidden start state releases after the stagger and does not clobber hover transforms; sb-nav-in deliberately animates the `translate` property rather than `transform` for the same reason (sidebar-redesign.css:132). Both are load-bearing choices that look like mistakes.
- test/setup.ts stubs matchMedia to matches:false, so every prefers-reduced-motion branch in App.tsx, useHudMotion.ts and the components is completely untested — a regression there will not be caught.
- CSS pitfalls recorded in memory that apply to this area: a `*/` inside a CSS comment closes it early and silently drops the next rule (tokens then resolve empty), and an author `display` rule beats [hidden] so a fixed inset:0 overlay can silently dim the page and eat every click. Both are relevant to overlay/state work.
- Two @keyframes live inline in TSX (cc-text-shimmer in text-shimmer.tsx:48, dcx-fade-in in display-cards.tsx:161) and will not be found by a CSS-only sweep of the animation layer.

### Motion + surface primitives library (Wx*)

**Route:** shared across every welcome view  
**Entry:** `App.tsx:4079-4620`

The reusable interaction vocabulary. A dashboard redesign that wants to feel like this page reuses these, not just the colors.

**Information displayed** (14)

- [ ] WxCounter (App.tsx:4079): renders `<b>{display}</b>`. Count-up over `duration = 1300ms` with `eased = 1 - (1-progress)^3` (easeOutCubic), started by an IntersectionObserver at `threshold: 0.35` which then disconnects. Reduced motion or no rAF → snaps to the final value. Safety net: a 1600ms setTimeout fires the run if the observer never does (so a stat never sticks at 0). No IntersectionObserver at all → runs immediately.
- [ ] WxMagnetic (App.tsx:4149): a `<button>` that follows the cursor. onMouseMove sets `transform: translate(dx*strength, dy*strength)` where dx/dy are the cursor's offset from the element centre and `strength = 0.34` by default; onMouseLeave clears the transform (so it springs back on the element's own CSS transition — `transform 0.28s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)` from .wx-btn). Takes className / onClick / ariaLabel / disabled.
- [ ] WxBloomField (App.tsx:4190-4265): the 'Bloom Field' mesh gradient (21st.dev 'Pipo'). Three radial-gradient blobs over paper plus an SVG feTurbulence grain data-URI. Blobs: apricot rgb(230,176,147) at 68.1%/46.03% r41.1; sky rgb(163,206,255) at 25.17%/75.99% r44.6; paper rgb(250,249,239) at 53.11%/12.71% r66.65. Each gradient has 5 stops at 0 / 25% / 50% / 75% / 100% of its radius with alphas 1 / 0.844 / 0.5 / 0.156 / 0. Animation: an rAF clock, `paint(t * 0.86)`, drift `blob.x + (sin(spin*0.55 + p) - sin(p)) * 14 * 0.72` (and 0.43 for y) — the `- sin(p)` term makes every modulation exactly 0 at ph=0 so motion starts from the resting frame; values are never rounded (a rounded centre steps visibly). Paused while off-screen via IntersectionObserver, with the clock kept continuous across pause/resume (`start += performance.now() - pausedAt`). Static single paint under prefers-reduced-motion. Renders `<div className='wx-bloom' aria-hidden>`.
- [ ] .wx-bloom CSS (welcome-redesign.css:1874-1882): `position:absolute; inset:-12%` (oversized so a drifting blob never shows a hard edge); `z-index:-1; background-color:#faf8ee; background-size:120px 120px, auto, auto, auto; background-blend-mode: overlay, normal, normal, normal` (the grain is the overlay layer)
- [ ] WxTilt (App.tsx:4266): sets `--rx`/`--ry` (deg) and `--gx`/`--gy` (%) from the pointer's normalized position inside the element: `--rx = restRx + (px-0.5)*2*max`, `--ry = restRy + (0.5-py)*2*max`; onMouseLeave resets to restRx/restRy (NOT the gradient vars). `max` defaults 10; the landing mocks pass `max={6}`. Consumers apply `transform: rotateX(var(--ry)) rotateY(var(--rx))`.
- [ ] WxTypewriter (App.tsx:4308): types `normal + em` one char at a time with a jittered delay `28 + random()*30 ms`, after a 350ms lead-in; sets `.wx-caret.done` when finished. Renders three layers: `.wx-type-ghost` (visibility:hidden — reserves the final layout), `.wx-type-real` (position:absolute; inset:0 — the animated overlay), and one `.wx-type-a11y` sr-only node carrying the full string (both visual layers are aria-hidden, fixing the double-read h1).
- [ ] WxRotatingHeadline (App.tsx:4356): 5-phase loop — (1) type the fixed prefix once at `26 + random()*26 ms`/char; (2) type the phrase at `42 + random()*34 ms`/char; (3) hold 1900ms; (4) delete at `24 + random()*18 ms`/char; (5) 260ms gap, advance index. Ghost reserves the LONGEST phrase's width so the centered headline never reflows. Hero phrases: 'move together.', 'stay in sync.', 'flow as one.', 'run on time.', 'stay on track.', 'move as one.'
- [ ] WxRotatingWord (App.tsx:4482): the same timings for a single trailing phrase, wrapped in `.wx-rotor` (`position:relative; display:inline-block; white-space:nowrap; text-align:left`) with `.wx-rotor-ghost` (visibility:hidden) and `.wx-rotor-real` (absolute inset:0). Takes a className for the phrase — the AI band passes `wx-grad-ai`.
- [ ] WxTypeIn (App.tsx:4528): streaming copy. Splits the text into per-character `<span style={{'--c': i}}>`; CSS `animation: wx-typein-char var(--wx-typein-fade, 130ms) linear both; animation-delay: calc(var(--c,0) * var(--wx-typein-step, 10ms))`. Because the fade (130ms) is 13× the step (10ms), ~a dozen characters are mid-fade at once — the leading edge reads as a soft gradient, not a caret. Runs ONCE: IntersectionObserver at `threshold: 0.25`, disconnects on first intersection. State rides on `data-run="1"`, deliberately NOT on className (a dynamic className near a [data-reveal] node fights the imperative `.in` class). Reduced motion / no IO → shows immediately.
- [ ] WxCompanyWave (App.tsx:4571): the wordmark marquee (see its own screen entry).
- [ ] TextShimmer (components/ui/text-shimmer.tsx): a gradient band swept across `background-clip:text`. Defaults `duration=2s`, `spread=2` (band width = text.length * spread px), baseColor '#9aa2ad', highlightColor '#2f6bff'; `background-size: 250% 100%`; `@keyframes cc-text-shimmer { 0%{background-position:100% center} 100%{background-position:0% center} }` linear infinite.
- [ ] BackgroundBeams (components/ui/background-beams.tsx): 50 hand-authored SVG paths with framer-motion `<motion.linearGradient>` swept along each — `initial {x1:'0%',x2:'0%',y1:'0%',y2:'0%'}`, animated, `duration: random()*10 + 10` seconds, `repeat: Infinity`. Comment says it is used ONLY by the removable #waitlist page and is safe to delete with it.
- [ ] Floating chip vocabulary (.wx-float / .wx-chip, welcome-redesign.css:1350-1422): `#fffdf9` pill, `1px solid var(--wx-line-soft)`, `box-shadow:0 16px 36px rgba(28,28,26,0.13)`, 13px/600 ink text, `padding:11px 16px`, radius 999px; parallax `translate3d(calc(var(--px)*var(--depth)*1px), calc(var(--py)*var(--depth)*1px),0)` with per-chip --depth 26/30/38/42; icon tint blue / #188038 green / --wx-g-purple / --wx-g-coral
- [ ] Dark 'product window' (.wx-window, :1197-1235): `border-radius:22px; background:var(--wx-win); border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); box-shadow:0 60px 130px rgba(28,28,26,0.3), 0 24px 50px rgba(28,28,26,0.18); padding:16px 18px 18px; transform-style:preserve-3d; transform: rotateX(var(--ry,0deg)) rotateY(var(--rx,0deg)); transition: transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)`, in a `.wx-stage { perspective:1600px; max-width:980px }`. Head has 11px macOS traffic lights #ff5f57 / #febc2e / #28c840.

### Cross-cutting notes for this area

- ONE TOKEN BLOCK: every colour, face and radius on the welcome page comes from the ~24 --wx-* custom properties declared on `.welcome-rx` (welcome-redesign.css:11-36). Derived systems (--cpx-*, --dcx-*, --gp-*, .cs-*) alias those values rather than introducing new ones. A dashboard match should re-declare the same token names, not new hexes.
- ONE TYPEFACE: Inter for everything. `--wx-serif` is a legacy token name — its value is the Inter sans stack (a comment says the display face was swapped off serif to match the dashboard). `font-style: italic` on `em` is used as the display accent; ui-monospace appears only in one marquee 'logo' treatment.
- ONE ACCENT: --wx-blue #1a73e8 carries every eyebrow, kicker, stat label, icon tint and link. The gradient trio (#4285f4 → #9b72cb 52-55% → #d96570) is reserved for exactly three things: the hero `em`, `.wx-grad-ai`, and the hairline above the hero badge. Status colour is Google-ish: #188038/#34a853 green, #f9ab00/#fdd663 amber, #d96570/#c04a57 red, with the pastel fills #e8f0fe / #e6f4ea / #fef7e0 / #fce8e6.
- TYPE SCALE ACTUALLY USED (all clamp()ed, all weight 500 on .wx-* headings and 600 on .cpx-*): hero 46→96px/-0.025em/1.02; feature-hero 38→78px/-0.03em/1.02; cpx-statement 2.5→5.5rem/-0.035em/1.05; h2 32→54px/-0.01em/1.08; whatis h2 34→54px/-0.03em; stat figure 46→72px; proof figure 42→60px/-0.02em; row h3 26→38px/1.12; footer tagline 22→30px; body 15.5-16px/1.6-1.65; hero sub 16→19px/1.65; helper 13-13.5px; eyebrow 12px/700/0.16em/uppercase; micro-label 11-11.5px/0.12-0.16em/uppercase. Weight 650 appears once (voice name), 700 for eyebrows/labels, 800-900 only in the brand mark and marquee marks.
- VERTICAL RHYTHM: `.wx-section { padding: clamp(76px,12vh,130px) 0 }` is the base beat; `.wx-band` is the loud beat at `clamp(80px,13vh,140px)`; `.cpx-section` is `clamp(64px,9vw,120px)`; the feature-row stack breathes at `gap: clamp(70px,10vh,110px)`; a section head is `margin:0 auto 54px` (46px in the voices section, 40px in the updates head). Consecutive sections routinely kill their own `paddingTop: 0` inline so gutters don't double.
- MEASURES: page 1140px (`.wx-main`), wide bands 1180px, feature hero 1040px, section head 640px, cpx measure 680px; copy measures in ch — 52ch lede, 44ch row body, 54ch whatis, 30ch stat helper, 26ch proof caption, 20ch band h2, 17-20ch hero title, 16ch footer tagline, 15ch mega intro.
- TWO CARD SURFACES, both from the same recipe: (a) LIGHT PAPER card — `background: var(--wx-card)` or `#fffdf9`, `1px solid var(--wx-line-soft)`, radius 18-20px, `box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgba(28,28,26,0.05)`, hover `translateY(-6px)` + `0 26px 60px rgba(28,28,26,0.12)`; (b) DARK GLASS card (`.wx-mock`) — it REMAPS the --wx-* tokens locally to dark values, then `backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(120%)`, `1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12)`, `box-shadow: 0 34px 80px rgba(30,8,24,0.45), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.08)`. There is also a light paper-glass twin (`rgba(255,255,255,0.72)` + `blur(14px) saturate(120%)` + `1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.7)`) used on the switch cards.
- 'PRODUCT WINDOW' TREATMENT: a mock never sits on the page ground. It floats inside a `#faf8ee` stage (`.wx-row-visual`, radius 26px, `1px solid rgba(28,28,26,0.08)`, `0 24px 60px rgba(28,28,26,0.08)`, `perspective:1200px`, `isolation:isolate`, `overflow:hidden`) over an animated WxBloomField mesh, and tilts on hover. The alternative stage is the aurora `.cs-panel` (three radial gradients + inset white hairline + 42px masked grid sheen).
- BUTTON VARIANTS (welcome-redesign.css:1066-1105 + 1836-1866): (1) `.wx-btn.wx-btn-ink` — pill `padding:14px 26px`, radius 999px, 15.5px/600, `background:var(--wx-ink); color:#fdfcf9; box-shadow: 0 8px 22px rgba(28,28,26,0.2)`; hover → `#000` and `0 14px 34px rgba(28,28,26,0.28)`. (2) `.wx-btn.wx-btn-line` — transparent with `border-color:var(--wx-line)`, ink text; hover `rgba(28,28,26,0.05)` + border `rgba(28,28,26,0.25)`. (3) `.wx-explore` — outline pill `padding:11px 20px`, `#fffdf9`, 14.5px/600; hover INVERTS to ink fill with `0 12px 28px rgba(28,28,26,0.18)` and slides its arrow `translateX(3px)`. (4) `.wx-hero-demo` — a quiet text link (`background:none; border:0; 14.5px/500; color:var(--wx-mut)`; hover ink + `gap` 8px→11px) that the HOME hero promotes to an outline pill (`padding:14px 24px; border:1px solid var(--wx-line); background: rgba(255,255,255,0.72)`; hover `#fff`, `0 10px 26px rgba(28,28,26,0.1)`, `translateY(-1px)`). (5) `.wx-mega-cta` — small outline pill `padding:10px 18px`, 14px/600, hover inverts to ink. (6) round icon buttons — 44px (updates arrows) / 40px (cpx rail) circles, `1px solid var(--wx-line)`, `#fffdf9`, hover var(--wx-bg-2) + darker border, `:active { transform: scale(0.94) }`. (7) `.cpx-subnav-cta` — the only SOLID BLUE button in the whole language.
- BUTTON TRANSITION SPEC: `transition: transform 0.28s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), box-shadow 0.25s ease, background 0.25s ease, border-color 0.25s ease`. Press feedback is `scale(0.94)` on icon buttons; the primary CTAs instead get a magnetic pointer-follow (WxMagnetic, strength 0.34) with the spring-back riding that 0.28s transform transition.
- HOVER GRAMMAR, in four moves: LIFT (`translateY(-5|-6px)` + a deeper shadow) for cards; INVERT (outline → ink fill) for pills; SLIDE (arrow `translateX(3px)` or `gap` grow 8→11px) for directional links; TILT (WxTilt `--rx/--ry`) for product mocks. Menu rows add a 2-3px `translateX` nudge.
- SCROLL-REVEAL MECHANICS, exactly: mark an element `data-reveal`; a root-level IntersectionObserver (`threshold: 0.16`, `rootMargin: '0px 0px -6% 0px'`) adds `.in` and UNOBSERVES it. CSS: `opacity:0; transform:translateY(30px); transition: opacity 1s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), transform 1s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); transition-delay: calc(var(--i,0)*100ms)`. The .cpx-* pages use the tighter 700/800ms + 60ms-stagger + threshold 0.14 variant. Second-order reveals hang off the parent's `.in` class (`.wx-feature-hero.in .wx-feature-hero-visual`, `.cpx-hero.in .cpx-hero-media`).
- REDUCED MOTION IS COMPLETE, and inconsistent by design: [data-reveal] is SHORTENED to 0.4s on the welcome home but fully disabled on .cpx-* pages; every infinite keyframe (wx-pulse, wx-blink, wx-levitate, wx-float-bob, wx-pin-pulse, wx-company-scroll, wx-word-wave, wx-cue, wld-draw, dcx-fade-in) is nulled; the marquee mask is also removed so the static strip is not clipped; WxCounter/WxTypeIn/WxTypewriter/WxRotating* all snap to their final text; the glyph portal reverts to reading flow.
- ONE-SHOT MOTION IS THE RULE: reveals unobserve, WxTypeIn disconnects on first intersection, WxCounter disconnects after running. Scrolling back up never replays anything. Only the ambient loops (aurora parallax, bloom mesh, marquee, dot pulse, levitation, footer wave) are continuous, and each pauses or nulls itself when off-screen or under reduced motion.
- PERF DISCIPLINE (learned the hard way, per the memory notes): aurora blur is 50px not 90px; `will-change: transform` only on the auroras, floats, marquee track and footer letters; bloom fields pause off-screen with a continuous clock; glyph-portal styles live in glyph-portal.css because its `:has()`/attribute selectors doubled every jsdom getComputedStyle; the root pointermove/scroll handlers are rAF-coalesced and set CSS custom properties instead of re-rendering React.
- A11Y CONVENTIONS worth copying: every type animation renders three layers (visibility:hidden ghost that reserves layout, aria-hidden absolute animated layer, one `.wx-type-a11y` sr-only node with the real string) so the heading is announced exactly once; decorative fields are `aria-hidden` + `inert`; the carousel is `role=region` + `aria-roledescription=carousel` with arrow keys and a `tabIndex` that follows the centre card; the glyph portal's letter picker is a real `role=radiogroup` with a coarse-pointer `<select>` fallback and 44px minimum hit heights; the .cpx-* page has one page-wide focus ring (`2px solid var(--cpx-blue)`, offset 3px).
- NO TAILWIND / NO SHADCN / NO `cn` / NO `@/` alias. Ported 21st.dev + shadcn components are rewritten as inline styles plus one inline `<style>` block (stagger-cards, display-cards, text-shimmer) or one scoped stylesheet (glyph-portal.css, interactive-hover-links.css), with the shadcn tokens mapped onto --wx-* (primary→--wx-ink, card→--wx-card, border→--wx-line, muted→--wx-faint).
- framer-motion appears in exactly two places in this area: `interactive-hover-links.tsx` (letter fan spring + useSpring/useTransform floating image) and `background-beams.tsx` (50 animated linearGradients, waitlist page only). Everything else is CSS keyframes or imperative rAF.

**Corrections** (5)

- crossCutting 'ONE TOKEN BLOCK ... derived systems alias those values rather than introducing new ones' is not accurate: the `--tone-blue/-green/-orange/-violet` set (#1a73e8 / #2f9760 / #cf8a1f / #7c3aed) is declared per page-id in compare-plans-, contact-sales- and reviews-redesign.css, and the form error colour #d1483a, the `.cs-badge` ramp (#2f9760 / #b07d18 / #c04a57), the glow's six conic stops and the `--cpx-paper*` ramp are all outside the --wx-* set.
- crossCutting 'SCROLL-REVEAL MECHANICS, exactly ... threshold: 0.16' understates the variance - 0.12 is the most common threshold across the area (see missingInformation).
- The stats-strip entry's 'the page's only dashboard-like data display' is wrong once the `.wx-tn-*` light mock and the `.cmp-table` comparison grid are counted.
- crossCutting 'BUTTON VARIANTS' and 'HOVER GRAMMAR, in four moves' are both short by two: the reskinned `.welcome-blue-button` ink pill and the frosted `.wx-hero-demo` hero pill, and the `translateY(-1px)` pill micro-lift.
- The hero entry quotes `.wx:not(.wx-overview) .wx-hero .wx-title` and the promoted `.wx-hero-demo` as if they were unconditional home rules; both are explicitly scoped OFF the overview page, which is an uninventoried screen using the other branch.

### Redesign risks in this area

- The hero copy is POSITIONED OFF GLYPH-PORTAL GEOMETRY: `.wx-portal-top` / `.wx-portal-bottom` are absolutely positioned against `--gp-word-top` / `--gp-word-bottom`, which the component writes from measured ink. Restyling the hero type (size, weight, family) silently moves the copy, and changing `.wx-hero`'s display breaks it (`.wx-hero.wx-hero-portal { display:block }` already exists to defeat the flex hero).
- The hero copy's rise delays (0.15s / 2.3s / 2.55s / 2.75s) are hand-tuned to the WxRotatingHeadline typing schedule (26+/42+/1900/24+/260ms). Change either and the sub/CTA either appear over an empty headline or arrive late.
- `--wx-serif` no longer means serif. Any new rule that reads it as a serif token will look wrong; renaming it touches every heading in the file.
- `.wx-mock` works by REMAPPING --wx-card / --wx-bg / --wx-bg-2 / --wx-ink / --wx-faint / --wx-line / --wx-line-soft to dark values. Introducing a new token for card surfaces (or hard-coding a hex) anywhere inside a mock will break the dark-glass inversion for every board, timeline, map and list at once.
- `.welcome-rx` is applied to ~30 welcome views via `isReskinView` (App.tsx:3283) plus a `style={{display:'contents'}}` wrapper for the mega menu (App.tsx:3757) and a `.cpx-subnav-portal` root. A token edit is site-wide across all of them, not home-only.
- One-shot reveals mean a redesign cannot verify motion by scrolling back up; and in a headless/jsdom preview the observers do not fire, leaving `[data-reveal]` at `opacity:0` (this is a documented, recurring blank-page symptom — memory: 'HUD reveal animations need forcing in preview').
- A DYNAMIC className on or near a `[data-reveal]` element wipes the imperative `.in` class → the element stays invisible. WxTypeIn already works around this by keying state on `data-run` instead. Any new conditional class in this area must respect the same rule (memory: 'data-reveal needs static className').
- `.welcome-rx` sets `overflow-x: clip` specifically so the glyph portal's `position:sticky` pin works; several sections escape the measure with `width:100vw; margin-inline: calc(50% - 50vw)`. Changing the root overflow or adding a transform/filter to an ancestor kills either the sticky pin or the full-bleed sections.
- z-index is a fixed ladder: portal field/art internals, `.wx-bg` 0, `.wx-cursor` 1, `.wx-main`/`.wx-footer` 2, `.wx-companies` 3, `.welcome-nav` 50, `.cpx-subnav` 60 (which deliberately COVERS the site header and is opaque for that reason). Inserting a new layer must slot into this ladder.
- `box-shadow`/`backdrop-filter` are load-bearing and expensive: the page is paint-bound and was already tuned once (aurora blur 90px→50px, static will-change removed). Adding another blurred layer or a 4th aurora is the likeliest way to regress frame rate.
- `clamp()` is everywhere with no fallbacks; `color-mix(in srgb, …)` is used by display-cards and `@property --wx-demo-a` / `animation-timeline: view()` are used behind `@supports`. A dashboard match should keep the `@supports` guard rather than assume scroll-driven animation support.
- Copyright/licence notices must survive: glyph-portal.tsx carries 'Glyph Portal © 2026 Christian Katzmann. MIT — keep this notice with copies', and glyph-portal.css repeats it; stagger-cards/display-cards/text-shimmer/background-beams/interactive-hover-links all carry port provenance comments.
- The stats are FLOORED (124 / 6 / 92) because the pre-login dataset is empty. Reusing WxCounter on real dashboard data means removing the floors — and then the 1600ms fallback plus the reduced-motion snap are the only things keeping a figure from rendering as 0.
- `.wx-band .wx-band-cards` is optically centred with `transform: translateX(calc(var(--dcx-dx) * -1))`, which depends on DisplayCards' internal `--dcx-dx`. Changing the fan offsets silently de-centres the stack.
- BackgroundBeams is documented as belonging only to the removable #waitlist page; the hero demo modal, the cobe globe CTA band and the cursor-confetti field were all already deleted for perf/lag (memory notes) — do not resurrect them as part of a 'match the landing page' effort.
- `.welcome-rx` is light-only. Welcome dark mode was deleted on 2026-08-04 (toggle, welcomeTheme and all `wx-dark` rules across 5 files). There is no dark palette to inherit for a dashboard that needs one — only the `--wx-win-*` 'product window' set, which is a surface treatment, not a full theme.

### B.3 Cross-cutting gaps (8)

Things that span areas and so fell between them.

- EVERY ONE OF THE 17 AREAS SELF-DECLARES INCOMPLETE. Summed from the JSONs' own completenessCheck blocks: 100 missingScreens entries, 347 missingInformation entries, 161 missingActions entries. Verdict strings range from 'incomplete-but-close' (sales-hub) to 'INCOMPLETE — ... misses 2 screens, ~24 information items and ~8 actions, and 5 of its claims are factually wrong about what the code renders' (schedule-week-month). Treating the 17 files as a complete baseline is not safe; the missing* lists have to be folded in first.
- THE GUIDED TOUR OVERLAY renders ON other areas' pages but is inventoried only as app-shell's BuildFlowTutorial (App.tsx:21222) — schedule-landing.json, schedule-list-kanban-matrix.json and map-timecard.json all list 'the guided-tour overlay that renders on this page' in their own missingScreens. Its per-page step copy (client/src/schedule/tour.ts) belongs to no area.

These are actions that only exist on hover/focus, so a redesign built from the inventory would drop them silently.

Only the Schedule category has a documented phone layer (client/src/schedule-phone.css). 266 @media blocks across 30 distinct breakpoints (480/520/560/620/639/640/680/720/721/760/768/780/820/860/900/920/940/960/980/1024/1040/1080/1100/1180/1200/1240/1280/1320/1420/1500px) are largely uninventoried.

### B.4 Redesign blockers (10)

Evidenced obstacles to a Tailwind/shadcn foundation in this repo.

- NO TAILWIND / SHADCN FOUNDATION EXISTS, AND THE REPO HAS AN ESTABLISHED ANTI-PATTERN AGAINST IT. client/package.json dependencies are react/react-dom/framer-motion/lucide-react/recharts/@dnd-kit/@tanstack — no tailwindcss, no postcss, no autoprefixer, no class-variance-authority, no clsx/tailwind-merge. `find . -maxdepth 3 -name components.json -o -name 'tailwind.config*'` (excluding node_modules) returns nothing. client/tsconfig.json declares no `baseUrl`/`paths`, so there is no `@/` alias any shadcn snippet needs. The project's documented convention (client/src/components/ui/text-shimmer.tsx header comment, and all 9 files in that folder) is the opposite: port shadcn snippets by DELETING their utility classes and rewriting them as inline style objects plus one imported stylesheet. Adopting shadcn means reversing the house pattern for every ported component.
- 60,798 LINES OF HAND-WRITTEN CSS IN 57 STYLESHEETS WITH AN ORDER-DEPENDENT CASCADE. client/src/main.tsx imports all 57 sheets in a hand-tuned sequence ending in `import './app-shell-hubspot.css'; // loads last so it wins` — the comment is the design. styles.css alone is 16,793 lines and sets global base rules (`*` at styles.css:28, `body` :32, `button, input, select, textarea` :38-41, `button` :45, `button:disabled` :49); redesign.css adds `html` :32, `*` :48 and `*::-webkit-scrollbar` :52. Tailwind Preflight resets exactly these elements, so it will either be overridden by the legacy sheet or overwrite it, depending on where it lands in that import list. There are also 49 `!important` declarations already in play (hs-home.css, field-updates-redesign.css and dashboard-redesign.css lead with 5 each).
- NO SINGLE TOKEN LAYER TO MAP ONTO TAILWIND THEME VARS — at least 20 independent CSS custom-property namespaces coexist: --wx- (2,908 uses), --cc- (521), --hsx- (343), --cpx- (200), --hsh- (113), --hs- (108), --sc- (76), --bfz- (72), --tc- (64), --gp- (34), --sim- (28), --hsc- (26), --mat- (23), --tone- (22), --eq- (19), --pr- (18), --mfo- (17), --sb- (14), --fud- (14), --af- (14). Nothing declares a shared palette, so `@theme` / :root token migration has ~20 partly-overlapping sources of truth rather than one.
- STYLE IS SPLIT BETWEEN CSS AND 249 INLINE STYLE OBJECTS (203 of them in App.tsx alone; `grep -rc 'style={{' --include='*.tsx'`). Inline styles beat every utility class, so Tailwind classes added to those elements are inert until each object is unwound by hand. All 9 ported components in client/src/components/ui/ are built this way by design.
- THE SCROLL-REVEAL ENGINE MAKES DYNAMIC className FATAL. client/src/useHudMotion.ts:33-53 queries `[data-reveal], [data-reveal-stagger]` and imperatively adds a `.in` class from an IntersectionObserver; the CSS default is opacity 0 (e.g. apply-redesign.css:36 `.careers-apply-page [data-reveal] { ... }` with `.in` at :45; same pattern in about-redesign.css:37/:46 and customers-redesign.css:35). App.tsx has 270 `data-reveal` attributes. Any React re-render that recomputes className — i.e. the standard shadcn `cn(...)`/clsx pattern — wipes the imperatively added `.in` and leaves the block permanently invisible with no error. This has already happened in this repo (memory note `data-reveal-static-classname`).
- COLOCATED COMPONENT CSS IS BANNED BY A JSDOM SELECTOR BUG, WHICH IS PRECISELY WHERE TAILWIND/SHADCN PUT IT. client/src/components/ui/glyph-portal.tsx's inline `<style>` had to be extracted to client/src/glyph-portal.css because jsdom's nwsapi mis-parsed `:where(#id)` and every test then read `visibility:hidden` on `<html>` (23 index-page failures), and because the block's `:has()`/attribute selectors made getComputedStyle ~2x slower and tripped 20s timeouts across the suite. The test suite runs in jsdom (client/vite.config.ts:119 `environment: "jsdom"`, setupFiles ./src/test/setup.ts) over ~3,964 lines of tests. `:where()` is the backbone of Tailwind Preflight and shadcn base layers; any of it that reaches a component's own <style> tag re-triggers this.
- THE DASHBOARD DRAG/RESIZE ENGINE HARDCODES PIXEL GEOMETRY IN TWO PLACES AT ONCE, AND USERS HAVE PERSISTED LAYOUTS AGAINST IT. client/src/dashGrid.ts:16-18 `DASH_COLS = 6`, `DASH_ROW_UNIT = 40`, `DASH_GAP = 16`, with `snapDelta` (:244) and `itemRect` (:250) computing drop targets from those numbers; client/src/hs-home.css:2046 independently declares `grid-auto-rows: 40px`. Layouts (x/y/w/h in those row units) are saved per user at `bf:dash:layout:<id>` (App.tsx:25740) and on the account as the `dash:layout` setting (App.tsx:23218). Changing dashboard spacing desynchronizes drag math from rendering and invalidates every saved board unless both constants and a migration are handled together.
- MOTION AND LAYOUT ARE ENTANGLED WITH THE MARKUP AT SCALE: 145 distinct @keyframes across the 57 sheets, plus a scroll-timeline animation behind `@supports (animation-timeline: view())`, framer-motion in 5 files, and @dnd-kit drag layers with their own ghost/lift/land CSS (DashDragGhost App.tsx:23479, DashDragLayer :23508, DealDragLayer :34574). None of this survives a wholesale class swap.
- EVERY APP PAGE IS SCOPED BY A BODY-LEVEL `-rx` CLASS AND ALL 11 SCOPES CARRY REAL WEIGHT: .welcome-rx (1,883 rules), .sched-rx (592), .dash-rx (583), .settings-rx (239), .proj-rx (219), .field-rx (202), .equip-rx (151), .mat-rx (137), .delayIQ-rx (123), .crew-rx (111), .sidebar-rx (43). Two scopes are declared in more than one sheet (.dash-rx in dashboard-redesign.css + hs-home.css + settings-redesign.css; .crew-rx in crews-redesign.css + field-updates-redesign.css), and .reviews-rx is applied in App.tsx but defined in no stylesheet — so the scope-to-sheet mapping is not 1:1 and cannot be migrated sheet by sheet.
- ALL OF IT LIVES IN ONE 39,194-LINE FILE. client/src/App.tsx holds 126 top-level components including every page and every dialog; the only components outside it are 9 ported UI files, TimeCard.tsx, DelayEarlyWarning.tsx, CommandPalette.tsx and the schedule/ tree. Incremental or parallel redesign work all lands in the same file, which this repo has already lost work to (memory note `hud-blank-preview-concurrent-edit-churn`: a black screen with an empty #root and no console errors caused by concurrent App.tsx edits).

PAGE-UNION COVERAGE — all 23 values in the Page union (App.tsx:361-382, the exact same 23) are claimed: welcome -> welcome-reference (+ states-and-motion); dashboard -> dashboard; bookmarks -> bookmarks-index-shared (+ app-shell); schedule -> schedule-landing; gantt -> gantt; week, month -> schedule-week-month; list, kanban, matrix -> schedule-list-kanban-matrix; projects -> projects; crews, equipment, materials -> crews-equipment-materials; contacts, companies, deals -> sales-hub; field, delayIQs, reports -> field-delayiq-reports; map, timecard -> map-timecard; settings -> settings. No signed-in page is orphaned. The gaps are all one level down: the WelcomeView union (App.tsx:385-439) has 55 values behind the single "welcome" page, and only 2 of them are inventoried.

WHAT CHECKED OUT CLEAN (so the parent does not re-run it):

- Dialogs/portals: I enumerated every `role="dialog"` / `role="alertdialog"` / `aria-modal` / `createPortal` in client/src (65 hits) and mapped each to its owning component by line range. All are claimed except `.cpx-demo` (App.tsx:9828). - components/ui/*.tsx: all 9 (background-beams, display-cards, expand-map, gantt, glyph-portal, interactive-hover-links, quantum-cloud-loader, stagger-cards, text-shimmer) are claimed by at least 2 areas. Caveat: background-beams' only host page (#waitlist) is itself uninventoried.

- Test coupling is NOT a major blocker: only 8 class-based `querySelector` calls exist across App.test.tsx and tests/ (.business-context-banner, .business-context-verify, .cc-spark, .cc-spark-line, .dash-block h2, .dash-board .cc-link/.cc-rec-btn/.cc-btn, .hs-home-promo); the rest of the ~3,964 test lines query by role and text, which a restyle survives.

FUNCTION COUNT — the brief said ~264 top-level functions; the actual figure is 126 in App.tsx and ~90 elsewhere (~216 total, `grep -rnE 'function [A-Z]' --include='*.tsx'`). Of App.tsx's 126, 57 are Welcome*/Wx*/marketing helpers and 69 serve the signed-in app; I checked all 69 against the inventories and every one is claimed.
